Arkadaşlar öncelikle merhabalar Steam üzerinden oyun saatim 3.2 saat gözüksede ben bu oyunu Steam' e düşmeden önce çok oynuyordum ve şuan hâlâ da oynamaya devam etmekteyim. Arkadaşlar Wildstar' daşuan gerçekten çok az Türk oyuncu bulunmaktadır, genel oyuncu sayısı da düşük bir seviyededir. Bunun yükü kesinlikle Wildstar üzerine bırakılmamalıdır. Çünkü ilk başladığımız zamanları hatırladığımda gerçekten bir çok şeyin ne kadar zor olduğunu hatırlıyorum... Alışılmadık hareket çeşitleri, dungeon ve boss sistemleri gerçekten oyun çok zordu... Raid yapmanız için gereken anahtarı tamamlamanız o kadar zordu ki insanların çoğu dungeon yapamayınca ya oyunu bırakmıştı ya da raid anahtarı ile uğraşırken bırakmıştı. Size wildstar harika bir oyun diyemem bu gerçekten yalan olur ama Wildstar' ın hakkettiği yerde bu değil. Benim kendi düşüncelerim olan artı ve eksileri sizler için sıralamak isterim.
Artıları:
- Ev dekorasyon sistemi harika ve kolay değil komşu olaylarıda çok güzel oyun da sadece zaman öldürmek için amaçsızca yapılacak güzel bir uğraş bence ve gayet güzel arsa tasarımları var.
-Görev aldın görevi bitirdin göreve geri koş derdi neredeyse yok çok akıcı bir şekilde oynuyorsunuz hele ki birde bir arkadaşın varsa yanınızda tadından yenmiyor.
-Raidler ve dungeonlar kolay değil lakin işini bilen bir ekip gayet hızlı bir şekilde bitirim bir sonraki dungeona geçebilir.
-Salvage etme yani kullanmadığınız bir eşyayı parçalama crafting item' ı sağlama işi çok hoş.
-Crafting sistemi çok güzel ve çok zor, bana göre oldukçada önemli birşey.
-Combat inanılmaz zevkli, ve konu mükemmel.
-Oyun içi item storedan eşya almak çok zor değil ki bence mountlar haricinde çok almaya değer birşey de yok.
-Gathering yani toplama sistemi çok hoş kimi zaman sizi sadece maden olan maplere atması çok hoş oluyor ama tabi süresi var.
-Oyunun premiumu dediğimiz signature olayını oyun içi CREED sistemiyle elimizdeki platinum ile alabiliyoruz yada gerçek parayla alıp oyun içi paraya satabiliyoruz.
-Oyun içi item tasarımları mekan tasarımları herşey mükemmel ve renkli.
Eksileri
-Oyuna gelen contentların içi dolu değil.
-GW2 gibi yeni crafting itemleri gelmiyor.
-Oyun içi Game Store' da güzel itemler yok.
-Sanki oyunla, oyun geliştiriciler çok ilgilenmiyormuş gibi bir izlenim var.
-Tek başınıza end game content ta yapabilecek çok az şey var.
-Oyuncu sayısı diğer mmorpglere ne yazık ki çok daha az.
-50 levela kadar pvp veya bg bulmanız neredeyse imkansız dungeon bile çok güç ancak chat'e yazarak adam toplarsanız o ayrı.
Arkadaşlar sonuç olarak bütün Türk arkadaşlarımı bu oyunda görmek isterim.  Oyunda her ırk ve faction beraber oynayabiliyor lakin ben Dominion'ım Draken Warrior server Jabbit oyuncu adım Mad Perv hepinizi yeni kurduğum guildde ve oyunda görmek ve tanımak isterim. İyi oyunlar.

Along with beautiful graphics and creative gameplay, Wildstar offers an amazing fictitious world in which players can explore, read, and learn. The little touches -- such as the voice-overs congratulating players when they gain a level -- are fun and amusing, and funny touches are present throughout the game. New players might take a while to get used to the camera and movement, but the sheer number of fun things to do will keep them coming back. In particular, the paths (professions) in the game allow players to pick the kind of gameplay they prefer. There's quite a bit of fighting action in the game, and the paths (Explorer, Soldier, Settler, Scientist) let players try other things that might suit them better. Plus, players can try different characters and different race-class-path combinations.

First stage review, 27.dec.14.
I've had a basic familiarisation with WM:T now. Eight hours is enough to do the tutorial, a couple of missions, and a couple of skirmishes. Initial impressions:
Pluses:
-Great IP, faithfully rendered.
-Simple, but deep
-Excellent range of units already in-game
-Graphics generally pretty good
-Game never feels like it's 'cheating' as it does in games such as XCOM: Enemy Unknown, where you can miss a 100% shot
Minuses:
-Blurry graphics
-Awful dialogue
-Hard on GPU's
-Terrible dialogue and voice acting
-Camera panning is clunky
-Dialogue and voice acting in single player campaign is utterly horrible and can't be skipped
-No in-combat save system
-Dialogue and voice acting are criminally bad, can't be skipped, and will make you want to kill yourself
-Additional units as paid-for DLC (although I'd let that slide if they'd fix the voice acting and dialogue)
-Doesn't look like you can cripple jacks by damaging components (ie a lucky shot blowing out a Jack cortex)
-Lt. Allison Jakes is possible the most annoying character ever... and I've been annoyed by the annoying orange
-Multiplayer/skirmish should have a range of points values, not everyone is looking for a 'big' game
Needs:
-Map/module/scenario/campaign editor
-Better scripting and voice acting
-Camera movement refinement
-Serious optimisation of graphics
-Better tutorial, covering things like combined ranged attacks and unit facings
-Better AI as opposed to simply 'more enemies'
-Custom warcasters who gain skills as they level up would be a work of genius
-Unit customisation/cosmetics (paint schemes, weapon shapes/sizes, slogans etc) even if pay2paint
-Multi-multiplayer (3, 4, 5+ players at a time with a turn time limit)
Overall, as a turn-based tactical (TBT) gamer, I'll give this game a 7/10, 8/10 if you're familiar with the IP and the tabletop version. It's a good game, it's just a little clunky. I have every confidence it'll get better.
I'm looking forward to the next patch.

I highly recommend WildStar and hopefully the community continues to grow. A well-made and polished MMO such as this should not be met with such a tragic fate.

A TL;DR for this game:
If you liked D2 but wished it was slightly faster paced, or you were disappointed with D3 because of the way loot works in that game, give this a shot. The only thing you might dislike is the pixel graphics, but I recommend you give it a try anyway. This is the most fun I've had in an ARPG in a long long time.
The skill trees are dense, so even if there are 4 classes, they can all spec in 4 different ways, and skill resets are basically free (not sure if this will change later). Lots of customization options here.
The gameplay isn't super grindy, and loot is satisfyingly great. Lots of zones as well so you can farm a whole bunch of areas in one go.
You can also re-roll stats and upgrade/maximize stats on your drops, so you're not grinding hours and hours for the same drop to get perfect rolls. Enchanter is really a godsend.
And of course, there are items that will tailor to your gameplay and spec (mostly based around what element and skill type you want to focus on), which gives you a reason to grind mobs end-game.
Overall, this is a really fantastic game. Even though it's EA, it definitely feels polished and ready to launch.

TL:DR available at the end!
At first sight it seems to be a good game...
+ Huge variety of ships - Great!
+ You can aim EVERY gun in your ship (manual AA guns, etc...) - Cool!
+ Good damage system. A ship taking a full salvo on magazine + engine + fuel tanks should not stay up for long, unlike in World of Warships - Mehh... depends on tastes
+ SUBMARINES!!!! Take that World of Warships!! - Y no subs in WoWs???
+ No aiming assistance, unlike in World of Warships - We aren't idiots, we can aim out turrets...
+ Nice maps - open sea maps are awesome and add another level of strategy to the game that does not exist in WoWs
+ Limited amount of ammunition - Nuff said
+ Low system requirements - You don't need a GTX 980 to run this game
... but soon after trying the game I found it's flaws, and they can't be ignored.
- Low system requirements - Crappy graphics, perhaps a stone age game engine?
- No physics whatsoever - Impossible to hit with a torpedo because ships can turn and stop almost instantly
- Copy of WG games in a lot of ways - The aiming circle of each turret is the same as the aiming circle of Arty's on WoT (although this is awesome the rest of the stuff makes people become enraged at this game for copying WG...)
This game takes World of Warships, World of Tanks and Navyfield, and then adds the stuff that's missing to WoWs, like submarines and better control over the Aircraft Carrier's loadouts (using a system incredibly similar to the WoT interface for choosing cunsumables, shells loaded, etc...), and it looks like Navyfield in so many ways...
BUT, it all ends after you see that the ship physics are garbage, ships accelerate and turn as fast as my car and because of that you can only hit the enemy with torps if one of the following occurs:
> Enemy is dumb
> You fire the torpedoes at 100 meters distance from the target
> You throw the torpedoes with your bare hands at the deck of the enemy ship
I played Navyfield for a long time, and I could handle the graphics of this game easily because most mechanics are enjoyable and well made, and being a copy of WG's games is not always bad, I would copy almost everything from this game to WoWs because it would make WoWs a GOD, or as it should be in the first place, but the physics kill the game, it makes the game feel more arcadeish than most arcade-like games.
TL:DR: Try the game! It is a game with awesome mechanics (except physics), and if you've played WoWs you'll be thinking "Why isn't this on WoWs yet???", but don't expect much from a game that's being killed by WoWs players and the game's physics. This game is basically a Navyfield merge with WoWs and WoT, and if you've played any of these you'll feel comfortable with the gameplay, so don't be afraid to give it a try. I hate the physics, but will recommend the game anyways because it has a huge potential.

Along with Shogun II, Medieval II is tied for being the best Total War game Creative Assembly has ever cranked out. The AI can be a bit weird at times, does the whole dancing unit thing occasionally, but it seems to do better at pressing an advantage or running away than the AI in more recent Total War games.(Warhammer really comes to mind)
Once you get tired of the base game, there are numerous mods for this game that are either completed or in development. Third Age: Total War, The Elder Scrolls: Total War, and Hyrule: Total War will all have you sinking hundreds of hours into this game if you let them. Or you can enhance the base game with the Stainless Steel mod and really give yourself a challege.
The hours I have on Steam for this game don't do it justice, honestly. I've racked up nearly 4x the amount if I include the copy I bought from Gamestop years ago. Seriously, this game rocks.

I'd heard about this game when I got into shogun 2 and I really wanted to like it but after playing shogun 2 it just isn't tolerable.
The camera is painfully clunky and hard to control. It's not intuitive in the slightest and I found myself constantly having to pause just to readjust the camera so I could see what was going on.
The units don't follow your commands very well, especially in seige battles, they won't form up they wander off, they go down ladders despite being set to stand guard. It's like trying to keep track of a small child in a zoo and it's just as frustrating.
In the deployment phase there are areas your men should be able to stand where they simply won't do it. no explanation they just refuse to be placed where you want them. It's especially irritating when one guy of an enemy troop gets past your front line and ALL of your archers in a unit stop shooting just to fight that one guy. Speaking of archers that hand red line from Shogun 2 that tells you when you are in range? yeah that's gone you have no way of knowing just how far archers can fire and I see them constantly shooting into walls and at things they can't hit wasting tons of their ammo and doing nothing.
The enemy AI is dumb as a rock, they ignore gates and funnel themselves into choke points making it really easy to win battles even when outnumbered.
Overall the game feels dated and clunky especially when compared to the newer titles. I really wanted to like this game but at this point I'm 90% sure that this game's reputation comes from a nostalgic fan base and not from any real quality of the game. I'm sure it was good for it's time but considering the improvements in later games it just doesn't hold up well over time.

Stellaris is the most enjoyable game I have played to date, and it continues to get better thanks to repeated love from Paradox in the form of extensive (but more importantly) FREE patches, which are sometimes paired with extremely worthwhile DLC expansions too. The DLC expansions won't set you back much, and are must haves in my opinion. The mod support is really where Stellaris shines for me though. The vanilla game and the DLCs are just the foundation, but the structure and the character of your game can and should be dictated by which mods you choose to install. There are so many, so you can really get creative with your giant space sandbox. If you love strategy and a very reasonable learning curve, Stellaris is for you.
EDIT: I am adding a bit to this because I am seeing a trend on the reviews from people who seem to be unhappy with an "unfinished" game. If you're sitting there playing vanilla still and by yourself.. then that's your problem. Get the DLCs, get some friends to play, and then you will finally get to experience the full package this game offers. Look how many hours I have put into this game with no sign of stopping anytime soon. Those aren't solo hours on vanilla people. I've played since release pretty consistently, and it only stays fresh when you make it stay fresh. Get the DLCs, play with people, and most importantly.. GET SOME MODS INSTALLED.

So, I have to say a few things about the game itself before going on to speaking about the PC-port, so just hang in there and try to get through the whole review (or just read the interesting bits, your choice).
NieR Automata is a fantastic game and there's no denying that.
Not does it only feature a great story, beautiful soundtrack and gorgeous graphics, it's only got various kinds of different gameplay from different gaming genres mashed into one game, and it's actually done really well, creating a truly unique experience.
Even though the main action within the game may get a tad bit repetitious, it's still really fun and does stay fresh for the most part by introducing new sorts of enemies as you progress within the game. Yeah, there IS a rather annoying mini game that disturbs the combat sometimes, but I do not exactly see it being a problem myself. It's only a very small section of a otherwise great game full of all kinds of different content for you to explore, and who knows, maybe you'll actually like that section as well. At least I did every now and then when it wasn't in my face all the time.
I also really enjoyed NieR's interesting take on the usual skill tree mechanics with their rather unique Plug-In Chips, which basically work like items that affect your gameplay and you can buy or sell them. What I really personally found interesting was how these chips also included things related to your HUD and UI, which makes it possible to make it even more challenging for you if you feel like the game is too easy for you even on hard difficulty.
Speaking of difficulties, this game handles different difficulty levels really well. Not are they already very well balanced for what kind of challenge you might want to experience with the game, you can adjust it a bit more to your liking by editing the chips I mentioned before.
I could keep on going about how good this game is in several other ways as well, but I think you've already gotten the grasp on how I feel about this game and how it actually does have lots of good points, so I'll just leave the rest for you to experience yourself.
Honestly, this game is probably one of the best games I've gotten to play in a long time (or maybe even in my whole life), and it's definitely worth every cent that it costs.
Especially since you can easily get multiple dozens of hours of fun by playing through all the 26 endings (trust me, it couldn't be more worth it as together they complete the story and the first ending is just the beginning for the actual game).
But as you can see on the other reviews, the PC-port for this game isn't really the greatest port out there amongst all the games on Steam or PC in general.
It has lots of issues with it, and a few of them are not small issues at all.
Luckily, most of these issues might not even bother you (like they didn't me) and for the most part it runs very well with a stable FPS (There are some frame drops when there's lots of stuff happening at the same time), but you will definitely notice these four main issues that people seem to have with this game's PC-port.
1. You can not run this game 1080p in fullscreen mode.
Yes, this game actually suffers of this problem and it's probably the biggest issue I can see with this port. But don't worry, you can still get around it by either using an app called Windowed Borderless Gaming which makes it possible to technically run the game fullscreen by having the game on windowed mode without borders...
Or you can always download a mod called FAR (Fix Automata Resolution), which fixes this issue along with many other smaller ones.
So technically, this issue isn't too much of a problem in the end if you're willing to deal with it quickly yourself (though that doesn't make it any more acceptable for the PC-port to have an issue like this).
2. The cutscenes are very laggy and stuttery for some reason on the PC-port compared to the console versions.
This can break your immersion and damage your gaming experience quite a lot, but if you're like me, you might not actually care too much about that after playing it for some time.
3. The controls for PC are not exactly good.
The controls for gamers who prefer using a keyboard and mouse are not simple or good.
They'll most likely leave you confused for some time and make the action parts of the game also feel way less satisfying...
But I wouldn't really recommend playing this without a controller anyways, it's pretty obvious that the control schemes were designed with controllers in mind, so you definitely should play it with a controller if possible.
4. There's lots of graphics hiccups everywhere around the game that might annoy you quite a lot (at least it did annoy me). Good examples of these errors would be things turning invisible when they should be visible and some textures rendering badly and looking awful (and I know that it looks like that 'cause of a some kind of issue since in the same location at a different time and it looks great).
In the end, I feel like this game is overall a great purchase on every platform, but I would recommend to pick up the console version instead if you have a console.
Though even with all of it's smaller and bigger issues, it can be a great experience on the PC as well (especially since some of the flaws are fixable by mods already, and the rest will most likely be later on as well, or so I hope at least), so do try picking it up on at least some platform if you like games like this as I'm sure you'll love this game.

I enjoy Afterlife Empire. It's a cute management-style game with the unique idea of managing your own haunted house. Seeing Vivian in the opening credits really made me grin, so keep in mind this review is biased.
That in mind, the game is only five dollars and I've already gotten a few hours of entertainment out of it. The basic idea is simple and fun, similar to rollercoaster tycoon as others have pointed out, but with a supernatural twist.
There are a number of glitches. The tutorial often freezes and you have to esc out of it to continue playing. When you load saved levels walls will sometimes be missing. Nothing bad enough to make me ragequit, but I can see someone who'd worked longer on their house getting pretty upset over it.

While I do find this game to be worth the five bucks, and recommend it, it does have it's fair share of problems.  I didn't expect TOO much for only five dollars, and I'm ultimately satisfied with what I got.
THE GOOD:
* The gameplay is fun enough.  You can design the rooms to have certain themes and have a variety of traps to scare people (to death) with.  You also get several different "scare powers" that are better used in different conditions.
* It gets pretty challenging as you progress.  With more people showing up, there are also those who will deplete your resources and disable/steal your traps.  You have to watch out for them.  It makes you keep your focus while playing.
* I like the visual style of the game.  They took their time designing the different characters in the game along with various animations.
* The game has some decent humor.  You can click the characters to have them say something (The exorcist will want to "cleanse this place in the name of fettuccine").  There's other funny little things scattered throughout the game.
THE BAD:
* The tutorial was broken (and from looking at other reviews, it wasn't just me).  I had trouble moving the ghost to the two teenagers, and had to actually click several squares before the end for the ghost to move there.  After that, I couldn't select my scare power, so I had to skip the tutorial altogether and figure out the game on my own.  Fortunately it was easy enough and only took me a few minutes of exploring the UI.  Plus, the more difficult characters are introduced slowly, with messages popping up saying what they do, so the tutorial isn't exactly necessary.
* I couldn't delete/move traps.  I don't know if this gets talked about in the tutorial since I couldn't do it, but it was annoying.  Especially since I wanted to rebuild a few rooms, so the traps ended getting stuck in a wall, but were still considered a part of that room.  Fortunately, the traps still functioned.
THE MEH:
* The scrolling seems reversed.  I scroll up to zoom out, and scroll down to zoom in.
* You choose resolution settings before the game starts, Windowed, Fullscreen 1080, and Fullscreen 720.  They could have easily put that in the in-game settings, with more resolution options.
* When you right click on a trap (in the build menu, not in the house), you get a message saying "[trap name] not much to say about them".  This is just sloppy.  They could have written something like how the trap operates, or even not have that message come up at all.  At least it doesn't take away from the game.
* The music is decent, however it's a single constant loop.  At least it's a fitting theme that doesn't get annoying.  Not very good, but not bad either.

This game sort of reminds me of xbill if you've ever played it on Linux based systems.  Where in xbill you are protecting your network from little Bill clones, in this game you are protecting your haunted house from Exorcists and Home Renovation Enthusiasts.  The main difference is that you are also building the house as you play (unlike the prebuilt network in xBill), and the traps in the house generate energy.  So, it's split between two modes.  Build mode (action is paused) where you add rooms, traps, decor (necessary to keep the bulldozers from coming) and ghost mode, where you frantically try to scare away threats.
Exorcists kill you, given enough time, Renovators kill your traps (preventing the house from generating the energy you need to survive).  As the game progresses, the house gets bigger and bigger and you get a second attack (smaller area but uses less energy).
I expect once you get used to the controls, you will probably put a lot of time into this game.  Not so much as sitting for a whole day playing it, but pulling it up when you have an hour to kill here and there. Now, I have only had a few hours to play it, but that's enough to recommend it to people looking for a game in this category. (I will say there are both more options for traps, and new threats as the game progressed, so I haven't seen everything it has to offer yet.)

Kickstarter backer.  I played single player multiple times and multiplayer twice.  The game plays up the randomness too much.  While it translates a lot of the rules from tabletop, theres a different feeling when you are the one rolling the dice rather than a randomizer.  Having an entire turn of misses scroll across the screen is demoralizing.
When I'm playing single player, my guys were just as survivable as the enemies.  I've done a fair number of turn-based games and when you're fighting against a force that respawns, your guys are usually just better.  I played mission 8 (the one where you kill a bunch of inactive juggernauts) and stopped.  Unless you get the perfect rolls and do things in the right order, one of the 3 (Rourke usually) gets smeared into paste by stray shots after holding him back the entire game to avoid it.
Animation isn't smooth.  It's incredibly choppy and the game plus along at 8FPS.  It's terrible seeing as I'm playing far more power hungry games at better graphics levels with no issue.
Finally, the mechanics within the game seem random.  So I move Jakes up and cast Positive Charge on my Lancer before attacking (doable on the tabletop) to get the bonus.  Instead, everything stops.  At other times, I can cast and attack.  Or the Lancer changes from a 2x2 grid size to a 1x1 grid size.
When making charges, you are warned about opportunity attacks.  So I'll pick a charge lane, go at it to find out that they didn't notify me of this opportunity attack.
All-in-all, this isn't a complete game.  If you want this style of game in fantasy, look at the Fire Emblem games from Nintendo.  If you want it in Sci-Fi, look at XCom.  But for the love of all that is holy, don't get this in it's current state.  I've wasted too much time trying to play this and I'm always frustrated by the end.

When I found the first trailers and teasers for this game, I was very eager to play it. Having been playing Warmachine for years, it looked like a good adapatation using the rich and detailed setting. As an advance graphically on previous games I've played, I did purchase some hardware upgrades, which had been overdue anyway.
I'm afraid I did not back the kickstarter, as it really didn't look like I was needed. Nonetheless, I kept an eye on the development logs and awaited it coming into open beta. I purchased it when the price dropped from the deluxe £60 to the standard £20, as I really didn't need or want the extra shinies offered.
What I got in beta was a game that was very much in beta. The multi-player game worked with a few bugs, but it did seem to roll along.  There was a certain scarcity of players, as several backers I'd talked to offline said they'd be waiting for it to be finished, while others were scared off by reviewers with higher standards than myself.
I played the multiplayer games on and off for months, reporting the occasional bugs and making new friends. When the first (of four?) single-player campaigns came out I was pleased, although the decision to then declare the game released was a little surprising. There were still a few bugs, which cropped up as I played through the campaign. Given the lack of an in-level save function (and a new baby at home) my progress was slow, but I encountered 3 crash-causing bugs in 20 missions, the first two of which were down to performance issues on my PC, and the last was swiftly fixed by a patch. For a game still in development, I am happy with this ratio.
After many hours of play, and reading the forums for this game, I think that White Moon Dreams has built this as a labour of love. It was a little premature onto beta, and again onto release, but it's now running smoothly, and WMD continue to work on it, add features, and interact with their players.
If you'd asked me when I puchased this game, I'd have said "wait a few months". A few months later, and I would reccomend this as an interesting and characterful game, with a lot of playability. For the standard price, I have already got my money's worth (in hours of entertainment) from this game and look forwards to the extra (and free) campaigns to come. The multiplayer side of things is also getting new content, bigger maps, etc, for those who focus on that.
I look forwards to seeing where this game goes next!

Stellaris presents itself quite well at the beginning, with good visuals and pretty music.  The early game is interesting, with well defined goals, and a group of intrepid scientists exploring the galaxy and running into nifty anomalies and event chains.
And then the wheels come off.  Those fun little events suddenly stop quite abruptly and the player is thrust into a far more traditional 4x style space game.  There is little in the way of direction at that point for the beginner, and the events are simply not terribly interesting.
Stellaris tries to spice things up with the occasional random event (The Worm in Waiting was particularly memorable), and various unexpected crises arising at the end, but for the most part it becomes a tedious slog.
If you are already a fan of the 4x genre, there are more complex variants.  If you are not, there is not much here to entice you.  Where narrative is provided, it is engaging, but it doesn't justify the high buy in price.

Well to start you're dead. And that's ok. Now it's time to haunt your house before you fade away!
To get to the nitty and gritty the core of this game is to expand your haunted house while dealing with a variety of threats looking to exorcise your ghostly self. The core resource is energy which is replenished by scaring people. But be careful as building your house costs energy too! Also scaring people can raise awareness which results in your house getting demo'd. You have to strike a careful balance between gathering energy to stay in the game and expand while managing your awareness against a variety of people wandering around your ghostly home. Reporters, cops, exorcists, and more will have to be carefully dealt with so they don't interrupt your bread and butter walking energy nuggets.
The artwork is cute and the gameplay engaging. I don't generally care overly much when it comes to these sorts of games however I find it to be quite enjoyable. It's also about $4.50 which is crazy cheap. For the bad however I do find the interface and controls to be counter-intuitive at times. Zooming in and out feels inverted and you can't for example open the options menu via escape but you have to use escape to close it. It's doesn't really hinder the gameplay any but it does take some getting used to.
Ultimately I'd say if this kind of game is up your alley and you have $5 go ahead and give it a go. I highly doubt you'll regret it.

Afterlife Empire's an unusual beast. A very simple little game, it simultaneously calls to mind games like Roller Coaster Tycoon and Theme Hospital - only in this case, you're one little ghost who's trying to continue to exist. The game drops you right in with a fairly straightforward tutorial, explaining various bits of the game relatively quickly and in succession. The goal is to build up your Haunt by scaring the natives and improving your ghost house.
But you have to be careful - because your scare energy is also your currency used to scare people directly, you can't spook all your ghost shekels in one place - better to save those skeleton dollars in the ghost bank, an-- stupid jokes aside, it's an unusual game in that you have to manage the scare energy you get carefully, resisting the temptation to splurge on one big item for your home without a little bit of scare energy in the bank just in case!
The game's humor is very tongue-in-cheek and both colorful and interesting to watch.
Pros:
* Simple, accessible fun
* Humorous as all hell with clever ideas
* Surprisingly bright and well-animated
* Character designs are cute and well-done
* Excellent asking price
* Mod-friendly
* More updates coming!
Cons:
* Music is pretty mediocre
* Screams can get somewhat repetitive
* Game feels somewhat like an ascended mobile game
* Audio can glitch if too much happens at once
* Progression is a little awkward
* Some parts of the game need to be tutorialized better

This isn't the deepest or most complex game in the world, and if you're the kind of person to focus on the aesthetics of a creepy haunted house then this game doesn't really provide that very well. But those are really the only flaws, and the game isn't really an ultra-deep-sim in the first place so they're forgivable.
The game is inexpensive, and also very fun - the basic gameplay is simple but addictive. The balancing act of making enough "scare energy" (i.e. Health + Cash) without exceeding a certain level of "awareness" is easily understood yet compelling. The game slowly ramps up the complexity as you play, so you never feel overloaded.
The graphics have a somewhat cute art style which helps the light-hearted "Addams Family" atmosphere, which is complemented nicely by the (admittedly a touch repetitive) soundtrack.
So overall, the game is fun, and provides good entertainment value. It isn't the deepest game ever but many players of a huge variety of age groups will be able to enjoy it. The Devs plan on adding achievements, and I hope they add trading cards too.
PROS
+ Fun and addictive basic gameplay
+ Cutesy atmosphere that works well with the morbid theme
+ Good value for money and most of the profits go to fighting cancer
CONS
- Not exactly deep
OVERALL
An enjoyable game that will be good fun for a huge variety of players. If you like games like Dungeon Keeper or Theme Hospital, you'll like this.

Secret of Mana meets Diablo.
Gameplay wise, it's very much a Diablo style ARPG, just with a retro feel.
- You can play 1 of 4 classes, and each class has 4 skill trees.
- You also have a mastery tree you can place mastery points in that can further customize your focus.
- Max level is 100, but there isn't a cap on mastery level.  So yes, you can get considerably stronger past level 100.
- You get kill streak bonuses for killing lots of stuff really fast, and at certain thresholds they do AOE explosion effects.
- You can buy potions to respec your skill points and mastery points, so you don't have to worry about screwing up early on when starting out.
Like other Diablo style ARPGs, there are multiple difficulty levels.
- You get bonuses to magic find, exp, and crystal (money) drops on higher difficulties.
- The best drops only drop on Legendary or higher difficulty.
- Like most ARPGs, you get resist penalties in higher difficulties.
- Difficulty continues to scale up in anomalies (end game dungeon with infinite levels).  The highest difficulty is Mythical, and beyond that it will continue scaling up by a numerical amount, for example Mythical XX, but you won't get a resist penalty for higher numbers of Mythical.  But mobs will get more powerful!
Gear options:
- You can reroll gear in this game, as well as augment specific mods on gear to raise their power.
- Once you augment a mod on a piece of gear it puts a * beside that mod, which means it can't be rerolled.
- Like most ARPGs, you have set items that give set bonuses, and some of the set bonuses are very powerful.
- In this game Legendary sets are generally "best in slot" for any build.  And you can still reroll and augment mods on these.
- There are a number of different legendary sets and true legendary items that are "build defining".  Meaning you make builds around these sets/items.
- A recent patch added gems to the game.  As well as a merchant that can reroll gem slots on gear.
- Gems can give a variety of bonuses depending on their type and which type of item slots they're placed in.
- Gems = extra mods on gear, basically.
Overall, this is a pretty casual ARPG, and not the kinda game that's another one of those 500-1000+ hour grind fests, you could easily get multiple classes to 100 + geared out in under 100 hours.  The time dump is if you want to get high anomalies like 1k+ and grind 700+ mastery level.
For the price, the game is definitely worth it, and this game will run on a potato laptop.

As a new player - and being a level 12 after 15 hours (and lvl22 after 36hr) - i have a few things to say about the game.
first of all the controls - for me they took a bit of getting used to - though that may be because i haven't played an MMO in a long while - and i'm still messing up my dodging but that will get better with practice. . . and you do have to dodge alot. There is alot of movement required in this game especially when you have multiple mobs on you also you need to be constantly turning to get out of their weapons range. It makes the combat system intresting and needing focus.
Combat can be customised by changing your attacks and leveling up only the ones you want to use and those points can easily be redistributed if you decie on another line up - this allows you to have multiple options however i haven't been able to work out if you can change the line up without having to open up the actual box.
quests are mostly the standard go get this, find that, interact with something, kill that speices - but it doesn't give you numbers instead theres a percentage which is an intresting feature, the quest narrative is intresting  to read and will tell you more backstory and more information about the world and the people. There are a few differant quests to mix things up - such as having to use an item or being turned into a creature to find and dig something up.
The lore is awesome. completly awesome.  As you go along you'll find books and if you choose scientist will also look for datacubes which give you even more lore. Getting the datacubes is also a great way to see more of the landscape and it's fun trying to figure out where the cube is and how to get at it. though it can be frustrating to come up against a wall and not be able to find a way around it, it takes a bit of patients and perceverance at times.
The housing is really cool. Your given  several plots where you can place plots like your house, a crafting place and a garden. and then you can put your decor whereever you feel like it - you get decor as quest rewards and drops or you can buy them and place then wherever you like, hoever you like - at the minute i have a floating mushroom :P
i've only just got the crafting system so only really played with cooking - which is useful up to a point you can only eat outside of combat but the food does give buffs which last 30 minutes - and architects which also looks intresting and usefull - and the resource points look like carrots and trees on the map which is an amusing little feature :D
Leveling - as mentioned it's taken me 15 hours to get to level 12 - for me this is fine i'm more intrested in the lore, the quests and just running around exploring. I haven't been grinding mobs just doing the quests which seems to be working for me. - The xp event has obviously boosted me up which is both good and slightly annoying as i almost missed a quest line until i wondered why i'd gone from level 15 quest to 18 but it does make it slightly easier being a bit higher than the mobs.
So all that was great but i do have a couple of downsides.
As have been mentioned on other reviews there is  a lack of player i've only see a few other people as i've been running around but the chat box is constantly moving with chatter which is great. The other downside is that at times i have trouble seeing where i'm going there have been 2 quests where you had to go into caves and i was in the dark and couldn't see a thing i don't know if i was missing something but it made doing that quest without dying slightly difficult.
On the whole i'm really loving this game and i hope that people will give it a shot.

I am redoing this review from about 2 years ago. Okay.
TL;DR Steel Ocean is a good game.
Steel Ocean is a World of Warships-y-kinda game. The graphics and sound aren't exactly anything to be too excited about, but gameplay-wise, this game is quite good. It's very close to World of Warships when it comes to the main gun battles, but when it comes to torpedoes and all, it's very different.
It also includes submarines, aswell, and the torpedo mechanics are very good. Instead of being able to shoot torpedoes at very close range, like  in World of Warships and basically destroying a battleship without it having any chance to escape, the torpedoes must go quite a 'long' distance to actually arm themselves, so destroyers cannot just sail up right next to other ships and fire their torpedoes & destroy you instantly.
The submarine mechanic is implimented well with how depth changes how the subs must play and all, and how depth charges, torpedoes, and other things can change how you must act.
My two only real big issues with the game is how fast Battleships can turn (making them avoid torpedoes easily, which can be very annoying as a sub captain,) and how your aircraft only really spot enemy ships about two feet away, far too late to really organize a drop on them. While AA does chew through aircraft insanely in my experience, I suppose it is realistic.
Note: You can control secondary & AA guns yourself. That's really, really nice.
Overall, beside bugs and the 2 things I listed above, I'd give Steel Ocean a solid 8/10.

When Early Access began for this game in July, I'd been waiting almost a year to play it. Its features were heavily limited, it was full of bugs, and it was poorly optimised- all things you'd expect from an Early Access game.
In the following months, the developers have shown that they care about both the game and the community- almost everything has been fixed in weekly patches, features have been implemented at an impressive rate, and a huge amount of our suggestions have been taken on board. For a debut game from a new studio, I'm mightily impressed.
Warmachine: Tactics, as with the tabletop Warmachine, is about clever army construction, positioning, patience, ruthlessness, brutality and keeping your cool. A warcaster defines how his army functions, so the same list can play very differently with the change of a single unit, and there are currently around a dozen units and four warcasters for each faction, so there's a huge amount of customisation possible.
If you've ever lost an evening to a turn-based tactical game, then I can recommend this.
As for downsides? The UI could use a little work and Mac performance is a little wonky, but there's nothing gamebreaking. The learning curve is steep if you've never played Warmachine, but you'll be rewarded if you persevere.

I like the graphics and the animations and it does an adequate job of representing the table top game on the computer, although some of the rule changes from TT to computer feel awkward and confusing.  The real reason I cannot recommend this game is the AI.  It is absolutely atrocious in the skirmish mode, and pretty weak in the campaign.  It is a waste of time to play against the computer in skirmish mode as it constantly makes ridiculous moves that make the game a pushover.
Those of you who have played tabletop will understand what I mean with a simple example: in a recent skirmish game, the computer ran Severius (a squishy backline caster) up to be adjacent with my warcaster, who happened to be the Butcher (actually Butcher3 from the minis game minus his argii/arguses).  Didn't attack or anything else.  Just ran him up base-to-base with what may be the deadliest warcaster in the game.  Another example (and even those who haven't played tabletop will understand this): Cygnar Gunmages.  They have the word "GUN" in the name of the unit.  So what do they seem to do most of the time in the game?  Charge into melee.
I've played to mission four or five in the campaign and maybe it shines there, but I doubt it.  I also have my doubts about DLC.  It didn't affect my recommendation, but I feel like this game is very expandable.  However, they're going to nickle-and-dime it, most likely.

Let me say first that this game is a good game. Very good combat mechanism, gameplay and story. I loved the game. That is why I decided to buy it after I beat the Denuvo free (cracked/pirated whatever you like to call it) version. However, I would not recommend this game, not untill you have tried it out first and can decide for yourself.
Here is why:
-(1) Graphical bug. My laptop is 1080p, so I did not have too much resolution problem, but there are objects in the game that have poor texture quality. The most noticable one is the cargo container next to your transporter in the resistant camp.
-(2) Crashes. Regardless which version you play, pirated or legit, you WILL get crashes. I had crashes several times after I bought the game. It can be quite frustrating considering the game does not have auto-save. Some people reported the game is unplayable. It is also possible. Again, you need to decide if you can tolerate the crashes,
-(3) Very POOR PC control integration. Keyboard binding is the only one you can change in this game. There is no way to change or assign keys for you mouse. Good thing I have a xBox controller.
-(4) NOT fully voiced. Other than the main story line and the side quests, the game is NOT voiced. It doesn't have voice when talking to NPC. It doesn't have voice when buying from merchant. It doesn't even have voice when talking to your follower (9S or 2B). WTF... There isn't that many character you can interact with in the game, there is really no reason for not including a voice for a few more sentences (Words in some cases).
For a game priced at 60USD, all these issues are unacceptable. It does felt like the game was rushed out of the production line despite it was delayed. I hope the above list can be removed in the future updates, but untill then, I would not recommend anyone to buy it unless you have tried and loved it.

I'll start with the bad first even though I do enjoy this game, in the hopes that if there's ever a sequel these can be adressed.
1. Ui, the ui in this game is very archiac and hard to understand at first. In particular manipulating objects. So far I haven't figured out how to rotate or move objects if I even can, all I seem to be able to do is clone and delete objects. It took me a while to figure out how rooms were formed as floors were only an option with no walls like the sims and the first three floor options don't actually make rooms. This also factored into the traps a bit as it seemed like the effective range of traps was only revealed to me after I placed them on the map not previewed before, but I could just be being unattentive.
2. The tutorial for me seems to be bugged as I can't control the ghost at all during it forcing me to skip it which if that hadn't happened I think my first pointwouldn't be as big a deal as it was to me.
3.The isometric view means you can't see everything in your rooms effectively, and also you can't place objects right up against the wall closes to you as the spot seems to be obscured, both visually and mechanically you can't interact with it once a wall covers it.
I don't mind the isometric view I just wish I could place items right up to the closest wall so I could have my rooms be symmetrical in some spots.
Finally the resolution options in this game are limited and as I use a normal tv not a Computer monitor with my desktop I couldn't fix the game to work in fullscreen mode making me have to play it in a stretched window mode. It's only a minor complaint but something I felt like noting.
Now with those points out of the way here are the things I liked about the game and why I think it's ultimately still worth playing if it interests you.
I like the aesthetic of the game, especially the ghost himself he's got a cute charm to me the way he giggles and displays different facial expressions throughout gameplay.
There's a surprising variety in the way different humans interact with the house and they're introduced gradually which means you don't get too overwhelemed by them.
The game progresses in sort of mini levels where you have to achieve a size and trap number milestone, to unlock the next set of objects to use in customising as well as more humans with more complex effects on the game.
Your ghost also gains a new scaring ability with each stage progressed into and you can use these at the cost of your resource points to instantly scare any humans in an area of effect around you.
The more scares you pull off in frequent succession the more awareness of your hauntings go's up. With higher awareness more people come to the house both normal people you can scare for points and others like Excorcists Journalists, skeptic bloggers and more that can drain your resources or raise your awareness even more.
So you have to manage having enough awareness to make your haunted house popular, but not too notorious or else the Police investigate the house draining your resources rapidly and leading to an almost guarenteed game over.
The game is surprisingly challenging, if you aren't paying attention you may spend too many resources and find yourself with not enough to keep going as your health and currency are both pulling from the same source. And if you get too carried away with scaring people you might cause one to die of fright sending your awareness meter so high your home will be swarming with cops ending your game very swiftly.
I wasn't expecting this game to be one that required my full attention but it was scanning the map constantly to find certain npcs  Iwanted to scare away before they got to my house or to spook a coward for bonus points kept me constantly looking around the map not just idling on my house and overall I felt it was pretty engaging so far. Gonna play more into it and see how much it draws me in.
Sorry for the rambling but I really wanted to get my full thoughts out on this game. It's rough around the edges, especially with Ui and Resolution options, but it's a great foundation and first attempt in my opinion. A sequel maybe that expanded on the tech side of things while addind more content would be fantastic in my eyes.
As for this one it's a pretty nice game, I enjoy it.

I have played about 3 hours on the beta for Afterlife Empire, and just over an hour on the steam release now. I really want to say that this is a solid game. While it does have it's flaws, it offers fun gameplay and hours of enjoyment at a very reasonable price.
Pros: A solid sim/strat game that offers good replayability. The audio is decent but not amazing. The graphics are the same. The graphics feel more like they were made for a tablet/mobile phone game than a straight out PC release. But the game runs very smoothly. The only bugs I encountered were during the tutorial. The gameplay is more casual than most of the Theme games, or Sim games, but that actually helps to work in it's favor imo. I could play for 20-30 minutes and feel I accomplished something, or I could play for an hour or more. This is a game that I will recommend to my friends who like sim/strat type games or who like mobile/casual games. For the price it is a serious buy.
Cons: The few bugs I did see were during the tutorial. I could not click on objectives, and had to escape out of the tutorial during the beta (so these bugs MAY be fixed now). This made it harder to get into the game at first. The graphics, for a PC game, could be better. For my taste I would enjoy more RPG elements, i.e. levelups, or stats... but that is my own personal taste.
Warning!: There is some controversy surrounding this game because of the #GamerGate situation. I say forget that crap and give the game a try yourself. For the $5 pricetag you get a lot more out of it then most games that are 15-20 bucks on release. I have enjoyed my time playing this game and I hope you will as well.

I was not even aware this MMO had existed before seeing it here in Steam. I looked into it some more and became intrigued that this is a standalone version with the option of running it as a server for friends  / everyone or as a single player. The age of the game becomes fairly obvious when you see the graphics. They are a bit reminiscent of the earlier Gothic games.  The online game has been around for quite sometime so this is not a total surprise and once you look beyond that you can appreciate the depth there is in terms of content and gameplay. There is a ton of things you can change from the graphics to character levelling. This is a good thing as it means you can tailor the game to be how you want it.
My advice to those new to the game is to play the adventure mode and then speak to the NPC in the middle of the starter town. He will give you missions that will train you on how to do things. It won't take you long before you realise how simple it can be to combine items in order to create new things. The survival elements work well and its pretty easy to find what you need when in the wild. The interface contains a lot of information and its as easy as clicking or dragging to  customise it to your taste.
The levelling system works by increasing your skills the more you use them. This is great because it means your character will develop in style that you play. I'm sure there is many, many things I am yet to discover but so far the game has been both stable and interesting. If you were a fan of the online version then this is a no brainer. If not then still consider this because if you play with friends you can become the gamesmaster and weave events in the game. There is a creative mode as well for those who would rather spend their time building.

First off, let's get one thing clear. This is NOT a game. What it is, is something from the depths of hell, spawned by Satan himself to punish Donald Trump for being a stupid and greedy redneck. Somehow Donald Trump managed to turn the tables on Satan and find a way to get even more rich by dumping this most unholy "thing" on unsuspecting Steam users. I'm not sure Satan minds too much though since now he gets to torture millions of innocent souls daily without lifting a finger. Damn you Donald Trump, damn you!
But you don't really care so let me just tell you what this is all about. It's really not a game but more of a fun little diversion while you wait for something better to do. All you literally do in this game is click a few buttons and then come back tomorrow and do the same. Over and over again.
The premise is very simple. You're given enough money to buy a single lemonade stand. You then click on the lemonade stand to earn some more money. Every time you click on a "industry" button it generates money. The lemonade stand doesn't generate too much at first but it's instant cash. So you click a few times until you can afford another lemonade stand and then another and you keep clicking to get more money. Eventually you have enough money to buy a manager who takes over the clicking and you then just sit and wait for the cash to roll in.
Once you have enough money you buy a car wash. Then a doughnut shop. You keep doing this until you have all the businesses, ending with the oil rig. Each business initially takes longer and longer to earn money but generate higher amounts of cash. Once you buy a set amount of each the times get shorter and shorter until everything is almost instant.
To get to that point though you'll need angels. Lots and lots of angels. And upgrades. As you get more and more money you attract angels which you can then claim by resetting the game and starting from scratch again or by paying the developer some real money to allow you to claim said angels without resetting. The game has a few micro transactions like this but you really don't need to spend any money to progress. You basically just pay to speed up your progression. Since the game is free I don't have a problem with this concept.
Is it fun? Initially yes. It's hard to explain but you'll find yourself coming back to claim your new angels, restart, get everything as far maxed out as you can and then come back tomorrow to do it again. there's no strategy or skill involved. It's just a clicker with a rather unique hook to keep you coming back.
Eventually you'll get quite bored of I suspect. Once you reach a certain point the progress really slows to a crawl and that is perhaps my one and only gripe with this game. It's entertaining at first but after you reach the crawling stage you'll wish there was some incentive for bothering to keep at it. Or some mechanic to make it worth while. It becomes quite apparent that the progress has been setup with the aim of generating micro transactions and unless you pay up you're not going to "beat" the game anytime soon or have fun doing so. AT which point you don't bother anymore.
That being said, for what it is, it is an entertaining time waster for those moments between downloads, waiting for a new game or wasting your lunch hour at work on. And it's free so trying it out won't hurt. Just don't expect a game in any real sense of the word. This is a click and wait gimmick that is looks like it would be quite at home on Facebook or an iPhone.

OK, so I downloaded Loadout when it was promoted on Steam. With the Dayz, Arma and Battlefield games I was playing I was looking forward to the "old's cool" style, fun arena shooter. And I was not disappointed. The game is visually pleasing and quite entertaining with all it's animations and crazy outfits (which you mostly admire in the outfitter instead of in the game). The combat is fluid and to me it really felt like I was once again playing something similar to Unreal Tournament, but with humor.
Soooo... Why do I not recommend the game then?!
There are a couple very big problems with this game.
1.After the first couple of hours of gameplay I was very impressed with the game. Ranking up was fast and rewarding, giving you options to mess around with your guns and test for the optimal gear for your play style. At the same time match making was working perfectly, you never felt like anyone really has any OP weapons and the matches were tense and exciting right to the end.
All that fun and excitement ends right about the time you hit level 10. After that, match making seems to be without any logic what so ever. 90% of games will be a one sided game, with one (losing) team just cycling through players who log out because of frustration. Which makes the game frustrating.
At that point, the leveling up also becomes just a grind for glutens. It loses it's fun mostly because the game doesn't reward players for their contribution to the game. It doesn't matter if you get 1 kill or 30, if you score with hammer 0 times or 5 times, it doesn't matter. You will still get 500 points for playing the whole match+50 for win and about 10-40 for your gameplay.
At that point you also pretty much understand that, even with the crazy amount of weapon customization, you only have about a handfull competitive weapons, while the others are just fun stuff either for new people or the ones that have everything unlocked and are just having fun.
And those three things combined make this game quite frustrating and boring. Oh and the fact that between every game there is almost always a 90s wait time, doesn't help the game.
2. P2W.... at first I was impressed. It looked like the only things you can buy with money are visual thingies like clothes and gestures. That made me want to support the project and throw some bucks their way and i was shocked at the prices. I thougth ok, 20 EUR should get you quite a lot, as i figured that 60 EUR would get you the whole game. But I was gravely mistaken.
I did some calculations, and if you would like to unlock everything in this game (apart from gluten and xp boost) you would have to pay just around 1.000 Euros. And that is if you buy in game cash only at the best price and the prices were rounded down.
Now, I don't know what the devs are thinking, but to price your game at 1.000 Euros is idiotic.
And later I also found out that you can buy xp and gluten boost. Which explains the problem I had before. they make first 10 levels fun and exciting and when you're "hooked" the leveling up becomes such a grinding bore, people would be almost forced to buy the boost.
3.   The game only has about 3 game modes, 3 characters and 3 maps. Which make the already teadious grind even more boring.
Yes, it is free to play. I understand that. And to anyone that wants to play, I recommend it. You will have a couple of hours of fun. But remember. There will come a time when you will stop having fun, but you will still want to play just for the leveling up. At that point you might also think of spending money to do so. DON'T... really, just don't. There are many  AAA titles with a lot more content, which you will get a hell of a lot cheaper than this "free" game.
ps.: Haven't tried playing with friend, but I imagine that option is the most fun.

I found Hellenica very addictive. I've gotten near the end of the storyline, but I keep exploring different areas to see the story unfold rather than progress down the main questline.
Some things I liked:
- Interesting steampunk reimagining of ancient Greece. Really cool character renditions (e.g. the Oracle of Delphi).
- Fun tactical combat that rewards positioning and strategy over brute force.
- Endearing characters with funny dialog. Banter between party members made me laugh out of loud multiple times.
- Branching storyline lets you follow the multiple character's intersecting paths.

A wonderfully realized tactics RPG in a unique setting with great retro pixel art. The characters are interesting and the story is well written. If you are interested in ancient Greek history you'll nod along with all of the characters and references. The story is lengthy with branching missions so you'll soon want to go back and play the other paths.
Do not approach the game with the expected depth of a FF Tactics experience with jobs and heavy stats or you'll be disappointed. Approach it more from a true strategy angle and you'll be heavily rewarded with well designed levels and fun encounters. What character should I attack that enemy with at what angle to cause huge damage? That question will have you replaying each battle to ensure maximum pixel carnage. Did I mention that your main character is also a bear? What's better than playing as a giant bear and knocking Luddites off trains, cliffs, and into other Luddies?!
If you like the retro style and are looking for a light, strategy heavy, tactics RPG with a good story in a neat setting you won't be disappointed!!

DISCLAIMER
I got my copy of the game free and early. I don't know the devs though I have met one of them and one of his friends is one of my friends and they knew that I liked games in this genre, so I was asked to play through the game for compatibility/bugs.
CONS:
- Scarce on animations and lots of re-used art in general.
- Too few character abilities spread across to much game; not enough incentive to play levels and progress once you've unlocked the main abilities you're interested in.
- Branching story felt unnecessary; would've preferred linear story rather than hearing about the same things over and over.
PROS:
- Fantastic character abilities. I feel like so many SRPGs are just about high DPS and very little to do with actual tactics or maneuvering. Each level has three bonus objectives to complete; for players that go for those they'll be forced more into situations that make them aware of the potential for the abilities. I had a lot of fun in particular with Nephele's little barrel that she can place which displaces anyone nearby. I was discovering new uses or aspects to abilities clear up until I beat the game. I think more than anything else I looked forward to meeting new allies so that I could see what their unique set of abilities would be.
- Great levels. I think many SRPG have boring levels; Vandal Hearts and FF Tactics are two games that got it right. I'd add this game to that list. You will end up replaying them, but they are well designed and fun.
- Good SRPG. I haven't played an SRPG that I liked in a very long time, so it's a big deal to me that I liked this one. Between Vandal Hearts and Final Fantasy Tactics, I prefer the former, so for me it wasn't a loss to not have items/equipment/more-leveling/more-meta. It's a stripped down experience but what's there is really good.
- Story. Others have said they didn't like the story or characters or that they just didn't care about it. I actually like the overall story and I liked the characters too. I think both would've been stronger if presented in a linear format, but for anyone who's afraid of the story/characters being bad, your-mileage-may-vary but that certainly wasn't my experience. I wish the game was longer/more-complete partly just because I wish the story could've been done better justice.
SUMMARY
Other turn-based tactics games have more content and better art; I still liked this game more than nearly all of them.
If you're an SRPG fan, this one's worth looking into.

I cannot in good conscience recommend this game to anyone who asks.
Not that this game doesn't have some good things in it, but overall in the tactics genre, it doesn't necessarily do anything better than the classics.
Let's just begin with all of the things I don't like about the game.
During the fights ALL of your controlled characters move first and attack then ALL of the AI enemies move and attack.  They do not individually take turns and therefore the overall map strategy and positioning are not necessarily in play most of the time.
Game becomes quite predictable and a grind. The above mechanic also makes it to where the AI either has to vastly outnumber your characters or throw gimmicks at you or both in order to give the player any challenge whatsoever.  You simply take a defensible position and hold off the horde.
The skills are different but for the most part they just help you deal with the onslaught of the numerous enemies on the map - such as being able to target several enemies in a line.  For the few hours that I played at least, the skills did not seem to combo well or not at all.
Even in the old classics the images of the people talking would at least change every once in a while.  A facial expression or a change in stance or even placing the characters neatly within the environment would've been nice.  Unfortunately the images stay completely static and because of that the personalities fall flat.
There's much too many words to read. I realize that it sounds like a stupid complaint but the story isn't very interesting.  I end up not caring about the main characters of Nephele and Diona and skipping through the dialogue altogether. How can I even care about the random people and allies you speak to during the story elemeints if their names are difficult to pronounce?
Is it all that bad though?  No!
There are diverging paths you can take and because of that you will meet different characters and allies.
The tactical maps are usually interesting and there are ledges to push your enemies off of or things to drop on their heads.  (Though again you'll usually never get to see the majority of the map since you are in a defensive position the entire match)
challenges on every tactical map to help gain extra experience and therefore gaining extra skills.
Overall the game falls flat in execution and the story elements are feels much too stiff.

This is not a finished product. If it's advertised as so, it's a lie. It's very much unpolished - you can, for example, zoom into the ground, revealing hidden units or objects (NOTE: This issue has been corrected in the recent patches). It has potential to be a great game, but there are a few things you should consider before buying. First of all, this game came from Kickstarter, where it received more than 1.5 million dollars to be produced. Anyone who plays it, though, wouldn't say that it feels like a "1.5 million game". There are much better games in the market produced with less money. I was a kickstarter backer and I feel kind of deceived, because it doesn't look like all the money we gave to the developers was well spent in producing the great game that was promised.
Voice acting is bad, the story is bad, gameplay is decent at the very best, and the main characters are very poorly animated. I don't know how they decided that "animate the wind blowing the character's clothes" was more important than "ANIMATE THE MAIN CHARACTERS FACES WHILE SPEAKING". Really, in all dialogues what you get is a blunt face staring at emptiness, while a voice-over is played - done by someone who clearly isn't a native English speaker. Hell, I'm not even english or american and I can tell the voice acting is bad and done by someone who's not completely fluent.
Bottomline: if you're a fan of tactical turn based games like me, wait for a Steam Sale and get it; however, you should also be open-minded and have a lot of patience to overcome Warmachine's current shortcomings. If you're not a die-hard fan of the genre, don't even bother.
It will also depend on how developers will fix/improve this game with patches over time. What I'm doing, and suggest anyone who bought it to do, is waiting 6 months or so until this game GETS FINISHED.

Such as oh I don't know the option to save in mission; either you complete a mission or you have to start the mission from the beginning. There is also no fog of war in this game, so when you are in a mission you can see all the enemy units (excluding any trigger created units).Looking at other reviews I see I am not the only one who is very disappointed in the choppy camera functions but this could easily be fixed. The controls for the camera are terrible and simply awful in comparison to other strategy games. Rather than a simple hold shift (or other key) and move the mouse to adjust the angle or rotate the camera, you have multiple sets of keys you to use in order to manipulate the camera to the desired position. But overall, I would still recommend the game. I just hope that the developers fix the various glitches and the camera controls.

I love the tabletop game and setting, and while the game does a decent job bringing the setting to the game, all of the "game" elements drag it down and make the game incredibly frustrating to play. I have had to force myself to try to play this game because I keep wanting to give it a chance.
The interface in this game is one of the worst I have ever seen, with a non-functional camera that is incredibly clunky and difficult to control. The camera is so bad and frustrating that it has caused me to rage quit the game several times. I can only take so much of the stupid camera clipping into terain/walls/etc. Also, whoever did the programming for movement indicators on tiles really messed up with how they show up in snow. In the 4th mission (escape from the train) I cannot even see the movement markers against the snow terrain because the colors are so oversaturated.
Also, unit movement is really a pain to manage, and I am constantly making unintential moves.
For whatever reason, the game also seems to redraw the scene everytime it moves across the map to show different sections. This results in huge fps drops and freezes every time a new unit moves. Major pain to watch. I have very good system specs, so I know it is not the issue, looks like just bad coding. Honestly have no idea why they decided to make this thing in Unreal...if it was simpler it would probably be a lot more playable.
Cutscenes so far are all still images and not animated...feels very cheap and unfinished.
Compared to other tactics type games, this one is pretty bad and definitely feels like it was done by amateurs, especially when compared to games like xcom. I want to love this game, but it really needs a lot of help and definitely is still in an alpha/beta stage.

TL;DR Review: Games ok in current form, needs work. Buy it if you're a die-hard Warmachine fan, but it's different from the tabletop.
Being fully released for a while now, Whitemoon Dreams has certainly made an impressive game for only having a little over a year for development and being an Indie Developer. That being said, the game still suffers from optimization issues and bugs. They are almost doing themselves a disservice by putting an FPS moniter in the corner of the screen. Playing through the single player campaign, my FPS changed with every mission, some hovering around 50, while others struggled to get above 15. The graphics setting do allow you to gain a few FPS by knocking down the quality, but sometimes that doesn't even help. Another big stumbling block is the bugs, which have gotten better. Sometimes these bugs are a simple graphical glitch, but other times, they either make the game crash or don't let a unit finish attacking, effectivly ending the game. In the campaign, the cut scenes are sometimes fully animated, but other times, it's just panning shots of still models. I actually prefer this to the way other games just plop the idle characters into place, idle animations and absense of lip-syncing ruining your sense of immersion. I understand that Whitemoon can only do so much, being an indie developer, and have limited manpower, but the cut scenes just feel inconsistant.
To anyone who plays the tabletop, this is a similar experiance, but there's a great differance. Some good, some bad. For one, it's a grid based system, as opposed to freely moving about the field to whatever distance is desired. This system makes melee ranges interesting. Stats are made more akin to a "out of 5" system, making some things hit harder than the tabletop, while others suffer. Another change is that Warjacks no longer have systems on thier damage grids, and it is instead more akin to a health bar now. Of all the changes from the table top, I really wish this one had stayed. In addition, certain units have gained abilites, like Assault Kommando Flamethrowers can now "Flush out" enemies hiding behind cover and push them back. On the subject of warrior models, there are no units in this game, all grunts are now solos with about 8 - 15 health. As a result, some damage has been amplified, like corrosion does 3 damage a turn and fire is even more potent. Warcasters, however, keep the same health they have on the table top.
Despite all this, I still adore this game. I love seeing the tabletop game come to life. I love seeing the animated cut scenes in the campaign. I love the progression that the main protagonist goes through. I love seeing units breathed new life with new abilities and mechanichs. I love the communication that the Developers have with the community, and how often they update the game.
All in all, it's not perfect, but I love it all the same.

I've played the MMO version "Wurm Online" for three years and it was a great game, one of a kind and it has come a very long way, especially these last two years. Wurm Unlimited is the private-server version of that great game, which allows you to set up your very own server or play on servers that other players like you have set up. A lot of the things are immediately custumizable, such as skill gain, action timers (time it takes you to craft, build, terraform etc.), farming timers and a whole bunch of other stuff through an ingame item called a wand, which you receive when you make yourself a GM.
Wurm Online's main complaint had always been the time it takes to do stuff. After the price hike many people were also unable to pay for the game's steep price. Wurm Unlimited solves both of these issues, as you can customize the game in any way you want to. Wurm Unlimited is also a one-time payment, which means you won't be paying anything besides the initial price of 25 euros (or an equivalent to that, depending on your country and currency).
The possibility of creating mods is also there, although I must admit I am disappointed in the lack of documentation regarding this. I have however understood that there is a certain community working on creating a framework for modding.
Overall, great game. Also impressed by the very smooth launch of it, I have to admit I was expecting many issues but I found none.
Also still impressed at the fact that I could spawn a thousand black dragons in one spot without lagging.
