First off, let's get one thing clear. This is NOT a game. What it is, is something from the depths of hell, spawned by Satan himself to punish Donald Trump for being a stupid and greedy redneck. Somehow Donald Trump managed to turn the tables on Satan and find a way to get even more rich by dumping this most unholy "thing" on unsuspecting Steam users. I'm not sure Satan minds too much though since now he gets to torture millions of innocent souls daily without lifting a finger. Damn you Donald Trump, damn you!
But you don't really care so let me just tell you what this is all about. It's really not a game but more of a fun little diversion while you wait for something better to do. All you literally do in this game is click a few buttons and then come back tomorrow and do the same. Over and over again.
The premise is very simple. You're given enough money to buy a single lemonade stand. You then click on the lemonade stand to earn some more money. Every time you click on a "industry" button it generates money. The lemonade stand doesn't generate too much at first but it's instant cash. So you click a few times until you can afford another lemonade stand and then another and you keep clicking to get more money. Eventually you have enough money to buy a manager who takes over the clicking and you then just sit and wait for the cash to roll in.
Once you have enough money you buy a car wash. Then a doughnut shop. You keep doing this until you have all the businesses, ending with the oil rig. Each business initially takes longer and longer to earn money but generate higher amounts of cash. Once you buy a set amount of each the times get shorter and shorter until everything is almost instant.
To get to that point though you'll need angels. Lots and lots of angels. And upgrades. As you get more and more money you attract angels which you can then claim by resetting the game and starting from scratch again or by paying the developer some real money to allow you to claim said angels without resetting. The game has a few micro transactions like this but you really don't need to spend any money to progress. You basically just pay to speed up your progression. Since the game is free I don't have a problem with this concept.
Is it fun? Initially yes. It's hard to explain but you'll find yourself coming back to claim your new angels, restart, get everything as far maxed out as you can and then come back tomorrow to do it again. there's no strategy or skill involved. It's just a clicker with a rather unique hook to keep you coming back.
Eventually you'll get quite bored of I suspect. Once you reach a certain point the progress really slows to a crawl and that is perhaps my one and only gripe with this game. It's entertaining at first but after you reach the crawling stage you'll wish there was some incentive for bothering to keep at it. Or some mechanic to make it worth while. It becomes quite apparent that the progress has been setup with the aim of generating micro transactions and unless you pay up you're not going to "beat" the game anytime soon or have fun doing so. AT which point you don't bother anymore.
That being said, for what it is, it is an entertaining time waster for those moments between downloads, waiting for a new game or wasting your lunch hour at work on. And it's free so trying it out won't hurt. Just don't expect a game in any real sense of the word. This is a click and wait gimmick that is looks like it would be quite at home on Facebook or an iPhone.

Got this game to kill some time and get my "ARPG fix" I need every once in a while and for me it did the job quite well. A lot of systems are very similar to other games in the genre; The skill tree reminds me of Grim Dawn, mastery points are a bit like the paragon system in Diablo 3 and enchanting is the same, but on crack.
I cannot say a lot about the story because in typical ARPG fashion I honestly did not care at all. However, the transition from act to act was nice since they look and feel quite different. Looking forward to the next - as of now missing - two acts.
Progressing your character feels rewarding and getting new skills is always cool. Unfortunately Chronicon makes the same mistake Diablo 3 did and offers way too strong bonuses on set items, which limit build diversity in the endgame.
Speaking of which: Anomalies, this game's version of infinite dungeons, are cool for a while, but become rather bland soon. On low levels of gear you are also much better off farming a specific boss or levelling area over and over again. Expecting a fleshed out endgame system is not realistic for such a small project though, and I got enough value out of this game. Especially if the developer, who is very active here on the forums and on other social media, expands the game in the future.
TL;DR A pretty fun ARPG for a while with heavy influences from other games in the genre. The dev seems like a cool dude and I'm looking forward to replaying Chronicon once it is fully released.

Chronicon is a pixel-graphics ARPG being developed by one dude. So far, it's got 3 (out of 5) acts, and a Greater-Rift-esque endgame feature called "Anomalies." There are your standard ARPG tiers of items, ranging from regular to "True Legendary," as well as set items.
There are currently four classes in the game:

Each class has four trees (representing sub-classes) and you can mix and match stuff from the different trees to create optimal builds. Like most ARPGs, some builds vastly outshine others, but, in my experience so far, you can play how you want and do decent damage.
There are also Mastery levels, which are like Paragon levels from D3, but a
of a lot more customizable. You start earning Mastery points from the get-go, but mastery levels take more XP to acquire than regular levels. The level cap is 100, but, AFAIK, mastery levels are uncapped.
The crafting system is really, really nice, IMO. As long as you have the materials and currency, you can create "perfect" items. There's a bit of RNG, but it's possible to get (almost) exactly what you want on each of your items.
The default controls are WASD to move, but there are also click-to-move and controller options. The controller works better with some classes than with others. Being somewhat of an ARPG purist, I immediately switched my control type to click-to-move. It's a bit wonky, but I'm sure it'll be smoothed out over time.

Dark Tower is another puzzle game in the guise of an RPG, taking after the free indie game Tower of the Sorcerer, the Steam game DungeonUp, or the DSiWare game Crystal Adventure. This one may well be the worst of those, however, because many of the key fun elements of the genre are missing.
The puzzle elements of the genre are fairly simplistic: Basically, fighting monsters is completely deterministic, and you can tell what the results of any fight will be before you get into it, in terms of how much damage you'll suffer, so you just need to figure out what order is the best for fighting things, what to put off fighting until you're stronger and can defeat it without taking damage, et cetera.
However, unlike all the other entries into this genre, you can't actually tell what an enemy's stats are until you fight it, and you can't attempt to fight an enemy that you wouldn't defeat, so if you run into an enemy you can't beat, the game doesn't tell you whether your attack is too low or your defense is too low, you just need to spend points and pray, and reset the game if you can't do that or if you did it wrong. The game also autosaves after every step, so there is no way to save before fighting an unknown monster and see if the results are acceptable. In addition, Dark Tower is pretty much entirely lacking in puzzles OTHER than determining the best order in which to kill everything, with essentially no level puzzles or secrets.
In conclusion: No, even if you like this genre it's not a good entry. Buy DungeonUp instead if the genre sounds interesting.

I have to wonder how much experience the gameplay and UI designers have with making games.  You have to manually select each unit before giving them orders instead of auto-selecting the next unit in the list.  There is also no easy way to move the camera so you can actually tell where you're moving.  While I enjoy seeing the action from almost any angle, can we include a consistent way to get an overhead view next time?  And the unit actions themselves can be confusing to navigate and are (again) inconsistent in how they are executed.  Sometimes you click a circle in the unit menu and other times you click on an enemy unit itself. There's a great game buried in here somewhere, but it's hidden behind the terrible controls and clunky camera.

The trailer doesn't show you any real gameplay, so a lot of people might be wondering what this game is.  Basically it is a tactical resource management RPG akin to "Tower of the Sorcerer", "DROD RPG", and "DungeonUp", the latter 2 of which can be found on Steam.
As a huge fan of this genre of game, I have over 250 hours on DROD RPG, have completed Tower of the Sorcercer in it's many iterations on mobile, as well as DungeonUp.  It's a great thinking-mans genre when executed well, unfortunately this game fails massively due to a few reasons I will try to explain for people not used tot hese typs of games.
The games I mentioned above have a few things that are critical for a game of this type to be executed properly.  For starters, the game does not reveal the stats of the monsters until you fight them, which in itself is bad because it makes it impossible to form a plan without face-tanking something first to see how bad it is.  It is compounded by the fact that the game autosaves every move you make without the ability to undo a move, something the others games of this type allow.  This means you have to make a decision blind that can ruin your run completely, basically forcing you to replay the game over and over to fill out the bestiary just to get information that should have been known from the start.
To make matters worse, the level designs are terrible.  After the first few floors, key management becomes pointless as many of the floors involve straight corridors with no routing options, creating hard walls that basically end your game unless you built your character almost flawlessly, again which is impossible without knowing the stats.  This pretty much removes all planning and routing decisions and defeats the entire purpose of the game.
The most outrageous aspect of this game is not the fact that it is a mobile game ported to the PC, but the fast that the PC version gives you a pop-up every 2-3 minutes asking you to LIKE the game on Facebook in exchange for in-game coins.  This is a despicable design and horrible business practice for a Steam game, trying to push the pay-to-win aspects of the mobile game to the PC version to compensate for the fact the game is designed so poorly.

At the time I'm writing this review, the overall score of this game is "mixed".
That being said, I'm glad that I bought it before the reviews came up, since I'd probably have skipped it if I had seen the "mixed" rating.
People who are leaving negative reviews are judging this game for something it is not; they are basically downvoting because this is not final fantasy tactics or tactics ogre. I am also a fan of those games, but i recognize that not all Strategy RPGS must follow their formula. So, I am going to talk about HELLENICA, judging it by it's own merits.
Hellenica sets up to do things differently and does a great job. It's world is very well develop and it's a joy to see how historical and mithological characters and places were reimagined in this fictional universe. It provides a creative background for an adventure and you can clearly see that a lot of love and research was put behind it by the developers.
The game does not have a class/job system, but you can see that it would ruin the game if the developers chose to adopt one. That is because in this game, each character is UNIQUE, each one having their own skills. To give an example, a certain famous philosopher has the dialetic skill, which can stun nearby foes by engaging in philosphical discussions with them. This is much more interesting than giving an historical character  the possibility of becoming a generic thief or knight.
The battle system also works very well. You have to find ways to make each character's skills compliment each other in order to achieve the objectives and earn experience points. It's a different system that disencourages farming for XP and really makes you think about how you will approach each battle and which skills you will choose. I like it a lot.
I think the branching storylines are also very interesting; they keep the story moving along and  allow you to explore the world, assuring that you are always somewhere interesting. If you are thinking "I wonder how X city would be portrayed in this universe", you can probably go there in this game. About the characters, I really like them. Nephele and Brasidas made me laugh a number of times.  The character art is also really lovely.
I'm not very far into it, but i already think Hellenica is a great game and that the developers have achieved something really special here. I hope to see more from this studio and they will have my full support from here onwards. I am entirely happy with my purchase and i recommend you give this game a try.
However, some changes i'd like would be for all objectives to be revealed before each battle and the implementation of controller support, for the complete retro experience. I would also prefer if cities were represented as explorable maps, instead of background images.

Okay so I am giving this SRPG a thumbs up.....
However, if you are looking for a deep stat heavy strategy game you are not going to find it here. This is really more of a casual game and there is little in the way of challenge for a veteran of the genre.
It fits the style of many of the great SRPG's of yore and there are some cool concepts wrapped around a unique setting here so I give these guys a hand for being original. The story is so-so and the characters have personalities that are not overly endearing but give you enough to keep you awake through the cutscenes. However, I can't recall any other steampunk greek settings and I found exploring this world to be enjoyable.
My biggest gripe here is that there isn't much depth to the combat system. It's not terrible combat system in that there is value in placing your units correctly and making use of attacks and abilities to push and pull other units around the map makes for some decent combos and interesting choices. What this game really lacks are basic staples of SRPGs. There is no equipment, class system, or standard individual unit leveling system and there all things that would have made this game alot better. The abilities that you do have for the most part aren't restricted and can be spammed which leads to some really repetitive gameplay. It seems like the mechanics were not though all the way through. For instance the lead character has a bear form that she begins every battle in and every three turns reverts to human form than back to bear form and so on. It would have been better to have the bear form come into play only after certain conditions where met and or mantained because as it is it just feels like your running autopilot.
I guess the long complaint is really a product of how much potential this game has and will go unrealized. Despite it's shortcomings there's alot to like here and having a few easier games added to the SRPG genre can only help to expand it's audience and hopefull usher in more of its kind.

This game reminded me of Tactics Ogre, which is why I got it. It is not that game, nor a clone of that game unfortunately. I went in hoping for a game like that, or like Final Fantasy Tactics, but the gameplay is really dumbed down in my opinion. There are no items, or a class system, only skills, and this really detracts from what I loved about those tactical rpg's so many years ago. It is not overly expensive, which is good, but probably should be $10, not $15. All that being said, I couldn't in good conscience, recommend this game to anyone. Some people will enjoy it I am sure, but from my perspective, it is a pale comparison to the old tactical games of yore that lit up my childhood.
Edit:  I want to stress one thing here, that I do not believe this is a BAD game. I went in hoping for something, that the devs did not deliver, NOR did they promise to deliver that. I got my hopes up for something that would have been awesome in my opinion. Final Fantasy Tactics and Tactics Ogre were triple A titles, that cost $50-$60 back in the 90's. This game is NOT on their level, and for the cost of this game, it shouldn't be. If you like straight forward tactical games, and don't care so much about story, this could be for you. Like I said though, it feels really dumbed down, and lacks a lot of hallmarks of previous Tactical RPG's of yore. If you want FF Tactics or Tactics Ogre, there are much better options out there, and they will not give you such a let down.
And enough about minutes played, I opened the game directly, not through Steam, to avoid Steam Overlay, which also does not track minutes played. I did give this game a couple hours, more than enough time to figure out it isn't what I wanted.

Let me say first that this game is a good game. Very good combat mechanism, gameplay and story. I loved the game. That is why I decided to buy it after I beat the Denuvo free (cracked/pirated whatever you like to call it) version. However, I would not recommend this game, not untill you have tried it out first and can decide for yourself.
Here is why:
-(1) Graphical bug. My laptop is 1080p, so I did not have too much resolution problem, but there are objects in the game that have poor texture quality. The most noticable one is the cargo container next to your transporter in the resistant camp.
-(2) Crashes. Regardless which version you play, pirated or legit, you WILL get crashes. I had crashes several times after I bought the game. It can be quite frustrating considering the game does not have auto-save. Some people reported the game is unplayable. It is also possible. Again, you need to decide if you can tolerate the crashes,
-(3) Very POOR PC control integration. Keyboard binding is the only one you can change in this game. There is no way to change or assign keys for you mouse. Good thing I have a xBox controller.
-(4) NOT fully voiced. Other than the main story line and the side quests, the game is NOT voiced. It doesn't have voice when talking to NPC. It doesn't have voice when buying from merchant. It doesn't even have voice when talking to your follower (9S or 2B). WTF... There isn't that many character you can interact with in the game, there is really no reason for not including a voice for a few more sentences (Words in some cases).
For a game priced at 60USD, all these issues are unacceptable. It does felt like the game was rushed out of the production line despite it was delayed. I hope the above list can be removed in the future updates, but untill then, I would not recommend anyone to buy it unless you have tried and loved it.
Judging by the quality, half of the price probably goes to BS Denuvo. I can tell you that this game will be the first and the last Denuvo game I buy. I would gladly support the developers, but I would never again support a bad publisher like SE and Denuvo, who promotes misconducts of bad game publishers.

PROS ~
+Combat - The Combat here is fluid and actually feels like you're making a dent, I play a Spellslinger so I'm naturally dodging around the enemy shooting as many holes as I can, and it feels great.
+Class Skill Building - As an extension to combat are skills and other...combaty things. Back to point is like most MMO's as you level up a class you unlock skills and attacks you can then assaign to your hotbar for use. HOWEVER, you also get AMP's and Upgrade Points that can increse character stats or even upgrade your skills entirely, respectively.
+The World - Nexus is gorgeous, The whole artstyle I could call a 'Cell-Shaded 80's Saturday Morning Cartoon'. It knows when to use color and when to turn up the spooks and edge and darkness. From Bright colorful forests of Celestion to the Orange Savannahs of Deradune to the Purple Strain of BlightHaven, it's just gorgeous
+Character - This game's humor is something I would liken to a slightly toned down Borderlands style of humor, if you want, Go onto Carbine's youtube and look up their Wildstar shorts, besides the fact that they are pretty funny on their own right, they do a good job at explaing basic concepts of the game (Classes, Paths, Races, Ect) Speaking of...
+Paths - Besides choosing a class you also are given a choice of a Path, which is pretty much how you enjoy playing MMO's. Like exploring an area and spamming your jump key? Explorer Path. Want to know the ins and outs of a Rowsdower and learn all you can about the lore of this game? Scientist Path. Enjoy being a team player and bring neccesities like shops to the farthest reaches? Settler Path. Just like killing♥♥♥♥♥♥ Warrior Path
+Housing - Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ Wildstars Housing is one of the best housing systens ive ever seen. YOU CAN PUT ANYTHING ANYWHERE, WANT A FIFTY FOOT TEDDYBEAR OVERLOOKING A QUAINT GARDEN TEAPARTY? YOU CAN DO THAT NO PROBLEM. Sorry, I get exited about housing
+Music - I make it a point to always listen to a games soundtrack, and Wildstar is one of the best I've heard. It's a big mesh of Sci-fi, Western, and 80's Action Film. It's such a treat to listen too. And hey, Officially released VG OSTS are always a win in my book
MIDDLEGROUND ~
~ Cash Shop - I'm putting the cash shop here because I don't see it as a good thing or a bad thing. Most of what you'll find there are cosmetic costumes, dyes, housing items and mounts. The most 'Pay to Win' thing is a Faster Mount Speed License. No overpowered weapons or armor. Not to mention as you play Wildstar you'll acquire a currency caleld Omnibits, which are used in the Cash Shop, and you get them EVERYWHERE
~ Crafting - Crafting is a hard system to pull off in anygame, they all have their quirks.
CONS ~
-Pacing - Wildstar has a level cap of 50. and I've been playing this game on/off since it's release in June 2014. I'm only level 25. Something about it's pacing spends too long on one sub area and not enough on another. However, I never feel like I'm under leveled or over leveled
-UI - The UI is just....less then ok, if you dont mind mods, find a good UI overhaul. Hopefully one that isnt a worse looking 'Minimalist' UI
-Playerbase - Unfortunatly, a steam release didnt bring in the hordes of people Carbine were expecting, If you're expecting to find massive ammounts of players like in The Broken Isles or Idylshire, look elseware. If you're like me and enjoy some quiet time in an MMO, Wildstar fits the bill
I give this game a 'Wii U/'10 - It's not as well known or as big as it's other MMO Cousins, but what is there is a solid release with a few quirks, at least give it a try.

Going to try to keep this short and sweet. I love basketball so I play this game a lot. There's really not much competititon out there as far the realistic basketball genre goes, so this is what you're left with.
This game isn't garbage by any means, but I would have a hard time reccomening it if you're not a die hard basketball fan. I've been playing the 2k basketball games since 2013 and I can say this by far the buggiest of them all. (In my personal experience.)
Positives:
-Offline can be fun to goof off in. (So long as you're not including mycareer)
-Animations and facial features have definitely improved since 2k16
-Decent soundtrack and sound effects.
Negatives:
-Unplayable online mode. Whether it be the barren wasteland that is 2k online or the UTTER♥♥♥♥♥♥input lag that you experience while playing online, it's quite frankly the worst part of the game imo.
-Buggy as all hell. My personal MyCareer character with 70 hours logged is completely broken at this point. It started with getting stuck in practice and unable to leave the gym. (Not game breaking. Just very annoying. Especially since it's a COMPLETE GRIND to earn VC in order to upgrade your character, you have to work them in the gym.) Now it's evolved into everytime I open my phone, the game freezes and it won't allow me to progress. Leaving that mode completely useless at this point.
-A complete cash grab if you plan to do anything but quickplay. Whether it be buying cards for your deck or upgrading your character. You can't do anything without VC. Which in order to earn VC, be prepared to grind your♥♥♥♥♥off. (Especially in MyCareer where your early character can barely make a free throw. You can play at a lower difficulty, but the game essentially punishes you for doing so. It will cut the VC you earn in half if you lower the difficulty.)
-Complete skill capping in MyCareer. Which basically means if you have any plans to create a KD or Greek Freak type character, you can forget it. You can only progress your characters skill tree to a certain point with each build. So if I create a great dribbler, there's no chance he can be a great shooter. (So that would be a no on a custom Steph Curry as well.)
-Difficulty scale very unbalanced. I can't stress enough how much the difficulty jumps from Pro to All-Star. This is best noticed on the 1v1 mode in blacktop. Defense is either mentally handicapped and will allow you to walk by them or they lock you down like glue with no hope of getting around them. They do have the option to custom slide the skills of the CPU you're playing, but the fact this has to be done to accurately adjust your opponent is quite annoying. It becomes literally infuriating. Especially considering my next point....
-INPUT LAG. INPUT LAG. INPUT LAG. I CAN'T stress enough how badly this game suffers from this issue. I've gone through settings, forums, and even controllers to fix this issue. But the game is just not built to respond quickly to your commands. Which is fu#$ing horse sh@t in this day and age. (Pardon the language.) But I can't tell you how many times I've wanted to break my controller while defending someone. Because the difficult is not scaled properly, you're left playing on a higher difficuly for realism. (In my case at least.) So that means when you're attempting to guard your oppenent, you're ALWAYS two steps slower than they are. It becomes impossible almost. (Just watch someone play a 1v1 and you'll get what I'm talking about.) And this is just in single player modes. You can forget online modes.
Overall, I play it because I love the game of basketball. Not because this game deserves it.
TL:DR - Don't buy this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥cash grab of a game. It'll nickel and dime you with the hopes of becoming fun.

Wurm Unlimited really is a game unlike any other in feel. When it says you can go anywhere and do it; you can. Now that the game is available off of the official servers it takes that tagline and runs even further with it. This offline version will not only offer the go anywhere, do anything mentality it will also offer moddability and innovation.
The game is written in Java and the code is thus far unobfuscated. This means that any modding community that crops up, and we're already seeing a seed of one, will be able to expand relatively unfettered. This means a lot for the longevity of the game, which by the way is already monumental (the online version has existed for a decade), will stretch even further. It will also allow for advances in approachability for the uninitiated.
The game itself is by first definition; relaxing. It lacks the fast paced motifs and get-stoned-by-some-naked-dude-as-a-fresh-spawn mentality of other games of this type. It also lacks cutting edge graphics, but the graphics it does present are relatively clean and playable. I see some beauty in it and you can too if you just look at the screenshots. This also allows for the game to run on older systems. The game also lacks smooth animations, but the animations that do exist get the point across.
The game's main to dos are listed in the various trailers and description. A lot of it fails to mention the passable magic/faith system in the game that takes it from just a medieval todo to a more fantasy one. Also, the dragons, fiends, giant spiders, and hellthings help move that along.
The game as of now offers two modes. An Adventure mode which I would recemmond to new players as it bundles in a tutorial, and a "creative" mode which uses the term not like that certain world-renowned voxel game, but in the sense that the land is virgin and it is up to you and/or your friends to shape it. The adventure has some prebuilt areas and will guide you through the shallows of the game.
Overall Wurm is a game similar to many, but in a way unique, and the first of it's kind by age, if not function. I'm not saying the game is perfect, because no one will say that, but it is a solid buy. Do not expect instant gratification from this game, and in return it will give you hours, days, months, and maybe years of play time.
So go now! Strike the earth, mold the clay, and fell the tree, but most of all... Welcome to Wurm Unlimited!

Galactic Crew is the debut title from solo indie developer, Benjamin Rommel Games.
Galactic Crew lets you take on the role of a space pirate or trader of your own choosing, dropped into a small space ship in a procedurally generated galaxy, and left to fend for yourself.
As a pirate you earn credits and renown by, well, acts of piracy. Destroy enough ships -- civilian and pirate -- and an overpowered law-abiding nemesis will spawn and chase you about the galaxy, homing in on your position like a spacey bloodhound. As a trader you, um, trade. Earn enough money and again an overpowered nemesis will spawn and track you down, in this case a pirate.
In the current Early Access state of the game I'm not entirely sure whether the game has a goal or if you're just supposed to wander around the galaxy until you get bored or die.
The graphics in Galactic Crew seem to be rendered in 3D, but the camera has a fixed angle, with only panning and zooming supported. Panning is sometimes jumpy and erratic.
The ships are the graphical highlight of the game. They look really quite good at first, but there are only four of them and the graphics are largely static, with only few visible changes as you play. The rest of the game seems to feature programmer art quite heavily. Character models are bland and uninteresting. Animations are reasonable, but not very varied. You can choose a model for your character when you first start the game, but they all look basically the same, with the same animations. Weapon effects are minimalist and disappointing: thin coloured lines with no special effects or visible damage.
The interface is only partly explained and sometimes unclear. Ship components, though very few in number, don't have tooltips and mostly have no obvious effects; it took me half an hour of pressing buttons and searching menus before I worked out that you need to walk a character into the teleporter manually to board an enemy ship in combat.
The few music tracks are okay, but mostly forgettable: a range of short, repeated electronic tunes with a minimalist feel, ideal for background music.
Sound effects are very basic, with a couple of different weapon sounds and little else.
The tutorial is fully voiced and there are a number of spoken status messages in the game, such as when a system is destroyed. This is a nice idea and the audio quality is surprisingly good, but the voices themselves seem amateurish and out of place.
Galactic Crew plays similarly and is obviously heavily influenced by FTL, but it is inferior in basically every way; comparing the two is an exercise in disappointment for the Galactic Crew player.
Each time you start a new game a new galaxy is procedurally generated. This itself is a bit disappointing, as there are so few elements that every game ends up basically the same anyway: a few space stations, one shipyard, and a number of other nodes of two different types, asteroid belts or "solar systems". 
Space stations allow you to retrofit modules and systems to your current ship and to trade from the small array of goods available; shipyards allow these same actions, adding the ability to buy a new ship from the four available; asteroids allow mining for resources, if you have a mining laser; and solar systems provide random encounters.
Ship layouts are extremely restricted, so retrofit choices essentially boil down to whether you want a teleporter or a shield and whether you can spare the crew/officer space for a hydroponic module, to save on food. Once you can afford the most expensive ship you no longer even need to make the choices; you can simply have everything.
Trading is limited, too. Every station seems to have the same prices for all goods, or very nearly so, and there's no practical differences in any of the trade goods except for food and energy crystals, which you'll probably end up mostly keeping for your own use anyway. The rest may as well just be removed and replaced with a generic "Trade Goods" placeholder.
Asteroid mining doesn't seem to work, or at least I couldn't manage to do it, even with the engineer background.
That leaves the random encounters, which one might expect to provide variation and replayability as in FTL, but which actually all devolve into four situations: nothing, combat, planetary exploration, or betting food or energy on potential gain. The first of these is straightforward: sometimes nothing of interest happens, or nothing you can do, anyway.
Combat is rudimentary. You select a character, select you weapon or weapons, and target an enemy ship component. Enemy weapons are never destroyed before the hull is reduced to zero, so there's basically no tactical targeting. Meanwhile your enemy is attacking you, so you assign your other characters to repair the module being targeted. If you have a teleporter and you can work out how to use it then you can also teleport characters onto the enemy ship, but mostly you don't need to bother. I loved FTL's combat. I have trouble staying awake in Galactic Crew's.
Planetary exploration sounds like a great idea, but as with combat it's rudimentary and boring. You teleport to the surface, wander around an extremely small map, pick up some resources, and leave. It's disappointing in the extreme. It's also very laggy to pan the view.
Finally, the remaining encounters let you help someone, explore a derelict, or similar. These either devolve into combat or consume food or energy to give you a random bonus: a crew member, salvaged resources, or nothing. There's little variation and little of interest.
Add to this lack of interesting content a number of annoying bugs and the game really doesn't seem very appealing at the moment. The worst I've seen are the exceptions (crashing the game) and broken in-game achievements. The price is also way too high for the content available, especially when you consider FTL's regular and sale prices.
Pros:
+ Some good ideas ...
Cons:
- ... implemented very poorly: boring combat, rudimentary AI, lack of content, ...
- Buggy
- Overpriced
I was really excited to have a chance to play Galactic Crew, but so far I've been disappointed. It's a bare-bones FTL clone with boring combat, limited tactics, and repetitive gameplay. Even though it's in Early Access I can't bring myself to recommend it, especially at the asking price. Play FTL again instead.

Some interesting mechanics buried in an unfinished game. It plays like most turn based, grid based strategy games. You have zones representing your move distance and your ranged attack distance. Attacks have a percentage chance to hit. Your "warcasters" have an interesting mechanic, where they have a limited number of action points per turn, that they can choose to spend on extra attacks or attack boosts for themselves, or give to their golem-like "warjack", which is big and powerful, but has to stay near them.
However, you probably won't care enough to learn more about the game than this. If they didn't claim otherwise, you'd think this was an early access title. I have never seen a worse camera in a game; half the time you won't be able to see your own units. The action camera will switch back and forth between normal view and zoomed in view every time an ally moves or attacks, which results in it flickering back and forth multiple times for every single unit. Everything looks like a blurry, pixellated mess. Attack ranges are unclear from the interface, and unless I am missing something, there's no way to undo a move after realizing you've moved out of attack range.

The story is set in an alternate history version of ancient greece twisting well known greek myths and heroes by adding steam powered technology. The story offers multiple branching paths with a goal to recruit a team of heroes to fight at your side for a final battle, it is impossible to accomish this task in a single play through so you will need to loop time and make new choices. Each loop takes 3-5 hours and features a half dozen or so combat maps. There is a significant amount of playtime available. The limitations of this small indie team are represented in a lackluster soundtrack, a minimal amount of combat effects and simple but effective sprite animations and a limited number of character portraits, which is a shame because I found the character designs to be fantastic and would have loved to see a selection of expressive portraits used during dialog sequences. NOTE: This game was given to me by the developer for review purposes. This did not influence my review in any way.
Hellenica is a role-playing game set in an alternate-history steampunk-themed ancient Greece, featuring turn-based combat and anime-style characters.
In Hellenica you play Diona, an Arktos of the god Artemis, with the ability to transform into a bear. The game begins with Artemis giving you a warning and a sacred quest to discover and overcome a dangerous threat to Greece. Immediately you're joined by the young and enthusiastic Nephele, a priestess of Apollo with a thirst for adventure, and the two of you set out for Athens to learn more.
Graphics - The game features chunky pixel graphics rendered in 3D. The battle scenes are divided into squares, and each square is a three-dimensional tile. Environments range from relatively bland and uninteresting to creative levels with moving parts. Characters are well animated large-pixel sprites that are charming in their own way.
Conversations in the game include large anime-inspired portraits that are mostly colourful and nicely drawn. Not knowing much about the game before I played I was a bit surprised to see the typical 'big eyes, small mouth' look of anime in a game about ancient Greece, but it works really well and looks good.
There are no graphics settings other than a full screen / windowed toggle and screen resolution.
Sound - Sound effects are minimal and have little impact. They work well enough, but aren't anything to get excited about. Music is pleasant enough to leave on, but when you pay attention to it you'll realise that you've been listening to the same track, or small number of tracks, over and over again.
Gameplay - Hellenica plays as a series of turn-based battles on small 3D levels, interspersed by short cut scenes using the battle scene graphics, as well as 'town' areas in which you uncover the story through conversations with NPCs, and unlock characters and paths forward. Each choice takes up a day on the game's timeline, and there's no way to go back to previous choices (other than restarting, of course), so the game provides at least a few play throughs to see each choice.
The battles are the core of the gameplay and they're very well done. I'm a fan of turn-based combat, so it didn't take me too long to get the hang of it, but the lack of any sort of tutorial is a shame, especially considering the game introduces some concepts that aren't that common in the genre, such as falling and collision damage, environmental damage, and throwing other characters around!
Each turn each of your characters can both move and use an attack or ability. The order in which you assign them is the order in which their actions play out, so you can rely on effects of previous characters when you assign orders to later ones. This flexibility is key to making the most out of your available characters, as each individual character's attacks aren't that powerful by themselves, but chaining them together -- especially when using the environment to your advantage as well -- can wipe out your enemies very effectively. Once you've assigned all of your actions you end the turn and all of your friendly characters move before any of the enemies. Then it's the enemies' turn and, assuming you're still alive, your turn again, and so on.
Enemies are fairly varied and so are your characters' abilities, and the addition of falling, collision, and other environmental ('trap') damage makes for some great combos.
The story is creative and interesting and mostly very well written, although I've spotted a couple of typos so far. And don't let the "Made with Unity Personal Edition" splash screen turn you off; this game is a perfect example of the sort of professional product that can be made with the free version of Unity. Kudos to The Dragonloft for doing such an excellent job.
Pros:
+ Excellent pixel graphics with nicely drawn anime portraits
+ Creative story that is well written
+ Fun and interesting turn-based combat
+ Multiple story paths giving some replayability
+ Steam (haha!) achievements and trading cards
Cons:
- No tutorial or how-to-play information, leaving you to find out controls for yourself
- It's a bit too easy to accidentally skip a character; a warning dialog when ending your turn with characters remaining would fix that.
Hellenica is an excellent new indie RPG with a creative game world, interesting game mechanics, tactical turn-based battles, and pixel graphics that have personality and charm. It's been quite a while since I played an indie RPG that I enjoyed this much.

Stellaris is a game that so very much tries to break the mold in every way. It tries to define itself as being different than other paradox strategy games, it tries to define itself as being different than other 4Xs. It succeeds by being an ultimately mediocre experience.
Don't get me wrong, Stellaris isn't bad per se. It is however, firmly lacking in any real depth and really just isn't good. Most of the early game is expanding while trying to produce enough energy credits, while mid and lategame involves being bored to tears with the simplicity of the game.
The biggest issue in stellaris is very poor balancing and design in general for a strategy game. See, in your normal 4x game, you can't cover an entire empire with one fleet. You'll be out of position for any defensive purposes. In Stellaris, this isn't an issue, as two out of the three starting options are great. Wormhole networks allow for ships to warp to or from a wormhole station at extreme range and speed, making you unpredictable and able to be everywhere at once, and warp has a range so large that it similarly doesn't matter.
On top of that, fleet engagements are primarily decided by if you have more DPS than your opponents fleet. Most wars are one side disabling the other's fleet, and then going around and destroying every single station, and repeating ad nauseum every war against them until they are completely absorbed. Shields and armor feel like they add only a mediocre level of variety, leading to a mid to end game that is boring as you slowly grind up other nations to reach an arbitrary counter.
On top of that, the research system is an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥how. Rather than any semblance of an ordered research tree, the game instead draws random cards based on your empire's research and the traits of your departmental scientist. This means that you can get into the situation of getting close to mid-game without being able to field weapons on par with your neighbors because you just didn't have the opportunity. The system, while likely an attempt to force players to work with what they can get, instead comes off as a gimmick to force more playing time by adding arbitrary difficulty to some runs.
In closing, the game is a waste of time I cannot in good faith recommend. It's a mediocre game that will make you wish you were either playing a better paradox strategy game, or a better 4x game.

This was a purchase that happened quite suddenly. I saw it in the store, noticed the charming similarities to Final Fantasy, Breath of Fire, and other turn-based RPGs of yore and took a chance. I'm glad I did.
For those players who complain about having to grind out a few levels/good gear, there is no hope. RPGs are not for you. These type of games encourage exploration, re-exploration, and aiming for the best. If you want your characters doing incredible damage, it takes time and effort, and this is reflected in the gameplay. There are 6 playable characters, each with a substantial amount of depth in their skills, special abilities, and battle bursts. This game can be a walk in the park if you choose to make it so, but setting it to legendary difficulty will stretch any player.
EXAMPLE 1: I was kicking major butt at lvl 8, I thought I had good gear, and my party was strong. Lvl 10 slime hunt in the sewers? Give me a challenge! 15 minutes later, my party emerged, beaten and broken. Lesson learned: don't over-estimate your abilities.
EXAMPLE 2: Spent an hour farming Mana Rifts for a few pieces of gear. I'd worn myself pretty thin and thought I'd quickly run back to town after the boss and replenish my potions. An airship passing by had other ideas. The scurvy crew aboard laughed at my pathetic attempts to beat them and soundly thrashed me. Next lesson learned: always be prepared.
This is a wonderful game with plenty of challenge, lots of achievements to aim for (the bestiary... ugh) and a storyline worthy of your time.
Do yourself a favour, put your patience in a box and immerse yourself in this great game. For the price, I doubt you will be disappointed.

Wurm....oh where do I start??!?
So, I've played Wurm Online (The MMO version of WU) And have had Amazing stories in the living, breathing world.  Good and bad, of course. Was it worth it though? Yes...So much yes. Especially with the friends I made. (hey! :D)
If you've played the game,.. Well, WU is basically WO...With full customization at our control.
Wurm is a Sandbox....For me, it's "THE" Sandbox. And now that it's released it's own stand-alone version, where I can mod the game to my liking, It's trully  - Finally - The game i've been waiting for.
With over a 100 skills (I'm not sure the exact amount) you can bet you will find many that you will enjoy, I won't lie though, be warned, Some (Like beverages) Have little use currently.  (There ARE uses, just not much) And some skills have this problem.  But once mods are made, I can't imagine what this will become.
However, there are PLENTY that work. Blacksmithing, Woodcutting, Carpentry, Weaponsmithing, Fishing, Mining, this list doesn't really stop.   most skills involve what we call "Imping" - Which is improving your tools, weapons, armour, gear, vehicles, Ect.  The higher the "quality" of a item, the better it performs in it's task. and the less damage it takes while in-use. I can assure you one thing, You can-not find a better crafting game right now. And I don't think you will for a VERY long time.  this game lives, and breathes, because of the crafting.
Now, in WO (Wurm online) The skill gain is very slow, it takes years to level up skills, and only a hand-full of people have hit "100" in a skill.  However, WU you'll be able to set your own speed, So if you wish - You can have it slow, Or you can speed it up. it's YOUR choice! (Default speed on WU is 10x that of WO)  - As a side note, The higher your skill, the better you can craft things /Improve them.  At very low skill,  lets say for example 30, it would be very hard to improve a item over 40.
The World: Everythings destroyable. Every tree, Every mountain.  Want to dig down 500 feet? Well, if your servers that big. go for it!!  Terraforming in this game was hard to understand at first (For me) But after a while, it got so much fun. You and the players build it, are you in the middle of a huge landmass in a lake, but want to connect it to the ocean? it may take a while, but you can dig/surface mine a "canal" To the ocean, so boats can enter!
Each tree is one that randomaly generates, or you plant.  You can "pick sprouts" from trees, "prune" them to let them live longer, ect.  Forestry/gardening is one of my favorite skills. I love creating my own forest for the world.
Trasportation? Yep. we got that. Horses with saddles/horseshoes/bardings to increase speed, armour, turning. ect.
Carts, Large and small, Wagons, and multiple boats (Caravel, Cog, Knarr, ect) I personally am not a huge fan of sailing, as it's pretty slow, but (Again!) we get to change that up in our own servers. :)
Combat: Combat is a bit odd, and I really want mods to improve/overhaul this.  The combat is, basically, clicking on a button for where you will aim (The head? The legs? Ect) and same for blocking.  The good thing is, aiming at area's have benefits.....For example, if your in PVP and you hit a guy hard in the foot, he will start moving slower.
There IS archery and spells, However, I will warn you - It's not exactly a "main combat" role at the moment.  Mods again, are likely to change this.  Archery REALLY needs to be easier to use as it's a button-click fest right now.  Spells are only "supportive" in combat, and not really a main fighting style.
And we have a "God" system in wurm, This is a very big part of the game, as we have "missions" (sort-of like quest that random-generate) to do things for them for karma (used in spells) and sleep bonus (used for gaining double exp for a short time)  Also, you can become a follower of one that gives some benefits.  You can also become a priest, Which allows you to enchant weapons, armour, and tools for special effects (Increased speed-of-use, More damage, More experience gain, Ect) I really can't wait to see what mods come out for priest...and new spells. :D  Also, champions.  basically a better version of a priest, but limited in number on server.  They're mainly used for combat - they're the big PVP guys you want to kill first! or you will face the wrath of there gods abilitys.
EDIT TO PRIEST:  Priest (Not champions) by default are limited in what they can do, For example, Vynora priest can't mine, dig, ect.  though they can cut trees, farm, ect (each priest has different can-do and can-not.  All priest are not allowed to "Imp" things.  However, in WU you can change this to have different/no restrictions if desired.  Champions do NOT have these restrictions, despite being able to cast spells ect.
CONS?
Bugs,  Lots of weird, little bugs.  I have very few issues personally, but some players have a lot.  (For example, a large cart on some players screen will appear 10 feet away from where it really is...) Or doors not opening (usually due to server lag, though)  Nothing to big usually, But a bit of annoyance at times.
Animations aren't the greatest.  I really wish there was more, and "better" of what we have.
Character models feel odd because of the animations. They also could have a model improvement IMO, however, they don't look to bad. (Also, some of the gear for them actually does look pretty sick!, that's not a con obviously :P )
Default speed of WO (which Isn't the same as WU) is pretty slow for the normal player.  WU is a lot faster from what I've seen so far.  But the game isn't like, For example, Ark. it's slow.  I personally Like this, as it gives a sense of accomplishment.  The good news is, however, that if you DON'T like this, you can speed it up as much as you like, and where you like. (Or the server you join can)
If you want a REAL sandbox, One that REALLY let's you do what you want...... I can't say there is a better game out there.  Since I found wurm, I've not found one even come close (and I've tried at times) And with being able to mod WU, really anything is possible.  I'd highly recommend.
IF you have any questions regarding Wurm at all, I'd love to help if able! Pm or comment and I'll see if I can help. And, please, If you agree or disagree with this review, please say so! I would love to hear other peoples opinions on this game, good or bad.  I wish I could share the storys i've had in this game, because I've had so many. Especially with all the friends I've made.
TLDR: Highly Recommend to anyone looking for the "true" Sandbox. Especially with WU being moddable.
Edit: Also like to state, i've played wurm since 2012, which isn't long at all compared to most members. But in that time I quickly grasped the game and have gotten to the point now where I can self-sustain all my things at 90ql and do my own enchants.  Most people specialize, I personally, can't.  My minds all over the place.  So if you only like a few skills, or only a few interest you - Don't worry. The skills have a LOT in them that you can spend, literally, years with.  or, if your interested in all of them......you can easily do all of them! (You aren't limited to skills, UNLESS you priest! I will add info to the priest section on this)

This is one of those games that are obviously indie in all the wrong ways - the lack of experience, budget and skill is clear in everything from the numerous bugs to the non-sensical design decisions (why make three versions of the same spell, with different cost, instead of allowing players to set it manually?) to the parts that just feel shoddy and unfinished, like the infamous camera.
I love the tabletop game and I was very excited about a computer version. Sadly, the only thing that really makes it worth playing is the single player storyline, which is decent, and the atmosphere. The game mechanics have been redone to the point where it's a completely different game system - so different that my interest in the multiplayer is quickly dying. It's not a game for WM/H gamers, it's a generic computer game based on Privateer Press IP, and it's not a very good one.
For people who aren't into the tabletop game, there is little point in buying this. I enjoy it mostly because of my love for the setting, I doubt I'd have played more than a few missions otherwise. The camera is annoying and takes a lot of work, the interface is clunky and inelegant, the game is riddled with bugs (including crash-bugs and bugs that allow both the player and the computer to do things like walking through walls), there are still minor problems that should have been gone long before launch (like the colour of various important lines and markers being too light to see on snow, or disappearing under landscape features), the default settings for sound and graphics are way off (I had to reduce the music volume to 2/10 to hear voices), you can't skip cut-scenes (adding to the irritation when you have to restart a mission - there is no option for saving during missions)... the list goes on forever.
In short, this game had a lot of potential, but it is so far away from being what it could that no amount of patching can fix it. I regret buying it at full price, and would caution others against doing the same.

I am slowly getting into the game (I am at Tier5-6 at all different ship classes available in game as of now) and like it very much.
I am a NF (NavyField, RIP) veteran and was really awaiting another game having the same appeal. With Steel Ocean, it is definitely the best game out there that could call itself a sequel, or an improvement, to NF.
I had the chance to test NF2, which is horrible, don't even try to talk about that game. I also was holding great hopes for WoWs by Wargaming, but finally, the game doesn't really align to what I am looking for.
The game is quite a big composition of different elements inspired from various games (NF, WoT, WoWs, Battlestation) and the result is a success, in my opinion.
There was this issue in NF that the BB class was clearly OP (over-powered) and you could actually win the game quite easily just by being a skilled BB captain, the game seems far better balanced here. Especially looking at the role of DDs and CLs/CAs, which where pretty useless in NF (except for AA and anti Sub, when subs where a threat, which wasn't a huge problem most of the time).
Yes, it's a F2P, and yes, if you pay you're going to have a better ship and all than a non premium player with less play time. But I feel that you don't need much to enjoy the game. As long as you use your head, which often allows you to maximize them profits by taking good decisions, and don't waste your money on non-essential features, you can allow yourself a painless grind and enjoy playing longer in your beloved ships by not gaining too much experience (if you're not using premium).
All in all, I recommend the game, it's free, you should take a look and see for yourself.

Living in the shadow of Borderlands 2 is a tall order, and in a lot of ways the Pre-Sequel does fall short: frustrating mission design, a critical lack of downloadable content compared to its predecessor, excessive Australianity, et cetera.
However, there is a lot here from which Gearbox can learn taking the franchise forward. Low gravity gliding is a blast for those with the patience to get used to the floaty maneuvering, and cryo damage, while rather overpowered, provides a very satisfying control effect that puts Borderlands 2's "slag" mechanic to shame. Banter between the protagonists and NPCs adds depth to the characters and replayability for my fellow fluff junkies out there.
Overall, if you played yourself sick of Borderlands 2, this is not worth a full price purchase. But in an age of Steam sales, there is no excuse for intrepid vault hunters not to sample this tasty little slice of Pandora's (moon's) history.

In the character making screen:

I'm fairly new to the NBA 2K scene so I've only played 3 games in the series, 2K13 (on the WiiU), 2K16 and 2K17 (on PC). I have to say, this is possibly my least favourite out of the three on most fronts. I bought this game with early tip-off DLC for £19.
First off, a positive. MyCareer is ok. I'ts better (story wise) than 2K16 (by a small margin) as it dosen't have weird, borderline impossible family relationships. It also focuses more on college basketball than highschool basketball before you reach the NBA. This is much better as, instead of making you pick a high school team that you know nothing about (as they don't exist outside the game) you go straight into picking from a handful of college teams.
There is however, a massive downside to the MyCareer section of the game. Although I wasn't really taken by the 2K16 storyline, 2K17 dosen't seem to have one at all! You rely on one sentace quotes during loading screens after your college games to tell you that (once again) you are the college student everyone is looking at drafting this season. It's generic, it's boring, but it's over pretty quick. You do actually get paid for college games this time based on your performance in the game which is nice, but kinda dosen't fit with the college scene.
Then, out of the blue, you get a call inviting you to go and play for Team USA. I didn't really see the point of this as it felt really out of place. One minute you're in a classroom learning about biology and doing a team project, the next, you're playing with Team USA. Also, side note, the guy who calls you's voice acting is utterly terrible. It's so flat and boring to listen to and I couldn't find a way to skip it. One of the commentators does say that it's tradition to take a college player on the team, but the transition from doing school work to playing basketball is way too quick.
When the draft comes around, you finally start to get to play NBA basketball. You seem to start off with better minutes than you do in 2K16. (This might be because I finally knew what I was doing this time as when I played 2K16, I didn't have a clue). After the draft, you go to your 'MyCourt'. This (for those who don't know) is your own personal, customisable space where you can shoot some hoops alone, or with friends. You can buy balls, backboards, wall murals, floors and much more.  In 2K16, the MyCourt looked really nice. It was sleek and it looked like a large, converted garage with lots of designated space to put earned memrobillia. 2K17's MyCourt is an old warehouse with a bar, snooker table and court. I really don't like the design and (as far as I'm aware), you can only place murals on one wall of the building and it's the wall you barely see unless you turn around and shoot towards the opposite hoop.
MyPlayer feels downgraded too. Some features such as asymmetry and blemishes have been removed. The rest is pretty much the same as 2K16. Your players face is the only truely customisable thing. You can't really change their body shape par making them taller, shorter, a bit heavier or lighter. I set my player to the lightest he could be so that I had more speed. My sister actually came in while I was playing it and said 'why is he so fat?'. I would have liked to have had more control over my player as it dosen't really feel like he is truely 'my player'. I also had multiple issues with the face scanning via the 2K17 Companion App which resulted in me just sculpting it as normal and giving up with it.
Maybe I'm doing something wrong, but off-days during the regular season are just practice, or nothing. With 2K16, you had the option to go places with NBA stars, meet fans, attend sponsors events for extra VC and much more. All that seems to be gone now. I've only had one sponsor, and that was Nike for some custom shoes and the like.
Also, when I try to load some items in the shop, I have to restart the game as it refuses to load the content. My internet connection is fine and this problem has happened multiple times while I've been playing the game. I also have the age old problem of players walking through chairs, putting their arm through other players and objects, coaches talking but their mouths not moving and multiple commentary errors such as how many free throws a player has been awarded. These issues have been in every NBA 2K game I have played.
When you play the game, the other team (and your own players) actions, seem to depend on how well you play. If you don't stay with your assignment, the other team will be able to make rediculous 3 point shots and get them in the basket perfectly. It dosen't seem to depend on where the shooter is standing, how far away he is, who is defending him and so on. It makes play feel solo. Like you're not actually playing with a team. For example, I was playing the Cavs, and I passed the ball (accidently) to a player who was heavily guarded. It said I had a turnover (one of the Cavs players had touched the ball but my player still had the ball and play continued as normal). Because of this supposed 'turnover', my player missed the easiest lay-up I've ever seen, causing the Cavs to grab the rebound and make a 3 point shot from just over the middle of the court. This sort of thing has happened multiple times where I will guard the wrong person (as it keeps changing and I don't realise) and the other team will make stupid crazy shots from my mistake.
There are however some good features in this game (not that these excuse the bad features). The soundtrack IMO is better than 2K16 as there are less songs with massive chunks missing as they had to be censored out.
The use of real world videos of outside teams staduims is very nice and the social media loading screen (although sometimes confusing due to the mix of dates) is quite a nice touch that keeps you up to date with what your fans think of you and your performance.
Overall, as much as I would like to, I cannot reccomend this game at the RRP. If the game was £15 in a sale or something then it's worth it. I beleive 2K16 is a much better choice, even if it is flawed.

Chronicon is a pleasant surprise. For a long time, I have been searching for an ARPG to play, but none of those I tried succeeded at entertaining me. Until I found Chronicon. This game is DEFINITELY worth your attention.
TLDR: ARPG done the right way, 9/10 (highly recommended)
I finished all three available acts in approximately 18 hours. During this time I haven't been bored or annoyed for a single moment. The leveling is reasonably fast, but it will definitely get slowed down a bit when the game is finished. Within 20 hours, I got to level 85 (the cap is 100), while playing on Veteran difficulty. That made me really happy, because I detest having to farm the entire evening and getting like 3 levels out of it.
The fighting system can be described as a pure carnage. After I got over the slow start, got my set of skills and better gear, the bloodbath started. I played frost-fire warlock that specialized in corpse shattering and burning. Most of the time I would just run around, turning enemies into chain-exploding nuclear bombs. The challenge of getting rewarding high kill-streaks makes you play as stylishly and brutal as possible, ensuring a lot of fun in the process.
The skill system is remarkable. There are 4 skill trees for every class that you can combine as you please. Some skills are of course slightly imbalanced, but given the fact that the game is still in the early access, I expect them to be tweaked. You can also easily reset your skills and masteries with a cheap potion, so you can experiment with your builds. Neat!
The difficulty itself could use a bit of balancing as well. Most of the time I would just run around and blow everything up. Sometimes I even instantly blew up bosses. But there were a few bosses who would just instakill me a few times, even though I was doing my best at dodging and kiting.
Items in this game are just great. There are tons of loot dropping constantly, so I would suggest smartly setting up your item filter for the Alt-key. This feature is handy and makes looting and sorting through stuff comfortable. Items of high rarity DO drop very often and moreover, all the legendary items (and maybe even unique, I don't remember) you find are available for your class. Amazing, isn't it?
On the other hand, I didn't find many uses for consumable items. As for the keys, I didn't have enough of them at the beginning, but now I have so much of them that it doesn't matter for me if the chests are locked anymore. Town portal scrolls are present basically just from the nostalgic obligation, as you easily gather more of them than you can use. I don't know what to think about these features, maybe they are a bit unnecessary. As for the buff potions, I didn't feel any need to use them, so I eventually stopped picking them up to save inventory space. I personaly think that consumable items could use a bit of developer's attention.
There is nothing much to tell about the story. I would say it's decent and it fits nicely with the game atmosphere. I don't care about the story in this type of game anyway, and usually skip story passages in additional playthroughs.
Music is nice and the "voice acting" made me giggle a few times. As for the art - I like the game visuals. It requires a bit of polishing here and there, but overall it's quite decent. I don't even mind the fact that the gear doesn't change the appearance of the character. What I would like to see though, is something that would make bosses look unique. Most of the bosses look like larger versions of regular mobs, which doesn't look that great. But then again, we are at the early access, so it may as well change in the future.
To sum up, the current state of the game offers a lot of entertainment. The developer is a nice person who updates fans with news regularly and swiftly comes to offer help to anyone in trouble. If he keeps up the good work, this game might become something very big. I wish him only the best and offer a big thumbs up, because he succeeded in something that even big companies regularly fail at - making a damn enjoyable game!
Final verdict: 9/10 (HIGHLY RECOMMENDED)
Depending on the future state of full release, I may as well change the rating to 10/10 - yep, it's that good.

#April 2017
Now that I have had some time to play I want to flesh out my thoughts.  Know that I chose Templar because the game presented it as the "default" class if you will, so I made the assumption that it would be the most stable with fewest odd skill/gear interactions.
Playing with her was a lot of fun for the first little while, but I quickly realized that at the default game Difficulty of Normal it was going to take me forever to advance my character so I bumped it to Veteran.
Right off the bat I found one of two things were true: at Normal the progression was taking a dog's age and at Veteran the fights were taking a dog's age.  I would like a tweaking of this.  Realistically I'm not going to put in a thousand hours in this game like I would Diablo 3, so please abbreviate the progression.  I'm not trying to be rude just realistic.  I have over 30 hours and my Templar is only level 70ish, so there's TONS of value for the money which is a good thing!!  I would just like things to speed up since the combat aspect of the game isn't all that deep and it's never going to be.  NOT a bad thing, it's one of the lovely things I love about this game, not insanely difficult and very satisfying in general.
I love the look and feel of the maps although even with ambient light turned up the game in general is too dark.  I would like to remind the art director that mood is best created with the contrast of light and dark, not just making a dark dungeon.  This is a minor gripe, the graphics are so cool to look at, I really never get tired of looking at them, especially the wide variety of monster sprites.  They didn't cut any corners and there are full death animations, etc.  So cool!  Double the animation frames would be so insane... what I can I say I lust for the days of pixel perfect animation like in Metal Slug, and something about the animation of Chronicon reminds me of that.
I find the maps to be detailed, creative and filled with ornamental touches like tapestries, lamps, candles, etc, etc, etc.  Overall the procedurally generated dungeons are waaaay too large.  I can't sit and commit to 60+ minute dungeon runs before I find the checkpoint.  Sometimes I only have 15 minutes.  I would like the devs to try to keep game experiences into 15 minute chunks the way many big league game co's do.  I'm not dropping names but it's a known practice to keep 15 minutes in mind.
Playing with Templar was boring as heck for the first 30+ levels.  I really didn't enjoy playing until I unlocked the 3rd spell.  Up to that point it was just hold the attack button and watch the enemy health bar go down.  I really think this "baby mode" of the game needs to be severely abbreviated.  Keeping a player with 2 primary attacks and 1 mana spender for 10+ hours is way to boring.
My biggest complaint by far is the mini-map.  It is so hard to use.  Since the levels are insanely huge you'll consult the map constantly, but no matter which of the 5 modes you have it on it never seems to work right and it is mostly in the way.  I'm constantly changing the map view and I hate it.  For goodness sake please fix the map.  Make a one-to-one pixel map in the top, whatever.  But not what it is now.
The 5 modes are
- Off
- Tiny box in top right where you can't see any more than you can on the main screen itself (useless)
- Humongous centered overlay where you can't see where your player is on the map or anything else really
- The above option but right-aligned
- The above option but left-aligned
I really love the loot system.  You can get it to optionally display pointers to things on the ground and you can set the rarity threshold so you can ignore commons, etc.  I would like to see "get all" incorporated into picking up loot.  Clicking a pot should get all pots off the ground.  Getting a legendary material, likewise.  I hate clicking like a banshee.  Once I pick up a common, I think the game can take the hint that I'm picking up commons for cash.
I would also like the potion spam to go away.  Just make 1 size fits all health/mana potion and have them restore a %.  Also make the legendary potions useful.  Zap an enemy with a tiny bit of electricity or whatever doesn't seem worth the bother and inventory clutter.
The "enchanting" area makes little sense, it's where you can re-roll weapon stats, etc.  WIP I assume.
I'm going to keep playing.  I really like this game and it is getting better the deeper I get and the more I level my Templar.  I would look forward to playing new classes once I finish the mission with Templar.  Great game, buy it!

Death God Uuiversity. If nothing else, the title itself piques your interest. And true to it's name - the concept of the game is pretty awesome. You are a student in a University, training to be a Death God. And your assignements consist of assasination missions - or maybe asassination makes it sound too sophiticated. You just have to kill people - no hidden blades or exploding gunpowder is used though. And therein lies it's true potential - the innovative killing methods.
Now if I just knew this much, I would have been interested enough to try it - but there's more. To make the game more fun, the targets are not ordinary people. In fact, most of them are not even "bad guys" in the traditional sense. Take Miley Cyrus for example. Not technically speaking bad, but annoying enough for you to have joked about killing her at least once with your friends. At least I did - and if you didn't then perhaps you should. What's funnier is that you find her in a construction area, surrounded by wrecking balls! This game is pure pun galore, and without giving any more spoilers - this is the gist of what the game is about. The teachers, targets and characters in the game are all borrowed from pop culture, fiction or even mythology - and the unlikelihood of these characters actually being in the situations that the game puts you in, is what makes this an enjoyable experience. (Fun Fact - Did you know Harry Potter smokes?... Like a lot?)
Now coming to my only 2 qualms with the game.
1) Poor framerates, random crashes etc. The technical problems was what marred my experience the most when I first played the game. But the devs responded soon enough, and now theres a patch (2 in fact, although I've not tried the latest one still) that fixes most of the problems. I have not got a single crash after the patch, and the overall camera swivels have become much smoother after patch 1.
2) A slightly diverted plotline. While it is fun to go kill people in unimaginable ways, sometimes you hope for a much more advanced sense of coherence to the overall theme - and DGU manages to do some of it, but not all. I'm only a few hours into the game - so I'm probably making rash early judgements - but there could be a bit more done to make it all come together in a unified sort of manner.
Nevertheless, DGU makes up for it's techincal flaws with a fun concept and humurous characters. The little fellows all run with their arms behind them in an almost anime-like style, and speak in a language that's akin to the minions from Despicable Me. It's totally worth a shot if you're bored playing the run of the mill kind of games being released these days, and while you may find flaws with some aspects, you will enjoy the game as a whole if you relate to this type of gameplay.

D.G.U. is a game I really want to like. It has all the personality and charm that you would want in a game like this. Making fun of pop culture references and being completely silly in nature. The gameplay is rather simplistic but for an adventure that is perfectly fine. The best way to put it is that the tone of D.G.U. is superb. From graphics to music, everything is adorable and strange. Where things fall apart are the technical aspects of this title. From resolution bugs, extremely long load times and lack of cohesive gameplay. I felt I spent more time battling the bugs and looking at loading screens then actually playing the game. When the game did manage to work well, the framerate would suddenly tank for no reason at all. The optimization needs to be fixed for this to be an enjoyable title because the issues suck the fun out of the game. Now the question stands, does the good outweigh the bad? I would say yes, I wanted to see more about the game, it's puzzles, humor, and gameplay. I still do, however the issues make it a sour experience. So I would recommend this game if you truly love the humor, genre, and don't mind dealing with optimization issues.
