Jacob Jones is kind of like Professor Layton's younger, somewhat clumsy younger brother trying desperately to follow in the footsteps of his more refined sibling and doing a decent job at it, if still having a lot of ground to make up.
It helps that he and everyone and everything else in Camp Eagle Feather is so darn cute, with characters that look somewhere between clay models and plushies, toddling around papercraft environments as they present each other with spontaneous puzzles. Jacob Jones in a lot of ways has the feeling of a developer with a wonderful idea mapped out for their game, but who haven't quite gotten a hang of executing it. Dialogue is charming but often a little stilted and drawn out, there's a noticeable lack of music during most of the game, and the interface can be a tad clunky to navigate as it still holds onto its touch-based origins.
They're minor things that never really annoyed me too much, but the game definitely has a somewhat awkward sensibility, which in some ways is charming and at other times just a little dull. Puzzle variety left me somewhat disappointed, relying heavily on observation and maze puzzles which while fine, tended to be simple or not especially well explained. I was disappointed by the lack of critical thinking required to get through most of the first episode, which largely came and went without a great amount of fanfare.
I still enjoyed it without doubt, as I tend to do with anything that takes cues from my much beloved tophat clad puzzle agent, but developer Lucid Games has left a lot of room for improvement in follow up episodes. It's a solid beginning that I'm eager to see expanded upon, I just can't help but notice that the distinct feeling of something missing, though whatever it is seems well within the developer's reach if only they can latch onto it.

games (except for Dark Souls)
Gameplay is fast paced hack 'n slash that flows really well. Once in a while, I know I double tapped the movement keys to dodge, but all I did was move a little to the side. Other than that, great feel to the combat thus far. It seems that Dark Souls has had quite an impact on the RPG/Action games as of late, as a lot of companies are using similar concepts. As NieR uses a similar death mechanic to the Souls series. In NieR when you die, your body is where you died at and you have to get to it to recover items that you had (except for your weapons) and if you die before you retrieve your body, you loose those items, and they can be very important. As when you die, you loose your chips, which is basically buffs like movement speed +4 ect. Also when you die and your connected to the servers, your body will remain for other players to find. In which they can either recover your body for money and a couple temp buffs, or revive your body that will assist the player fight enemies.
As for graphics, I feel as though this could easily run on an Xbox 360/PS3. The graphics are nothing special, tons of better looking games out there. A lot of greys, browns and some green in the first area.  But so far i'm in the first open area, and while it is decently sized, I feel it shouldn't require a PS4 or current recommended PC specs. The grass in the open areas has no physics, and everything feels bland. Which Zelda Breath of the Wild has grass physics and the switch is no where near as powerful as ps4/pc. Many invisiable walls also hinder the exploration of said open areas. One thing I do like is the flowing rivers and streams. They look good.
Another issue I have with the graphics is there seems to be a lot of noticable pop in. I think I read thats from the community mod, but I honestly cant remember. Another thing I have noticed is the NPCs don't move their mouth when they speak. To a lot of people that doesn't matter, but to me, it is very anoying and I notice it every single time, in every game this happens.
Controlls are my main issue though. With M/KB, the controlls are the worst I have ever experienced. Often times you have to take your hand off the mouse and use the arrow keys, which happen during the flying body suit segments, and sometimes segements where it plays more like a 2D sidescroller/topdown twin stick shooter. If you don't use the arrow keys, the aiming is controlled by the mouse, but you have to drag the mouse in the direction you want to aim, or it instantly snaps to the direction your moving. Sorry i'm having a hard time explaining that part, can't think of a better way to put it. Also, some tutorial prompts tell you to use a certain key like the / key, when you can actually just left mouse click, so it feels like it expects you to constantly move your hand from the mouse to the arrow key location. I prefer the M/KB setup, but if you use a controller, I expect you would have a better experience with the controls.
Overall, I'm a fan of gameplay/story (when the story is actually good) graphics mean nothing to me, and I would highly recommend this game to any RPG/open world/Hack 'n Slash fan.

Quite possibly my favorite game of all time, and certainly the most beautiful in terms of the overall package. I am going to start out with it's strongest points.
The story in this game, and more so the way in which it is presented, is nothing short of amazing. I have finished the game now, and found it to be the most thought provoking piece of media I have ever consumed. I feel like I probably sound over the top right now, but this game really resonated with me.
The music is truly a cut above the rest. The quality, the placement, the variety, the appropriateness, the impactfullness of it all; it is just fantastic.
The voice acting is good overall, but one stood out in particular, and I think it deserves attention. Kyle McCarley did the voice for 9S, I had to look him up and had never heard of him, but he absolutely killed it in this game. I thought his performance rivaled Jennifer Hale's in the original Mass Effect trilogy. I hope to see more of him in future games because he seems extremely talented.
The combat and gameplay were all excellent as well. It wasn't the greatest combat ever, but I found it to be very satisfying and I enjoyed it very much. I played the whole thing on Normal and I thought the difficulty was spot-on. I was frequently challenged, but never frustrated. The save system is slightly unusual, and you are only able to save at certain places in the world, but they are numerous and I never once found myself having to re-do a large chunk of the game. You will be stopping by these save points often so it is very easy to remember. Also, contrary to what the actual game tells you, there is some small form of auto saving. There were a few times during the game where I died midway through a multi-phase boss fight, and when I returned, I was still on the phase I died at, and did not have to restart the entire fight. I think that if I had turned the game off at that point, I would have been sent back to my last save, but it was overall much less stressful than I feared it would be. Also, I have an AMD 280x, I had exactly one white screen crash at the very beginning of the game, turned the settings down to medium, left it alone, and never had another problem during the 60 or so hours I spent in the game, and things still looked great.
Overall, if it is not obvious enough, I love this game. It consumed every free moment I had for about a week. I lost sleep, I became a hermit, but it was well worth it, I loved every second of it, and I think I might do it again soon. Nier: Automata  is an absolute work of art, without being pretentious. I think it is a game every human being should play (ya know, if they can actually run the game without it crashing, hope they fix that one day soon.)

Every unique song fit its enviroment while carrying a sense of weight and emotion that fully envoked the history behind the world and its inhabitants.
The real bread and butter though is the story and the characters in it. The level of writing that went into this is on a different level entirely than what we're typically force fed nowadays. You can tell the sheer amount of thought and effort put into each and every character you meet, from our protagonists - all the way down to the shopkeepers and background npcs. I actually found myself dreading finishing this game, it's not every day you find a videogame that comes together this beautifully.
NieR:Automata is an top class 10/10 game and this world is a slightly better place because of it.

Stellaris is a game that can teach you how to be patient. There is a learning curve as with most other strategy games that can be mastered after a few playthroughs in single player. After you get used to it this game is VERY ADDICTING you have been warned!
Some of the things that I can say about this game is:
-Multitasking-
Tons of things to manage:
-Worlds/Sectors (infastructure, populations, governor hiring)
-Diplomacy (Federations, rivals, trading, alliances)
-Technology/Discovery (Hiring Scientists, picking the right technology paths to be ahead of other empires, getting modifiers,building science/research structures, Surveyng)
-Traditions ( more along with choosing empire path)
- Internal Governing (promoting/embracing/supressing factions, hiring empire leaders)
and much other details...
My favorite parts about this game are the roleplaying as the empire you chose which can range from a spiritulist pacifists/monks to WORLD DEVOURING SCOURGE INSECTOID HIVE. I also like the random event chains that can appear which really are interesting and have cool backstories such as the HORIZON SIGNAL.
I did not like the endgame that much because I felt it was introduced into the game a little to late in my single player campaign. I had the unbidden, which are inter-dimensial beings coming to suck the energy out of all living things in our galaxy. When they came they took over a small chunk of the galaxy, but on the other hand I had a federation that included over 50% of the factions ( including a fallen empire). So they were easily defeated. I wish to of have expected the unbidden to wipe out more than half of the empires in the galaxy but they didnt wipe out anyone. Then, after that there is currently nothing to do besides complete all technology or just win the game with domination, federation, or the other thing. Another thing I did not like was how slow it is in the beginning to get started. Just the amount of hours to get certain technologies or find all the other empires felt like a real waste of time in real life.
Overall, great game besides the cons of course and I would recommend to a friend!

The early/mid game is fun and dynamic. The sound track is phenomenal. The extent to which you can customise your race is awesome. But at almost $80USD for the game + DLC (and it's Paradox, so that's only going to keep going up), I can't recommend Stellaris until one major issue I personally have with the game is addressed: The Warscore system.
In the current system, when you declare war (or have war declared on you) you choose from a list of planets (and some other options like humiliation/vassalisation/liberation etc) that will become yours if you win the war, each costing a certain amount of points. The score limit here is 100, most planets costing between 10-30 points, so most of the time the best you can get is 3-6 of their planets, or make them a vassal or tributary. Capturing planets and defeating fleets increases your score, losing them decreases it, first to 100 wins, although somewhere after 50 you can work out an agreement and settle for some of the things on your demand list instead of all of them.
It sounds fine at first but (for me at least) this leads to a few frustrating things. First, even if your fleets and armies destroy every ship and raise your flag on every single planet they own, when the war is over you still only get the 3-6 you could afford from the initial list, and you give the rest back to the empire you defeated. If Vassalisation happened to cost 101 points, you can't put it on the list, so it doesn't matter how bad you beat them, they retain independence. Secondly, you could choose to add their homeworld or best productive worlds to the list, even if you never attack them, and they never see a single part of the war.
Imagine if the allies landed at Normandy, took the beach, and said "Yep that's good enough folks, we'll give this beach back to the Nazis then aaaaand we'll have Berlin, thankyou very much." Or imagine if after defeating Germany all across Europe and marching into Berlin itself, a peace was negotiated where... only Spain and North Africa are liberated, everything else remains under Hitler's rule, the allies go home and aren't allowed to try again for another 10 years.
Depending on your playstyle, war is a significant part of the mid-late game and it consistently turns the first few hours of fun into more hours of frustration. The whole galaxy could be divided between two huge interstellar alliances but when they inevitably go to war even if thousands of ships burn the balance of power will only change by a few worlds, then you must wait 10 years to try again. The end game becomes a very slow, very tedious grind.
There are end game crisis events that can sometimes be fun, but for the most part they either spawn on or in your borders and you either deal with it right away or get destroyed by it right away, or it spawns on the other side of the galaxy and becomes the AI's problem.
If the Warscore system was changed so that the spoils you get in war were related to what you actually claimed during the war, I would happily recommend this game, regardless of the price, because there is a lot of great stuff here. It all just happens to be marred by this one backwards mechanic that makes no sense. Until that changes, save your money and your time, and play something else.

Pretty amazing to see what this game started out as here on Steam to where it is now. Bought this when it first came to Steam last year and let me tell ya it wasn't far off from an unplayable garbage fire; back then I might not have left such a generous review, but the devs have been super active from the beginning and turned this game around.
It's really come a long ways, you can finally sit down an play this for a few hours at a time without issue and actually enjoy it. The last two weeks it's crashed twice and I've maybe lost the progress of a race or two, thankfully though the game saves frequently. Mods are still a little funky, you can't just download a mod and then boot up the game, it's a bit more involved then that but this game's been around forever and there's a ton of support for anything you want to do.
Don't get me wrong, it still has some issues, but $5.99 is a very honest price for where this game's at right now.

Sure other reviews complain about crashes, graphics, stablilty, missing content, etc. But this game was never truely finished way back in the day. It got picked up and restarted and still is being updated by the current devs. If you enjoy tinkering with cars and modding them out then this is the game you have been looking for. Mods make the game more complete with real cars, wheels, engines. I recommend this game strongly just dont expect a racing "sim" handleing, although if you crash your ride you will be fixing it yourself and paying the bill for it!

If you're a fan of the Professor Layton games on the DS, then give this charming title a look. Although it borrows (read: steals) a few of the mechanics from that series-- such as the merit points awarded and finding soda cans instead of hint coins (which fulfill the same purpose)-- this is by no means a bad thing. The world is also beautiful to look at and explore, filled with some very amusing characters with genuinely funny dialogue. Despite the game's shortness-- with just 24 puzzles and the story included-- £4 is good value for what you get, with more promised by the developer to come soon. Despite being somewhat inferior to the Layton series, this is still worth your time if you're craving some lighthearted puzzle action.
PROS:
+Stylish graphics make the game look great
+Charming characters with funny dialogue to boot
+Puzzles are more challenging than the art style suggests
+Cheap
CONS
-Suspiciously similar mechanics to the Layton series
-Some difficulty in clicking on soda cans when Jacob blocks view of them
-Short in length
-Writing memos can be somewhat tricky with a mouse
Overall score: 7/10, would recommend

Amazing game! It has become one of my most favorite mmo's, if not my most favorite.
It has tons of things to do, it has good gameplay with a good battle system (once you get used to it, I will admit it was slightly complicated at first), it has lots of exploration and things to discover, which I love in a game. And it has an amazing story in my opinion, at least for the Exiles. I don't really know much about the Dominion side other than the bad side of it you see from the Exile standpoint...which has kind of put me entirely against the Dominion side and makes me not even want to make a Dominion character even for just testing and curiosity like I originally wanted to do to be honest. I suppose that could be counted as a con.
But anyway, from what I've seen of the Exile story so far, it has a lot of emotional moments and humorous moments. I love games...or anything really...that can actually make you feel something, it adds more depth and makes it more fun in my opinion. It is a game I would highly recommend.
The biggest downside I've discovered so far isn't really anything that has to do with the game itself but how much space it takes up. It's a pretty big game, which makes it difficult for anyone that has really limited harddrive space to even get it. However, if you have any other games you don't really play often and are just sitting around taking up space, or any other unused applications for that matter, it's well worth deleting a few games to make room for this.
PROS
- Amazing Story for Exiles (Again...I can't vouch for the Dominion.)
- Lots to Do
- Lots of Exploration and Things to Discover
- Good Gameplay
- Good Battle System Once Gotten Used To
CONS
- Huge Game (But still well worth making room for it if you can.)
- The Exile Story Makes the Dominion Look Really Bad (If you want to play both sides for curiosity's sake like I originally wanted to, I suggest playing the Dominion side first. Unless of course you simply like playing the bad guy regardless, in that case this likely won't bother you.)

I, like many others, probably looked at the characters of Nier: Automata and thought that it was a game for pervy weebs and I would have no interest in it. However exposure on ♥♥♥♥♥ and Reddit and rave reviews from friends got me to bite the bullet and try it.
This game almost immediately become one of my favorite games. It has a plot that is like the animes you watched late at night growing up, with some of the most badass hacking and slashing combat with shooting mixed in as well. You are drawn in not only because you want to learn more about these mysterious, evolving machines attempting to mimic human cultues, but also because you NEED to see what happens next to these poor psycholigically damaged protagonists.
These poor androids, locked in centuries of combat, forbidden to love, dying only to be resurrected to fight more. They are programmed to serve human masters they have never seen and crave human attention and affection they may never receive. This game quickly hits you right in the feel bads and you no longer care about the wacky outfits the androids wear. You realize it's symbolic. They are blindfolded because they follow orders without question. They are dressed and designed to seem pure but are quickly dirtied and corrupted by the end and are utterly changed by the game events.
Nier: Automata is a mix of Zelda, Final Fantasy, Metal Gear Solid, The Matrix, and Wall:E thrown into a blender and the end result is one of the most fantastic games I have ever played.

Alright I have played about 11,5h thats not to much but I played a little more than a quarter of the American Tree so I can tell you what I like and dislike.
First off I want to say  you get free Gold sometime for completing stuff etc. to buy XP or convert gold for coins and so on.
The game has some features I like:
+The Guns accuracy: The guns are only accurate if you leave them locked in for a few seconds, if you move them they have to adjust again.
+Submarines, SUBMARINES! I think that speaks for itself. Even though they are kinda hard to play.
+Aircraftcarriers: You can adjust your plane setup as much as you want it to be, not like in WOWs where you have pregiven setups.
+ You can control: Main battery, AA GUNS, Torpedoes (Fire one at a time). You can also drop underwater charges from a cruiser to give submarines a hard time. Only Machineguns are controlled by AI.
+More things to research.
+ Customization for ingame Cash -> Lasts only for 7 Days but its not that expensive if you are good player. I think 12k for a camo, thats not much.
+ The Grind: Grinding isnt a pain in the a** that much, it becomes harder if you go up the Tiers and thats good in my opinion because you keep a ship longer and learn more about it's strenghtes and weaknesses.
+ Runs good on weaker PC's, much adjustment to the graphics can be done.
Theres more, find out for yourself, but every good game brings negative aspects with it.
- Physics: The ships accelerate to fast and stop to fast, the weight of the Ships is not to much of a factor yet.
- Shipclasses: The Battleships are crushing right now, the main guns shred everything, hope it's going to be nerfed.
- Matchmaking: Because many people play Battleships right now or Submarines in lower tiers, the matchmaking becomes odd sometimes but you never play with Ships that are higher than 2 Tiers, except you play with a friend who is Tier 3 when you are Tier 1.
- Performance: With some things in the graphics the performance gets kind of bad, the FPS drop down to 20, the game isn't very old so it's more of a "hopefully gets fixed" negative point.
- No European server, normally american server is no problem for me, if my internet has a bad day, I am unable to play but same as above, they will most likely work on that.
These are my main points I want to Stick out to the people thinking about getting the game, it's for free and the dev's are working constantly on it, so give it a shot.

Read a lot of comments that accuse this game to be just a clone of World of Warships but thats kind of an insult for this game in my opinion.
Sure there are some similarities like the progression system for example but it does many, many, many things just way better then WoW.
-The Gunplay requires much more aim and skill then it does in WoW
- Balance ! Matchmaker works great so far. Ship classes are 100% mirrored in 9/10 games. In 1/10 games one team has another cruiser instead of a battleship but things like Submarines or Carriers are always 1:1
-SUBMARINES ! They are well implemented. Of course they can dive but they just have a limited time under water since oxygen runs low pretty fast. There are 2 levels: 1st stage they use less oxygen, can fire torpedos themselves but get hit by torps as well. 2nd stage they can't shoot torps and neither get hit by them, only by water bombs (deep cahrges).
Submarine players really have to be patient and carefully. If you meet a Destroyer u're dead.
-Torpedos: NO AIM INDICATOR ! =WIN. Aiming torps needs practice. You have to judge the targets speed, have to split ur torps so that some will hit if target changes speed/direction and you need to get pretty close. Torp shots at ranges over 1km will probably not hit if the target recognises them.
-BUT !: Torpedos have a range minimum. If yo get to close and shoot ur torps they won't detonate.
It's a brilliant idea. Torps do massive damage but also require some skill and sometimes even pure luck to hit.
-CVs. AWESOME ! They are still strong but it's no OP killfarming machine anymore. Minimum Torp Range applies on torp bombers as well so there is a chance to evade if u pay attention. Also aiming your torpedo salvos is a bit harder then in WoW.
-AA. AA works great. CVs can't just roll their bombers into groups of ships and get away with this. AA kills planes pretty fast. Even faster when players decide to control their AA manually ! Even strikes on single ships with good AA have to be quick. Planes can't circle around ships for minutes while looking for the right anlge to place their torps. If they get into AA range they bein to die.
-Rock, Paper, Scissors. The ship classes are very well balanced. Threre is no one OP ship that can kill everything. Lone wolves won't survive long as well. You really have to play with your team. Every ship has a counterpart. For example:
-BBs are very effective against cruisers but can't do anything against a submerged submarine (they can't even see it without sonar)
-Destroyers are very strong against submarines and battleships if they manage to get close enough for torpedos.
-Cruisers are strong against DDs  ....
A lot of people don't seem to understand that by now. See a lot of cruisers and DDs rushing forward alone and get instand killed within seconds. While DDs can still try to dodge, cruisers usally are toast when they rush forward, get detected and bombarded by BBs. Doesn't mean that cruisers are weak or BBs OP, they are often just played wrong.
You really have to wrok together, know your role within the fleet and have to support each other. If DDs for example rush forward and leave their BBs behind and a hostile submarine manages to slip trough your lines and reaches the BBs it's not the fault of the BBs that they get killed (at least not only), the DDs were supposed to prevent that ;)
All in all the game is very well thought through and if u like naval games definitely worth a try.

It's probably the best JRPG style game I've played since FFX (or FFVII). That said, I like the dialog writing better.
The storyline is quite straightforward, though... not many sidequests, and it's impossible you miss the main story getting distracted by other things to do. Still, it's a good story, and you're along for the ride.
There's a grind part to level up the characters, but is not as bad as in other RPGs. Here, combat is actually fun. The neverending combinations between characters has made me level up all of them, and when I can't beat a specific boss with some characters, a different combination may prove better for that purpose. It's a pity you can't change them on the fly during combat, or in the middle of a dungeon (unless you leave and go in again).
Visually enticing, I really like the looks of it. They make justice to the spectacular original comics. The fact that they choose some comic-style cutscenes instead of videos is a wink to its origins, and I couldn't be happier about it. Pity that they weren't done by Madureira himself, though, but the artist is competent.
Now, my complaint is the unstability of the game. Sometimes I can get a few hours straight of playing, sometimes I can't play for more than 5 minutes. I have a load of error logs due to the game freezing and crashing 10 times in a session. Then maybe next time runs flawlessly. I don't know if there are any bad interactions with other software or what, but it is the same for both my desktop computer and my Surface Pro 4.
When the day is right, though, it plays perfectly in both, using the best graphics configuration (My Surface has Intel i7 with 16 GB of RAM and Intel Iris graphics, my desktop has an AMD Phenom II with 8 GB of RAM and a GeForce GTX 750 Ti). Depending on the combat there might be a slight lag in loading the 3D models for it, but it's like a hiccup that lasts less than a second, in any case.
Best played with controller (I have a Logitech F710), but it's fine with keyboard and mouse. I only wish it could be played entirely with point-and-click, because then I could play with the Surface in tablet mode entirely. I already can do that in combat, and it's like it was designed for it, but moving the characters in a dungeon or in the map needs either the controller or the keyboard. Food for thought.
In any case, despite the bugs and freezes and crashes, it's still a great game, and I'm afraid that I'll be left wanting more when I finish. So I really hope for either DLC content, or a full-fledged sequel. I'd get it without any further thought.

It sucks that Steam doesn't allow you to give a game anything other than a thumbs up or down. This isn't a good game, make no mistake, but it is worth a look if you're a game designer and want to study what not to do when trying to make a JRPG.
It's almost painful, specifically because you can't get through ten minutes in Battle Chasers without feeling the love for the genre and games in general just wafting off of the creators. Joe Madeira has managed to crib almost every rule in the JRPG playbook but he doesn't understand the fundamental concepts behind those rules.
First of all, the game is slow. It's so slow, that I imagine if the game had been designed better most people would take 10 hours to complete it, rather than 20. There are pauses when you enter combat, before you can make an attack in combat, between turns. More popular RPGs like Persona or Pokemon can get by with turn-based combat because of how quick they are designed, especially if you're smart. Do yourself a favor and time the average combat in Persona 5 or Pokemon and measure it against Battle Chasers and you'll see what I mean.
In addition, the characters move at a middling pace. Normally you wouldn't notice movement speed being slow, but there's an awful lot of backtracking required to accomplish every single side quest, and the space between locations will begin to wear down on you. This is especially egregious on the main map, where locations are spaced far apart with little to nothing to do in between them except gather from one or two nodes, and the occasional fight. At higher levels you can skip these fights, which just demonstrates how long it takes to walk between any two locations.
And despite there being a map, there is no indication of where you are on the map, so you can get lost. Normally this would be good, as overwrought UIs are a problem with many modern RPGs, but since the overworld map is a little less Final Fantasy VII and a little more Candyland, it's an exercize in frustration. There is absolutely no reason for the map to exist this way, other than the programmers obviously had a problem with it.
This is a Kickstarter game, and while the visuals do get a lot of polish, there's some serious frame dip and stuttering, especially going to and from combat.
A lot of people have been asking if the game is easy or hard. The game is easy, but it can feel hard due to all the grinding you'll have to do. Normally for me, I'm ok with grinding if I can speed up the process by playing smart. But there aren't very many choices to make from turn to turn in this game. There's an overcharge system, where you can get a discount on spells, or cast spells for "Free" by using the overcharge, but overcharge is raised through combat, and does not persist between combats except for one ability for one character.
I bring this up, again, to point out that many JRPGs can have boring and tedious combat, but oftentimes they're boring and tedious because you're trying to save up MP for the boss fight of a dungeon. Battle Chasers is the same way, but spells all have cast times, and with overcharge being as lucrative as it is, and MP being so low for all characters, the ONE path you would normally take in a JRPG to speed up combat is made actually WORSE in Battle Chasers.
In addition, enemy types are repeated consistently, especially with slimes. And while the designs are great for the characters and many of the monsters, they're also very stale in the mid to late game when Battle Chasers throws the same stock standard undead minions you'll see in Warcraft.
To really hammer in how boring the title is, the music is very poor and mediocre, and that's when the music plays. Most of the time there are no tracks. However, the ending theme is the one standout tune that's interesting to listen to. Otherwise anyone could compose better tracks with Frooty Loops and a month's worth of experience, which I expect is how much experience the two music composers had between them.
Ok, so all that sucks. It's slow and boring and full of bad design. So what's good?
Well, obviously, the art is good, and the character designs are spot on. Even random NPCs get some great touches here and there. The sound effects are also top shelf, whoever did sound design for this title deserves to work at a better studio. The post processing effects are good, with subtle color and special effect cues that make the visuals pop even more. And, wouldn't you know it, the voice acting is surprisingly on point. That said, nothing coming out of the mouths of these characters is particularly pithy or clever, but the voice talents sell their characters well.
Oh, forgot the most important part of a JRPG, the plot. It's generic, sloppy, and uninteresting. The interactions between the party are really the only thing this game has going for it in regards to good writing. The main cast are pretty cynical, apathetic or dickish, but they have a rapport with one another that's very charming. Of course all that goes out the window when Alumon shows up and throws wet dishwater all over what was a fun little game about friends on a cursed island.
That's all I have to say about this game. I hope the designers read this (won't, I know) but I hope they could read it and maybe it would help them see where to focus their efforts in the future? They setup this game to end on a cliffhanger, but before making a Battle Chasers 2, maybe they need to rethink how RPGs are put together first?
As sad as it is to say, there are RPG Maker games better than Nightwar. Let that sink in. A high schooler with minimal knowledge about game design could do just as well or better than what's on display here. All Battle Chasers has is a production budget.

Over 200 hours in and I realized that I haven't written a review yet! Holy cow. Okay, so I've always enjoyed really deep games. I'm not the type that goes for something as simplistic and repetative as Starcraft II. Sure, I'll play through the campaign and even enjoy it, but it's nothing I'll truly get my money's worth out of. Enter any game by Paradox ever. Right off the bat you're overwhelmed by mechanics and they keep adding things on top of that in the form of updates and DLC. This inevitably means there will be bugs, but that's to be expected (looking at you primitive notification spam!) But with the money I've spent on the game and two of the DLC's, it comes out to roughly 35 cents an hour (rounded up). I'd say that's money well spent! And those hours have been enjoyable. My favorite moment in this game, and this is out of many:
- In one of my first games, I'm building up my empire and expanding. I'm the United Nations of Earth, so I'm using my diplomatic skills to ensure all races get along. I'm not expanding my military beyond what I think I would need to defend my few colonies in time for my allies to make short work of the enemy. After all, I'm not a militarist. We need to expand our knowledge through science! What's this? A subspace signal? Interesting. Oh, the Unbidden? Cool looking... you want to feast? Maybe we can negotiate. No? I'm food? What's their military look like? WHAT? One of their fleets is bigger than my navy? Time to build up like crazy! They invade and crush empires that would have made me nervous had they gone to war with me like they were nothing but an annoying fly. The other empires turn a blind eye - they wouldn't dare invade us, so you're on your own. I stand alone. I send in my fleet to intercept and destroy one of theirs'. A small victory! Perhaps a glimpse of hope! Oh. There's four more fleets exactly that size. I retreat, lick my wounds, and pour what little resources I have into bolstering the fleet. I know where their portal is. Crucial intel while hunting for fleets that I could reliably kill to chip away at their military power. But now, knowing reinforcements come through that portal, I have to end this before all hope is lost. I send the fleet on multiple jumps through enemy territory and go straight for the portal. 3/4 health. 1/2 health. All four enemy fleets jump in and start to zero in on my only hope of saving the galaxy. My heart was racing (not being dramatic) and as my fleet engages fleet after fleet, we finally take down the portal. We've cut off their reinforcements. I retreat, and (again, not exaggerating) throw up my hands in excitement. Best gaming moment I've had in years. The underdog wins a desperate battle for all life in the galaxy, and comes out victorious. All I have to do now is go back to my original plan of chipping away at their fleet.
This was back when Stellaris first came out. Now it's more polished, has more features, and more ways things can either go really well or quickly go sideways. Think your empire is doing really well? Think again. This game has surprises in store for you.

Stellaris is a game that can teach you how to be patient. There is a learning curve as with most other strategy games that can be mastered after a few playthroughs in single player. After you get used to it this game is VERY ADDICTING you have been warned!
Some of the things that I can say about this game is:
-Multitasking-
Tons of things to manage:
-Worlds/Sectors (infastructure, populations, governor hiring)
-Diplomacy (Federations, rivals, trading, alliances)
-Technology/Discovery (Hiring Scientists, picking the right technology paths to be ahead of other empires, getting modifiers,building science/research structures, Surveyng)
-Traditions ( more along with choosing empire path)
- Internal Governing (promoting/embracing/supressing factions, hiring empire leaders)
and much other details...
My favorite parts about this game are the roleplaying as the empire you chose which can range from a spiritulist pacifists/monks to WORLD DEVOURING SCOURGE INSECTOID HIVE. I also like the random event chains that can appear which really are interesting and have cool backstories such as the HORIZON SIGNAL.
I did not like the endgame that much because I felt it was introduced into the game a little to late in my single player campaign. I had the unbidden, which are inter-dimensial beings coming to suck the energy out of all living things in our galaxy. When they came they took over a small chunk of the galaxy, but on the other hand I had a federation that included over 50% of the factions ( including a fallen empire). So they were easily defeated. I wish to of have expected the unbidden to wipe out more than half of the empires in the galaxy but they didnt wipe out anyone. Then, after that there is currently nothing to do besides complete all technology or just win the game with domination, federation, or the other thing. Another thing I did not like was how slow it is in the beginning to get started. Just the amount of hours to get certain technologies or find all the other empires felt like a real waste of time in real life.
Overall, great game besides the cons of course and I would recommend to a friend!

Read a lot of comments that accuse this game to be just a clone of World of Warships but thats kind of an insult for this game in my opinion.
Sure there are some similarities like the progression system for example but it does many, many, many things just way better then WoW.
-The Gunplay requires much more aim and skill then it does in WoW
- Balance ! Matchmaker works great so far. Ship classes are 100% mirrored in 9/10 games. In 1/10 games one team has another cruiser instead of a battleship but things like Submarines or Carriers are always 1:1
-SUBMARINES ! They are well implemented. Of course they can dive but they just have a limited time under water since oxygen runs low pretty fast. There are 2 levels: 1st stage they use less oxygen, can fire torpedos themselves but get hit by torps as well. 2nd stage they can't shoot torps and neither get hit by them, only by water bombs (deep cahrges).
Submarine players really have to be patient and carefully. If you meet a Destroyer u're dead.
-Torpedos: NO AIM INDICATOR ! =WIN. Aiming torps needs practice. You have to judge the targets speed, have to split ur torps so that some will hit if target changes speed/direction and you need to get pretty close. Torp shots at ranges over 1km will probably not hit if the target recognises them.
-BUT !: Torpedos have a range minimum. If yo get to close and shoot ur torps they won't detonate.
It's a brilliant idea. Torps do massive damage but also require some skill and sometimes even pure luck to hit.
-CVs. AWESOME ! They are still strong but it's no OP killfarming machine anymore. Minimum Torp Range applies on torp bombers as well so there is a chance to evade if u pay attention. Also aiming your torpedo salvos is a bit harder then in WoW.
-AA. AA works great. CVs can't just roll their bombers into groups of ships and get away with this. AA kills planes pretty fast. Even faster when players decide to control their AA manually ! Even strikes on single ships with good AA have to be quick. Planes can't circle around ships for minutes while looking for the right anlge to place their torps. If they get into AA range they bein to die.
-Rock, Paper, Scissors. The ship classes are very well balanced. Threre is no one OP ship that can kill everything. Lone wolves won't survive long as well. You really have to play with your team. Every ship has a counterpart. For example:
-BBs are very effective against cruisers but can't do anything against a submerged submarine (they can't even see it without sonar)
-Destroyers are very strong against submarines and battleships if they manage to get close enough for torpedos.
-Cruisers are strong against DDs  ....
A lot of people don't seem to understand that by now. See a lot of cruisers and DDs rushing forward alone and get instand killed within seconds. While DDs can still try to dodge, cruisers usally are toast when they rush forward, get detected and bombarded by BBs. Doesn't mean that cruisers are weak or BBs OP, they are often just played wrong.
You really have to wrok together, know your role within the fleet and have to support each other. Basically the best turn-based strategy game there is. Except possibly XCOM. That's no exaggeration, this is easily one of my top five games ever!
As a single-player game, it's better than the other Massive Assault games, but it doesn't have multiplayer. There's a separate game for that.
I'll compare it to two games here:
Advance Wars is a turn-based military strategy game. You build units, you attack with them one at a time, and you try capture cities so that you can build more units.
Hearthstone is a turn-based card game. It's selling point is that every turn is a maths-based puzzle, trying to work out the most effective way to attack.
Massive Assault combines the two. It's a turn-based strategy game with no probabilities and simple figures, so it's possible to work out how a turn will go as soon as you start it. And that's just the START of why it's brilliantly designed!
Oh, and it has undos. Because there's no probabilities or unknowns, you can redo everything up to the start of your turn. Which is excellent!
The big downside is the story and voice acting. The story is just another excuse plot, but at least it's not the main focus, and the voice acting.... oh, it's hilariously bad! Seriously, you haven't lived until you've seen a former soviet try to do an Italian accent!
For the record, at the time it was behind in terms of graphics and sound too. Sound effects, the music is still great. But, like Mischief Makers, now it just looks like a regular old game. Which is good!

Update: 4/22/17 at bottom of review. Original review below:
TL;DR: (6.75/10)
The graphics and presentation are top notch but numerous gameplay problems hold it back
Graphics: Awesome (9/10)
2k has been getting this part right for a while. The players and courts look realistic and move in realistic ways (at least most of the time) The only problem I could point out is that some textures are inexplicably blurry despite being in a high resolution. This is easily countered by using something like ReShade to boost the sharpness, but it's worth pointing out.
Presentation: Awesome (9/10)
Any 2k fan worth their salt will tell you that this series has perhaps the best presentation of any sports game series. The commentary is organic and lifelike and the presentation is top notch. The attention to detail really shows! However, like graphics, there is one small problem worth pointing out: There's so much presentation that you have to mash the "A" button after just about every basket and especially before the game/after the game/between quarters to skip all of the flashy presentation just to get back to the gameplay with no way to turn it off.
Game modes: Awesome (9/10)
Ok, I admit, I've given the game a lot of credit with three straight 9 of 10's. The thing is that these three things are the things that 2k does better than ANYONE ELSE IN SPORTS GAMING. In fact, they've been the best since at least 2k11. There are so many game modes and each one of them is very well fleshed out. Only a handful of changes would make them better, and they're pretty much irrelevant.
Customization: Good (7/10)
2k is better than most when it comes to customization, but there is so much room for improvement here that if you're looking for a fully customizable experience, you won't feel disappointed, but there are other games that do just as good or better. One thing to note is the team relocation mechanic that allows you to fully customize the NBA and even add up to 6 teams to the assosiation in a variety of game modes. The problem for people who love to customize (Like myself) is that this option is ONLY available in certain modes and is not normally available through the main customization tools like player creation and roster editing. This is a major disappointment, and really needs to be remedied in 2k18 (or even patched into this game)!
Gameplay: Passable (5/10)
Here it is, the one thing 2k17 struggles with heavily! Unfortunately, this is the single most important part of the game for 99% of people! Here's a list of just some of the most glaring issues. (Many of these carry over from 2k15/2k16)
-The game is slower than real life, players jog around the court and take floaty shots (set gamespeed to around 55-60 to fix this easily)
-Animations are sluggish, this is especially the case with dribble moves as they are useless most of the time
-It's entirely too easy to get drawn into animations, just run into the back of a player on a fast break to force them to slow down and let you get beside them or even pass them up while rarely drawing a foul in the process
-The AI is all-knowing, making plays with its back turned on a regular basis and simply stands around rather than rotating on defense or getting open on offense
-Layups are too easy to make meaning running toward the rim and spamming them is usually a winning strategy even on higher difficulties
-Fouls are too easy to rack up as they get called too often
-And-ones go in on a regular basis rather than making fouls mean something
-Speed is non-existant in this game as players like Shaq can keep up with Allen Iverson in most situations
-"FAST BREAK, WHAT FAST BREAK? PLAYERS DON'T HAVE UNCONTESTED FASTBREAKS!" says the game. In 200+ hours I've had 1, YES 1, uncontested fastbreak despite telling players to run in transition
-Invisible walls on the edge of the court put on extra "Player Repellant" this year, meaning that you can sometimes run head first out of bounds and get knocked back in by nothing to keep you in play
-The mid range shot is useless in this game, open or not. Unless you're Michael Jordan.
-Dunking in traffic is nearly impossible, leading to easy blocks on most of them even if you go up with two hands. Unless you're Michael Jordan.
-Most of all, the game often considers "well contested" shots that would normally be open rendering stepback J's and shooting from screens pointless.
If there are so many gameplay problems, then why recommend the game? Because most of the issues can be fixed by creating your own sliders for the game. After tweaking the settings, I would say that it gets closer to a 7.5/10 or so. If you don't want to make your own, then you can always download someone else's sliders, even mine if you want. The thing is that even my sliders aren't perfect and are constantly being updated for realism/balance/fun.
Update: 4/22/17
The latest gameplay patch: 1.12 just dropped a few days ago and I decided to go back to defaults to see if it is better. It is.
The points below only apply to the Gameplay portion of the review and to nothing else.
-Dribble moves are no longer useless, but body-up sensitivity is still way too high by default.
-3pt shooting is no longer OP, but they nerfed it too hard. It's impossible to hit 40% with Steph without tweaks to sliders.
-Mid range still garbage.
-Players no longer lube up their hands before every game, but still lose the ball too often.
-Layups and inside shots haven't been touched at all, still way too good. (Set sliders to 40-ish)
-Shots still contested from 5+ feet away.
All in all, this update changed the game from a balance of high scoring Inside/Outside ball, to Isolation/Post up/Get to the rim ball. Just foul out the other team's center by driving inside all game and hitting around 50% of fouled shots to get your three pointers the old fashioned way.

As most of you reading this will know, NBA 2K17 is the best basketball simulation game right now. However, the reason behind this fact is that it's the only game out there and the lack of competition is hurting this game tremondously. As there is no longer any needs to make sure that its gamers would not switch to other series like NBA live, the game continues to evolve further and further away from gaming entertainment and its community.
Overall the gameplay is an overhaul from the previous installment of NBA 2K16 as the player movement is becoming more and more robust, however specific algorithms of the game is getting less and less accurate in terms of simulating a real world experience. For example, contested shots are basically impossible to make in this game, meaning that the Kyrie shots over defenders are entirely impossible to simulate in this game and the difference between players are getting less and less significant and there are very few things a bench player could not do that a star player can. In fact some of the most lethal players in this game are rather low rated, but due to various reasons they are able to do the things done by all-stars to a respectable level. That itself is a little concerning as the realism of the game is not quite established.
The biggest problem with this game, however, is an extremely fatal one. In this year's game, playing online -- something that is possible ever since the original 2k on DreamCast -- is basically impossible. On the steam platform, it is basically impossible to play a game online at an acceptable level of satisfaction. Not only is the server extremely unreliable, causing endless crashes that will destroy a team's promotion and records, the players on the servers are mostly unacceptable to play with. While I am sure that there exist honest, respectable players, they are overwhelmingly out numbered by cheaters, hackers and ones who exploit the system of the game. From off-balling in a my-team match to spamming steal due to the same foul-out rule in half of an actual game's time, the game itself encourages players to play irresponsibly (e.x. a player gets fouled out in an 48 minute nba game if he commits 6 fouls, or 1 foul per 8 minutes; where as an online game is only 20 minutes long and 6 fouls translate into 1 foul per 3 minutes). Much worse, hackers are able to cause their opponents to lose by crashing the latter's game app to force a loss, and cheaters are able to alter the auction house rules by bidding at less than 110% of the previous bids. With all evidence in mind, this is to say that the company has utilized their resources (mostly the purchase of gamers) into advertising campaigns instead of actually making the game more playable. This could be explained (no competition, again) but is definitely not justified. Also, this probably explains why quality players are lacking in this game, likely due to that they have given up wasting time online.
Overall, the gaming experience is pleasing when offline, and disgusting when played online. For those who own nba 2k16,  the need of an upgrade is minimal, meanwhile, it is still a relatively good game if one can keep away from playing online.

I have been playing this game well before it was put on Steam. I'm actually really happy its on Steam now since I lost my old CD keys, this game is quite a gem. This Total War game is the one I compare every Total War game to and none of them ever come close to this one in terms of fun and replayability.
The seige battles for both attack and defence in this game feel genuinely better than the ones in future installments. They are satisfying to play, whether you are taking down the walls with catapults/cannons, storming a citadel with seige equipment like rams and ladders, or just defending against invading forces storming your city.
The units in this game matter, but its how you use them that makes for the most interesting battles. Clearly when the professional (late game) units go up against peasants and such, especially in an open field, we know who is ultimately going to lose (in most cases), but with right combination of units, including peasants, and the right kind of placement, you can easily defending a settlement against even the most advanced/elite units. This also depends on difficulty too as the AI can be vicious if given the chance.
I aslo enjoyed the religion system in this game, but mainly for the catholic factions. The Papal states are not a minor faction and they will wreck you with not only their own units (which are pretty powerful) but all of Christendom will come together to crusade your face in should you get excommunicated or if the pope doesn't favor your faction nearly as much as the others (meaning he'll look the other way for a bit). For what it is, it is a complex, but straightforward system that can either be used to your advantage or used against you.
The modding community for this game is pretty awesome too. Hyrule: Total War and Stainless Steel are both mods I love and they work so well with this game that it gives me endless hours of entertainment even to this day. The game still has a rather active modding community for something of its age, which is great since it just makes a great game even better.
Finally, the game is just all around fun. How you play this game can easily make for a great time or just a great way to waste time in general all the while being entertained. I wish Sega and the Total War series in general looked back to this game and Rome: Total War (the first one) to see what they got so right about their game series and just put that + whatever improvements and mechanics (like naval battles) into the game. If they were to make a modern day version of this game with everything that made this game great, I would buy it in a heartbeat. But in the meantime, there is this game, so if you are looking to pick it up, do so and enjoy!

If you've played WoW: This is WoW on steroids (in the good sense).
If not, or you just have a thirst for reading:
Wildstar packs a hell of a great gameplay with fast-paced action, a customizable actionset that encourages experimentation, great PVE and PVP mechanics and some nice features that, while many of them are not entirely new, but their execution is so good that they bring some really nice feel to the game.
One of these that I really want to point it (because I freaking love it) is the housing system:
You get an instanced housing plot (to make it "lore friendly", they say it's a floating plot in the sky), that has some space for stock stuff like your house in the middle, and other interesting stuff you can collect in the game and build there. Beside that, you get plenty (really, a lot) of space where you can just build whatever you want.
We've built a 3 storey house with my girlfriend which we are furnishing for a while now and we just love it.
One other thing that is well worth the mention is how the in-game transactions work: if you have any thought that it's a pay-to-win game, forget it. You have access to all basic features from the start, and you can buy the rest with an in-game currency called omni-bits, that you get simply by playing. This covers stuff like more capacity to post auctions, more character slots etc.
You can buy all these with real-life money, of course, but nothing that really gives you an edge in combat over other players.
If you decide to spend real money, the game also gives you some permanent stuff that you'd have to unlock by omni-bits (like the ability to create guilds opens up permanently by just 1 time of signature payment, alongside with a lot of other stuff).
Download it, give it a shot, you really don't have anything to loose
P.S.: The overall rating of the game looks underwhelming at first, but if you look at it, most of it is just technical stuff, where people couldn't get it working on their microwave oven, or a switched off monitor. Some technical issues are sure to exist, afterall it's a vast game, but speaking for myself, I haven't encountered any (beside some minor addon bugs, which are solved by a simple command that reloads the UI), so it can't be that bad.

The first audience group this game missed is the group that likes games to be difficult. If you go to the discussions for this game, you can read post after post where people complain the game is too easy.
The second audience group this game missed is the group that does not like to be sweating bullets when they play video games. Since I am a part of that group, I will explain why people rage-quit this game.
But first, here are some pros and cons for the game.
+ The art direction for this game is very good.
+ The music is above average.
+ The voice acting is above average.
+ Randomly-generated dungeons is a nice touch.
+ Fast-travel! Blinkstones transport you to places you have been on the map.
+ Red Monika. I would be remiss if I didn't mention the sexy rogue as a hearty boon to the game's cast of heroes.
+ Having the ability to exit a dungeon, rest, and come back to the dungeon before the enemies respawn is a must-have for this game.
- This game needs to go a LONG ways towards telling players how to play the game.
- The game lacks story depth.
- As I mentioned, I don't know what audience the difficulty of the game targets.
- The game's economy is something I could never figure out.
- Why put level requirements on weapons and armor in this game? It makes no sense to me.
- The perks system is unlike anything I have seen in video games. That wouldn't be a negative thing if I could understand how any of the perks actually help any of the heroes.
- Many people have complained about the long battle animations and tedious loot rewards screen.
Note: The game maker has recently added a patch to punish people who skip the loot rewards screen. Clearly, the game maker has not been reading the discussion posts, for that recent addition is something no gamer wants.
When you get to level 10, the game difficulty spikes. That is when many people head to the forums to see what they are doing wrong. I have read the posts that tell players to start repeating dungeons. That is what I did. But when it came time to repeat Junktown, I found my team getting wiped and wiped and wiped. My team members are the same level as those I am fighting. I shouldn't be getting wiped.
This is what I am encountering in Junktown:
1) One enemy group has two healers and one damage dealer. The healers can heal 50-70 percent of the WHOLE TEAM'S HP in one spell. Compare that to my team heal spell that heals 20 percent of the team's HP.
2) Another enemy can one-shot two of my three team members. Meanwhile, he takes a ridiculous amount of the top damage-dealing spells from my team before he falls (if I can actually beat him).
3) I can't buy or make revive potions. I can't make any health potion that heals more than 15 percent of the average member of my team. I can buy two "moderate" health potions that heal 30 percent of the average member of my team between every time I clear a dungeon. That is nowhere near enough. I can't make ANY mana potions, and I even invested in the curio shop in order to be able to buy more recipes.
4) I have maxed out investments at the smithy, but all the high-end armor I can't equip because I am not high enough level.
5) There was a quest to go down and fight slimes under the tavern in Harm's Way. Normal slime mobs were a bit tough, but nothing out of the ordinary. The boss, however, is WAY over the head of my team. I had no way of knowing that before I went into the dungeon. Furthermore, the option of fleeing was not an option for the fight. So what happened? My team wiped, and I lost 300 gold. That is incredibly frustrating.
How can an average gamer read the above list of experiences and NOT be hugely frustrated? I just don't understand that.

In short: this game is a blast. The visuals are stunning, the voice acting is great, the music is awesome, and the gameplay... oh, the gameplay. Battle Chasers' combat system is the best I've encountered in recent turn-based RPG's. Fast, strategic, fun. The crafting system is as deep as it is original.
Of course it has its drawbacks. You're going to need a good amount of grinding, since the characters you don't carry in your party don't level up, so you'll find yourself revisiting dungeons in order to have them at the same level of your usual party. The overworld map consists of predefined paths, which is a letdown at first until you realize there's more possible routes and hidden corners than such system may suggest.
Battle Chasers is an indie game, but unlike most indie games, it has tons of content, great visuals and, most importantly, an awesome gameplay.
Buy it if you're into classic JRPG's but don't mind a modern twist.

I, like many others, probably looked at the characters of Nier: Automata and thought that it was a game for pervy weebs and I would have no interest in it. However exposure on ♥♥♥♥♥ and Reddit and rave reviews from friends got me to bite the bullet and try it.
This game almost immediately become one of my favorite games. It has a plot that is like the animes you watched late at night growing up, with some of the most badass hacking and slashing combat with shooting mixed in as well. You are drawn in not only because you want to learn more about these mysterious, evolving machines attempting to mimic human cultues, but also because you NEED to see what happens next to these poor psycholigically damaged protagonists.
These poor androids, locked in centuries of combat, forbidden to love, dying only to be resurrected to fight more. They are programmed to serve human masters they have never seen and crave human attention and affection they may never receive. This game quickly hits you right in the feel bads and you no longer care about the wacky outfits the androids wear. You realize it's symbolic. They are blindfolded because they follow orders without question. They are dressed and designed to seem pure but are quickly dirtied and corrupted by the end and are utterly changed by the game events.
Nier: Automata is a mix of Zelda, Final Fantasy, Metal Gear Solid, The Matrix, and Wall:E thrown into a blender and the end result is one of the most fantastic games I have ever played.

After a few hours of gameplay and a first season of the career almost completed, it is time to drafta review for MXGP2. I'll start with the graphics: motorbikes and pilots are well reproduced, the motorbikes in particular look very detailed and gorgeous when covered with mud. the tracks are well designed, whereas the crowd and the details on the side don't look very convincing. The overall impression is that itmay not be the most advanced game in therms of graphics, but it's still pleasant to look at and it is stable and fluid. The sound effects are ok, I don't have experience with this kind of motorbikes so I don't really know how accurate their sound reproduction is.
The gameplay is a bit arcadey, and is fun: touching with others is not to punishing and they don't seem stupid. With a bit of practice you'll soon start to take the difficulty level and physics level up for a more challenging experience. I find ridiculous, even if it is really not a big issue, that you can change direction while flying after a jump, like super mario.
The game offers a good variety of game modes, ensuring thus a lasting experience. I am still doing the first part of the career, which is fine, I hope that at any point something spectacular will come out, like for example the 24h of Le Mans in GRID, to provide a climax of some sort.
In conclusion, I think MXGP2 might not be super impressive at first but is a good game with lots of fun for many hours.

The customization in this game is very detailed, whether it be the riders equipment or the everything about the bike. I love how they setup the career mode, how you can create your own team and make everything look the way you want, or you can join a real team. Pretty solid F2P MMO, but some of the downs are really gamebreaker (for me anyway) 05/10.
Ups:
+ Fluid combat system with a lot of movements and telegraphs
+ Uses classic "Holy Trinity" (Tank, DPS and Healer) system, but since several classes can do tank, several others can heal, and all can DPS, there is alot of combinations possible
+ All classes feel unique, beeing the skills, the resourse system or the telegraphs itself, and thats for all roles
+ Interesting "Path" missions and skills available. There is 4 to choose from.
+ Very good LAR (limited action bar) build style, with a lot of skills to choose from and upgrade, as well as a lot of "talents" choices that gives anything from stat bonuses to unique perks or unique skills
+ Has alot of good features like action house, bank, mail, in-game store (which you can buy the majority of stuff with in game currency if you are patient enough), pvp and a few styles of pve instanced content (dugeons, adventures and expeditions)
+ The "premium status" and microtransactions in general that you get with real money are pretty fair. There is not a "pay to win" spirit built in the game as a general rule.
Now the downs:
- *Absurdly long PVP queue's (I had the chance to play 0 matches so far, nada...)
- *Absurdly long Dugeon queue's (I had the chance to play about 3 dugeons so far, they are great but it doesnt nearly make up for the queue time....)
- *Absurdly long Adventure queue's (I had the chance to play 0 of them so far, nada too....)
- Decent (at most) queue's for Expeditions (This one I have played quite a bit, and you have an option to just go solo for it, but I personaly rather with a group, cause MMO.....and that takes a good time to pop up)
- (note for the first 3 itens above with a * mark - that means that every single time I enter the game the first thing I do is to queue up on PVP, Dugeons and Adventures. That means that at the time of writing I have around 50h of Queue on all of those. Look on the number of times I got a chance to play each and judge yourself)
- Altho Dugeons have a really neat feature to scale your caracter level to the correct level of the dugeon, for some reason it doesnt happen for expeditions. If you add that to the fact that the "Random Expedition" option to get you bonus gold and bonus xp select all the expeditions (even the ones completely irreletant to you since you overleved it absurdly), it means that if you use the randon button you will play 95% of the time on the very first expedition with mobs so low that they die with 1 swing, and in the end you get some gold and a tiny of xp (from the bonus itself). If you only want to play relevant content, you must choose spefics expeditions, making you queue times go sky high and your rewards go down (in a way, since you lose bonus)
- One of the worst optimizations I have seen (the games even runs smooth'ish, but it leeches way more hardware juice than it should need, comparing to several other MMO's, or even newer games)
- Leveling up feels too slow and too grindy after mid levels, again comparing to other MMO's. The way leveling is passed it fails to give any sense of satisfaction IMO. It would be vastly better if the dugeons queue's were consistant. Or existant for that matter.
- Altho the game has more than average VA, which is neat, the story itself (as in the quality and depth) is.... well, how to say it politely... not good. Overall its boring and hollow (even most cutscenes) There is a lot of "hidden lore" to discovery and read, but even those are dull. The presentation as a whole of the story, characters and world stories, are below avarage.
- Altho the game has several neat features as already said (for instance, filtering a AH search with some options like item level) it also lacks some really basic ones along the way (like for instance the option to filter the AH search with level required to use itens)
So, overall the game has solid good points, but it also has some godly negative ones, thefore downvote for me.
But in the end of the day its a F2P game. If you looking for a MMO it wont cost you to try it.

If WoW & Borderlands ever had a baby; it would be Wildstar. It has somewhat the same gameplay as WoW, as when I first played this game, I honestly thought I launched WoW instead because of the GUI. It has also a really has a sense of uniqueness with the graphics, because it somewhat looks like Borderlands graphics which is really cool, and the first MMO game to ever do graphics like this.
This game indeed is not P2W, I don't understand why many people are claiming it to be, because the only in-game items you buy are just cosmetic items & mounts. You can get to a high level really quickly & be as strong as a casher if you have the patience to keep grinding & farming. Most mobs in the game do not agro on first sight, unless you hit them, thus you can actually get past a few main missions without having to engage in combat, but if you ever want to quickly level up like me; then you will be pretty much stuck at one area farming for the XP to level up because completing mission does not give you a lot of XP nor does completing task too. With that said, this game also has quite a number of bugs, as claimed by many players, but only a few surfaced for me as of now. This game has a really awkward movement mechanic, where sometimes you are able to use the mouse the rotate, and at times it just messes up, and you can only use A & D to look around, while your mouse just goes crazy. One more thing that annoys me is the often prompting to do micro-transaction; for example, they have missions where you are suppose to buy from their in-game store, yes it's an optional mission, but it came out a few times for me and when you need to confirm your IP Address, they will redirect you to a micro-transaction page, which shows you the prices of the in-game currencies. Honesly, in my opinion they should not have done that, micro-transaction should be added because they want players who are willing to pay to further customise  their character, and not as a desperate measure, and even make a couple of missions out of it.
Overall, the gameplay mechanics can still be improved, but it is a similar game to WoW; but you hardly see players around, maybe my level is too low, and no one is at my level anymore but it is indeed a must have game if you guys are fans of WoW  but do not have the money to continue paying for it. I'm rating it 6/10

I had never heard of this game until it showed up in my Queue.
I'm giving it a thumbs up, but the game is not without problems. Overall i'd rate it about 60-70%, if some of the issues are fixed that could get much higher. The game is still quite early but it looks promising.
Let's start with the good:
PRO:
Nice variety of ships off the bat. Adding submarines gives destroyers a very defined role besides scouting. I've yet to play carriers but i've been told they're quite fun, and allow custom deck set-ups.
Very good shooting mechanic - this is akin to the way artillery works in World of Tanks, if you move it resets. Making gunnery challenging and intense.
Ability to manually control secondaries - you can manually jump on those secondaries, including AA! This makes Carrier captains much less scary if you're actually paying attention. However if you don't spot those planes fast enough, you'll pay for it!
Submarines! - I know this is something people have wanted for a long time, and I think this is implemented well here. WoWs for whatever reason could never figure out the gameplay balance. I think Steel Ocean does a nice job of making submarines challenging and fun, while still definitely serving a role in the game.
CON:
Graphics - while not terrible, they are definitely dated. The models seem to be very low-poly count/detail with some pretty bad textures at times.
UI - At first glass it seems to be a direct rip from WoWs, however some things are missing. Like ability to preview your ships before you buy them. It just feels clunky overall.
Mixed Server - All regions play on the same server. While making match making better it makes communication almost impossible. You will have people from Korea/Japan/Germany/USA etc etc all on the same team. It's very frustrating.
All in all I think the game has a good start and the gameplay is fun, however for me personally graphics/UI/and server situation really holds the game back. I'm hoping they fix this in the future as the game has some promising tidbits of gameplay.

Had a surprising amount of fun with this game the short time I've played it. Highly recommended for anyone wanting some WWII naval combat action. The graphics aren't particularly pretty, but the gameplay is fantastic.
I feel the UI for managing your ships' officers could use a bit of work though, but aside from that, all of the other issues I've had with the game have been niggling at worst.
There's a huge amount of ships to choose from, and judging from the patch notes, they're continuing to add more. Furthermore, all of the ships seem to be relatively balanced in the sense that DDs don't feel inferior or superior to BBs since they serve a different tactical function. Also, in combat with each other, torpedoes hurt...  a lot.
Although I haven't played much, the matchmaking system seems really good. As opposed to players being divided purely by ELO, they're divided by ship classes. So, both sides will have the same number of DDs, SSs, CVs, etc... which makes a HUGE difference given that every ship class has its own inherent strengths and weaknesses (you will never have the horrible fate of a full team of SSs vs BBs/CVs).
All in all I'm glad I found out about this game and am looking forward to seeing it get updated.
EDIT: Can't tell if the community is just dead or if the matchmaking is just wonky lately, but there seems to be some odd matchmaking setups i.e. 3 SS + 1 CV, 4BB, 1CL + 2SS. As a result, the game isn't quite as fun as it could be. Honestly I wouldn't mind being placed against ships of a much higher tier at this point if it means more ship diversity (especially considering the timeline of WW2, such engagements did happen). I'd prefer both tier and ship class to be taken into account with matchmaking if they do that though. So, for example, not only are there 3 DDs, 1 CA, 1CV, 2BB on each side, but also 1 Tier 2, 3 Tier 3s, 2 Tier 4s, and 1 Tier 5

SLRR is a little unstable, and it does crash quite often, but the gameplay itself is unbeatable. As a racing/mechanic sim, it is extremely detailed and given its low price, I would say it's definitely worth the buy. If you are someone who enjoys good gameplay and doesn't mind outdated graphics and the prevalence of bugs/crashes, I would strongly recommend this game for you. If you are someone who prefers modern graphics, and is intolerant of glitchy games that crash, I would not recommend it.
To summarise the pros and cons of SLRR :
Pros:
Great gameplay and vehicular handling (handling is affected by weight of parts/car)
Good variety of tracks/ races
Epic vehicular customisation (both cosmetic and mechanical)
Ability to remove, repair, and respray individual panels of vehicles
A large number of vehicles available.
Challenging AI (especially in Race of Champions)
Cons:
Can be buggy on occasion
Crashes quite often (ensure you save your game regularly)
In-race penalty system can be buggy. (e.g. being given penalties due to interference by AI's)
Main Menu UI can be a little buggy sometimes.
All in all, for the price of $6.00, I think this game is well worth it, despite the presence of bugs and crashes.

What could be an incredibly awesome gaming experience ruined by a developer that cares more about money then developing a masterpiece -- which this game could come so close to being.
