I like CK2 a lot - This is not CK2 in space.
I like 4X games - this hits the spot.
I love turn based strategy games - This is real time strategy which I don't like, however it feel's like they've just streamlined turn based so you dont have to keep pressing enter. They've done it well (To be honest they just used the same system that works on CK2, but its not CK2 in space - I promise).
The inevitable Moo2 comparison :
I have played & mostly enjoyed many turn based 4X space games. Most just made me nostalgic for Moo2. Some intoduced good stuff. Some re-hashed stuff already done. Moo3 just had all the enjoyment of doing a tax return with a migraine. This game doesn't play like any of them. It's not a Moo2 clone in any way other than being 4X & set in space. I love Moo2, but after far too long I have now moved on. This game has filled the space I had in my heart for Moo2. It has succeeded it & improved on it.
Now about the game :
It is very complex but enjoyable from the start - expect to restart quite a bit at first though simply becaus as you learn whats what you learn what you've done & why it's wrong. Or just play it out for as long as you can.
There is a lot of customization options to begin with - species - culture - politics - preferences - (probably more I dont remember) each choice you make will potentially open further choices, possible end game victory options or even end game disasters! Additionally there are plenty of options for the galaxy you play in.
With the real time gameplay you can speed it up, slow it down or just pause it after every day if you insist it has to be played turn by turn (I did this for a while - change is scary). Eventually you get a feel for how the game is progressing & it just becomes natural.
The tech progress is nothing too radical but has been done well & seems balanced. There are three main tech progression paths that have seperate research points allocated to them, and each is slightly randomised so each game will play different.
The ship design is interesting & allows a lot of variation while keeping it as simple/streamlined as possible. You start off only building small ships, then cus of tech you get bigger ones, also cus of tech you need to keep them upto date with better weapons etc. Nothing new there, but because of the various restrictions fleets work better with diversity (as in more than one design filled with the best gun you got), and even the original small ship remains useful by being repurposed once certain tech is available - obsolete gunship to torpedo boat for example - You could design a fleet of ships that successfully destroys your one neighbours fleet with ease only to find out it may have a few too many vulnerabilities when faced with your other neighbour. And that's assuming a similar level of tech.
The diplomacy works well & covers a lot of options. In addition to this the information on display shows why you are doing good/bad with a particular race. From your original customization options its possible you have just selected the exact oposite choices so you guys will not get along & war is inevitable, or you've just found your long lost twin and friendship is instant, also everything inbetween. Interestingly how you deal with each race, and all the other races, and even your own people is over time taken into account by all the other races.
Exploration is interesting & is covered below.
***The above is just the standard info that compares to other space based 4X games - now for what makes Stellaris different***
You aren't the ruler of a race who started on one planet and reach into the galaxy to claim his/her destiny through conquest/ascension/genocide/glory/oblivion/galactic-appocalypse. Your just not.
In this game you design the original planetary leader, but only that one and only because one is needed to begin with.
Have you ever read a book or seen a TV show where you thought : I'd do something different, I wonder how that would have turned out. Well this is your chance. This is a fully interactive story that is different every time you go through it. That's what makes this special. Every time you explore somewhere it's exciting - a hundred hours I've played so far & I still love exploring. I'm still encountering new stuff. Even stuff I've encountered in previous games is exciting because I can take those other options.
This is the story of the race you chose - the story of their leader's, hero's, war's, friendship's, glory & folly. The story of a race that reaches from one world into the stars & the galaxy is a very dangerous but interesting place.
Also if yor not bored yet:
Like CK2 Stellaris is made by Paradox - this means it is being updated constantly & new expansion DLC is guaranteed. So the game is getting bigger & better & optionally more expensive. I'm not sure how I feel about that cus most of my CK2 DLC was purchased while drunk, but it was on offer & I really wanted it.
Also since I decided I needed the 1st DLC for this I can now play as an imortal(but not un-killable) galactic hive mind. So, playing as a single entity spread accross worlds & star systems I guess I could say it was my story, but I prefer other races & single these abominations out for extermination!!
Oh yeh - there's multiplayer - doesn't interest me.

This game is fun, really fun actually. Paradox has made a great game and I think it is, gameplay wise, worth the money. But not right now. Not in the current update 1.5.1. And this is for one reason. Bugs. They ruin this game and your experience of it. As an example:
Was playing an ironman mode game (You can not use backup saves to save yourself from mistakes, whatever you do happens and can not be unturned.) and having great fun. I was dominating about 20% of the galaxy and had great plans on the rest. I think I had invested about twenty-ish hours or so in to this campaign and was ready to clean up some borders by defeating a minor empire.
I declare war and start by laying siege to one of their planets. It gets to the end of conquering and all of a sudden I get a popup. The end-game screen telling me I won. Which is odd as I was no where near winning. And behind the popup I see my fleet explode which is even more odd. So I exit planet view and see that my entire empire has vanished by only traces of my existance left. I am basically booted from the session.
This is one of the bugs Paradox hoped to fix in the current patch but low and behold it still exists and as I was not aware this could happen and my game saved and is now corrupted like this. I loved the game with its story and all but this broke my heart and I will probably revisit it later, for now though I'm sticking with other games.
And this bug has happened for many people not just me, sadly it has not been fixed and through some googling I found out that conquering a planet is what causes this, if you do find yourself in the situation, exit the game through Ctrl + Alt + Del, reboot the game, then delete the army that is conquering the planet or stop conquering. That worked for someone.

This game is awesome - until you realize that the AI is abysmal and is insanely bad at doing anything.
It's as if you are playing soccer, and you're like "Man I'm doing great yo", but you look over the shoulder and realize that the rest of the players have no legs or arms and are kinda just smiling and waving their arm stumps at you.
Summed up, the AI works as following:
If player fleet power is lower than mine > Be hostile and actively harass player and attack their territory
If player fleet power is higher than mine > Do nothing - Ever
The AI never uses any kind of strategy either, it will create a stack (of ships), and as soon as war is declared they will send their stack of ships against yours, and whoever wins the battle has won the entire war. That's it.
Like, they wont regroup or recover, because past that point all they will do is continuously build single ships and send them on suicide missions against your fleet.
The AI will never collaborate with other AI either, they don't do joint attacks, and rarely if ever unite against a threat, even if that threat is you, and you are a xenophobic fanatic purifier that is actively genociding the galaxy one empire at a time.
The AI is also incompetent at managing resources and researching, and you'll often find planets that are say, exclusively food producers. Like, several planets, dozens and dozens of planets, that produce nothing but food.
I think you can see where this is going considering that you get severe tech research penalties the more population and planets you have.
I also never once saw them build megastructures of any kind, or really even get Jump Drives or anything either.
Diplomacy is also fantastic, in the sense that it isn't, at all.
In fact don't even bother playing Pacifist or Fanatic Pacifist, unless you are a complete masochist or want a game that lasts for half an eternity, because your options boil down to:
a) Aggressively do Liberation Wars and also be so powerful that friendly empires will just straight up surrender to you and ask to become your Vassals.
b) Build a Federation and cry yourself to sleep whenever a singular Fallen Empire decides to declare war on one of your allies and promptly goes on to murder all 13 of you because one of them glanced in the same general direction the FE was at.
c) Do literally nothing and wait for the Unbidden to show up and absolutely trash everyone else. Then trash the Unbidden.
You get, three flavors of AI aggressiveness and three flavors of AI difficulty.
Low to High aggression: Pretty much all the same, only changes how likely they are to declare war on you in general.
Difficulty levels: Does absolutely nothing for the AI ITSELF, but rather determines how many cheats they get enabled.
So on Normal they are on equal levels with you, no cheats.
Hard = Get 50% more energy, minerals and research, and can also build 50% larger fleets.
Insane = Same as above, but 100% instead.
None of that even means anything because the AI is incapable of taking care of itself, and once you've passed the magical threshold of "player has more fleet power than AI", you have basically won over the AI.
There is so much more to talk about too, like how completely meaningless and poorly implemented the whole planetary invasion/land warfare mechanic and ALL of its related research/buildings, etc is, or how the multiplayer seemingly doesn't work for random people, but why even bother really?
The game has it's moments, like the events, which have interesting little stories to them and whatnot, there's also mods if you wanna roleplay I guess, and it's pretty fun for your first few starts while everything still feels new and cool.
Get it on sale, if you can look past the genuinely awful AI.

Poured quite a lot into this game. Within 200+ hours I have completed (that is, won or lost) game 3-4 times. Stellaris is a gem in grand strategy games, which I adore a lot. I could not comment on the game without the DLC's, as I have bought every single one of them upon release, there are numerous useful and interesting mechanics which are not offered in the base game.
One of the things I like the most about Stellaris is the modding support. I have roughly 140 mods, 90% of which are cosmetic improvements such as planet variety. I also use a couple of mods for balancing purposes and fixes of clunky AI.
Therefore, it's rather difficult to write a review about a product which was modded so heavily from my side, and, I believe, other players have different experience of Stellaris based on the mods they used.
As far as base game is concerned, I love it's combat system, ability to construct your own empire the way you see fit. At the moment I have a Swarm: a devouring empire which conquers others just to have a delicious meal of some moluscoid race, which is then served with some plantoids. ;]
One of the charming elements of Stellaris is its unpredictability of outcome. For instance, I was conquered by one neighbouring empires and became their vassal. Naturally I was considering to start a new game; however, I've decided to see if it's possible to rise from ashes. In 20 years (game time) I have built a strong enough fleet to declare war on my masters and completely crushed them, ceding their planets as mine; and so did the servant become the master.
I do like the game, and I think it is worth the price. ;)

- The sound: It's horrible. Nothing more to add. The engine sound sounds more like some random noise. No real rev limiter. Just completely in the wrong direction in this department, I can't even find words for it.
- Tracks are not rough enough: They are always like the first lap of practice, completely perfectly shaped and pretty boring at times. Lommel is the best example, it's 100% smooth and therefore not Lommel. However I can imagine that rough tracks would be quite hard to ride as well with the poor physics.
- No qualification race: Come on Milestone, you could have at least given us the option of having a real weekend with different practices and a qualification race.
- Boot models: please make them a little more detailed and add "height" to them. They look like painted rubber boots.
Buuuuut there are also many good points, like great customisation, good graphics and all the licenses. All in all it's a real fun game and I just listed all negative points that deserve to be worked on for the next game.
I actually recommend the game, even if you're not 100% happy with it. But if you don't buy it, they'll stop making mx games as well and soon we won't have any games besides MX SIM which would be a shame, so support the sport!

First of all, I must say that the game mechanics are great! They feel like the closest to actual racing than any other motocross game I have played. You really do have to plan your lines ahead and make sure you are applying the right braking style around certain corners. I haven't played the first MXGP, but i have played games like MX vs. ATV: Reflex and the movements feel much more realistic and passing people actually feels like an accomplishment. I also find it pretty cool that when you lean, you reallly have to be careful because lean to much and you are in the dirt.
The customization options are an awesome factor as well. I was almost able to perfectly recreate my own Yamaha with American flag graphics! There are so many brands to choose from includ Fox, FMF, and Renthal. The only problem i ran into while customizing my bike was a constant flickering that would appear on the bike, but the developers are already aware through discussions and are probably already fixing it.
My favorite mode so far is the Career mode, where you get to race with the MXGP 2015 Roster. Although i don't really follow those races as I like to watch AMA Supercross in America, I am having a blast making my own character and bringing him up in the ranks.
Graphics-wise the game looks and runs great with my fps staying between 50-60fps on the max settings.  Here are my specs:
i7 4790k
AMD Radeon R9290x 4gb
16gb Ram
The most common complaint that i do find relevent is the sounds of the game. The engine noises are not up to par and can be made more realistic as well as maybe the crashes. However, this problem does not take my enjoyment away from the game and shouldn't be the deciding factor in purchasing the game or not in my opinion.
Overall, the gameplay is stellar but that is not to say that there are things that could be worked on. I definitely recommend this game to fans of the sport or anyone that enjoys realistic racing games.
Cheers!

A game the revitalised rogue-like (or -lite) genre. You go in, you walk around the basement, you explore the rooms, you kill monsters, fight bosses and collect different loot. You fail and start again having nothing from previous run but your own knowledge. Seems simple, but in the end it sucks you into playing and replaying for hours straight.
The key is the amount of content and random generation. The amount of items is so big that at first every single run will feels completely different.  Everything is random too - rooms, monsters, bosses, items. So the more you play, the more you learn about game. The more you learn - the deeper you go. And new challenges await there. And they will kill you and it will trigger the whole learning cycle once again.
The art is quite quirky and controls don't feel right at start but after a while you'll get used to it and enjoy running "just one more time" again and again.
Recommended.
ps: No native gamepad support, so use Xpadder or JoyToKey.

The Withering
CM Softworks
CM Softworks
3D survival horror
I’ll say this right off the bat: The Withering is no State of Decay. Is this a good thing? It’s most certainly reflected in the price tag, which I’d say that it manages to cover the dev team’s expenses and time invested into their first Steam project. The fact that it’s still Early Access, gives me hope that The Withering shall receive its well deserved futher support through several updates. It needs a lot of polishing, but the gameplay mechanics as they are now, present us with a fully functional zombie apocalypse simulator which puts an emphasis on managing a camp of survivors from the onslaught of the undead hordes. And they will come banging on your gates soon enough. There’s never sufficient time to properly prepare but you shall have to manage the base accordingly. From crafting new materials and temporary buildings and all the way to controlling the scavenging missions directly.
It’s Unity Engine in all its shining glory even though the game could use more visual assets and a whole lot of work into the sound department. I get it, it’s the end of times but you have to come up with more sound diversity than a few zombie growls and the wind howling in the distance. I didn’t ask for smooth jazz, just some sad strings or I dunno. The entire silence of the grave trope doesn’t quite fit in, since the dead are rising and want to eat your brains. Overall, I’m looking forward to Withering once it leaves the Early Access state. It’s a budget orientated alternative to some of the honestly overpriced zombie games out there on the Steam Store.
+ Decent story and graphics.
+ Well priced for an Early Access.
- Needs more sounds and gameplay diversity.
- No Steam Trading Cards or Achievements.

text: I love paladins. As good as overwatch if not better. That is if you have a competent team!

My Opinion:
(PLEASE KEEP IN MIND I WILL BE COMPARING THIS TO OVERWATCH)
Okay, So I haven't unlocked all the newer champions, I haven't even downloaded this on my new gaming PC. But I digress, I'm going to try to make this review as honest as possible, "Overwatch and paladins are the same thing right???" And to that I say... NO THESE GAMES ARE NOTHING ALIKE IN A GOOD AND BAD SENSE. Okay so that may of come off strong But its sort-a like comparing TF2 To Overwatch, In a feel-y kinda a way. They feel different and are completely different games, In the same genre. The games look the same, They don't really play alike, They do in the sense that you gotta "Capture the point!" And "Push the payload!" But the reason they don't play alike. Is because the games feel different, Its not like a "Oh boy-o its basically the same thing with different characters" No-No-No. These games feel COMPLETELY DIFFERENT. Sure you got "Emo death guy" And "Tank who can pull you in with a hook..." Huh, It feels like paladins is beginning to sound like Overwatch alot... So about my opinion I think Overwatch is better for a couple reasons, Like. You don't have to pay in-game currency for the heroes, Or ya' know. I mean paladins comes out with new heroes every month. But it seems like they just keep getting bland and bland-er-er? I don't know Maybe its just me. Overwatch's characters feel like real breathing human beings! With emotion that you tase to death as a gorilla. And paladins just feels, Eh.
(EDIT: And I know people are getting annoyed that people are comparing this to overwatch but, I just can't help myself So if you want a quality review, Go look somewhere else I guess.)
The Actual Gameplay:
So in paladins the gameplay is simple, Form a good team and capture and-or defend a point, Easy, Simple, and fun. And where paladins beats Overwatch In some places, Is quantity and sort-a quality, You see Overwatch takes a very long time to make and release heroes, let alone on the Public test region. And I'm not saying Overwatch is not quality, Its just, Paladins has so many more heroes to choose from. So now onto the hero selection (In more detail.) In paladins there are About I dun-no' Twenty? Thirty Heroes? Something like that, Like I said, I haven't played this game for awhile. But with paladins you can't switch your heroes Mid-Game Meaning you better have a healer, Tank, Good chunk of team effort. In Overwatch you can switch heroes on the fly, Meaning. "Oh, They have a Genji! Better switch to Winston to take care of it!" In paladins its like. "Oh they have a Maeve... Better just try to avoid her."
TL:DR
*this is for all you lazy people who don't like to move y'alls' eye balls.*
In retrospect, Paladins is a great game and an amazing thing to go too if you don't have money for Overwatch. I recommend this game to anybody who doesn't like the, "*PEW* *PEW* BLOOD, DEATH! *PEW* *PEW*" Kinda games. Its fun and bright and happy! The heroes are bland-ish, And they come out in a quantity sort-a way. But thats fine Its fun and thats all that matters. I give this game a 6.9 (I couldn't think of a number six was too low and seven was too high I guess.) Its fun to pick up and play with your friends, Go play it! If you don't have money for Overwatch! My experience with this game has been neat-o, And I like it a bit. (NOT AS MUCH AS OVERWATCH THOUGH, HA-HA-HA-HA-HA.)

Amazing game so far.  World of Warships meets Battlestations Pacific.  Well balanced and defined weaknesses and strenghts of each ship type.  Would be better off if the PR department would get off their♥♥♥♥♥and start advertising!
Pros:
-Subs (Done to perfection.  Uses a simple depth system with oxygen bar that prevents perminantly being submerged.  No reason WoWS didn't impliment this.)
-Skill Based Gun and Torp firing system (No target assist)
-Hard Counters and Well Defined Roles (Battleships are the big mean bully of the playground until they run into a Sub, immediately running with their tails between their legs.)
-Manual control of all armarments. (Secondaries/AA/Smoke)
-Spotting system is much more developed and depends on smaller ships and scout planes. (TEAMWORK!)
-"VIP/Premium" Time for the game has a per-day and per-battle function, for those who donot play often.  Also per-day is pausable by purchasing a per-battle VIP and remains paused untill the per-battle is used up. (This is huge for those who play casually!)
-Multiple "Commander" roles for one ship (Captain/Gunner/Helmsmen/Radioman/Engineer) that works on all ships without penalty.
-Awesome Maps that seem more focused on reality and less on MLG "Everything needs to have a tatical purpose or scrap it".
-NIGHT BATTLES!(Fun!)
-Less Inertia-dependant ship controls. (Ships seem more reactive and torpedoes less deadly to skilled drivers)
-Carriers done right. (Planes have fuel.  Planes are weak verses anyone maning their AAA but arn't always visible like in WoWS so they can easily sneak up on people, drop torps, and get out before anyone can shoot them down.)
Cons:
-Severe lack of player base at the moment.  Seriously, Steel Ocean, get out there and advertise!  You could mop the floor with WoWS untill they impliment some of your mechanics!
-Severe lack of higher tier players. (See first con for reasons why)
-Complicated captains system.
-No perk system/customizability for captains.
-Less impressive graphics than World of Warships.
-Night Battles. (Sub hell)
-Less Inertia-dependant ship controls. (Seems slightly unnatural when a Battleship goes from 0 to 10knots in 3 seconds, avoiding your torpedoes)
-The Atlanta's Main DP Armarment isn't considered AAA.
-Fighters seem to play less of a role in this game, assuming you have people paying attention to planes and swapping to AAA to shoot them down.
I'd give it a 8.5/10.
PS: French sub has 205mm cannons.  Thats right, a sub.

My playthrough is still in progress - but I'm at a point where I want to voice my dissatisfaction.
Firstly, I never played a game like this (3rd person brawler) before so this was new. Ultimately I did not really like the mechanics. I was able to learn the basics but it just did not click with me (I think one of my biggest problem was that I could not find a satisfying camera setting that let me focus where I wanted to in combat mode), so I set everything to auto after a while when I finally gave up on the challenge part - after that the game thankfully just pretty much played itself during fights.
I did this because even though one of my reasons for getting the game was to try something from the genre - the bigger draw was the intriguing story/world. Sadly, it didn't do anything for me in this regard either.
All I can see is pointless sentimentalism. I don't much care for metaphores and symbolism and I suspect this game is full of them and I just can't pick up on it.
The setting is that of a kind of generic post apocaliptic open world rpg (desert, forest, overgrown city and abandoned factory) filled with uninteresting samey mooks. I found no meaningful story so far (I did not go through all the endings yet), things just happened in a particular order without much influence on or link to one another. It's fascinating for a while but it got boring - nobody really learned anything or went anywhere. Well, sometimes people died (in uninteresting ways and without much reason). It tried to do the usual tricks to pull my heartstrings - but without my investment in the characters or the world that just did not work on me.
Overall, it's not bad at all, it's just ...meh. I'm happy for all the people who managed to get something out of it but it seems it is not really for me. (I still intend to finish all the 3(?) main endings but I don't know if I can push myself through with my quickly waning interest.)

I dont normally write reviews, in fact this may even be my first. But I feel compelled to after playing Nier: Automata.
This is probably one of the best games I have ever played. I don't say this lightly, I am a harsh critic and it takes a lot to impress me. I dont normally buy games on the first day of release due to the price, but I took a chance on this and I am so glad that I did because it is worth every penny.
The story is engaging and gripping to the point where I was up all night playing it and then had to go to work on 3 hours sleep. Also, I am not an emotional man, in fact I am much like the protagonist :P but there were certain parts that had me sobbing like a baby. Make no mistake, this game has some very dark themes to it which is bound to affect you in one way or another.
The graphics and visuals are amazing, the fights are exciting, the music is epic and really adds to range of emotions you will go through when playing this game.
Sure there are a few things I felt could have been done better, it's not without it's flaws. The overall world that you play in feels a little small once you've explored the whole map, I wish there could have been more zones, more places and people to visit. There were some technical issues when it was first released and the game sometimes crashes on me, I wont lie. The cut scenes are very choppy in terms of frame rate. For some reason it caps the cutscenes at 30fps. During gameplay it goes back to 60fps. I dont know if this will ever get fixed. But all of these things are completely eclipsed by the game's good points that it doesnt bother me. It's not enough to keep me from giving this game a 10/10.

A game the revitalised rogue-like (or -lite) genre. You go in, you walk around the basement, you explore the rooms, you kill monsters, fight bosses and collect different loot. You fail and start again having nothing from previous run but your own knowledge. Seems simple, but in the end it sucks you into playing and replaying for hours straight.
The key is the amount of content and random generation. The amount of items is so big that at first every single run will feels completely different.  Everything is random too - rooms, monsters, bosses, items. So the more you play, the more you learn about game. The more you learn - the deeper you go. And new challenges await there. And they will kill you and it will trigger the whole learning cycle once again.
The art is quite quirky and controls don't feel right at start but after a while you'll get used to it and enjoy running "just one more time" again and again.
Recommended.
ps: No native gamepad support, so use Xpadder or JoyToKey.

The game is a love letter to all JRPG fans with its 3 men-cell teams and turn-based combat. The character designs are memorable and the whole world oozes of the Darksiders games visual style. There are a lot of enemy types despite the absence of a few fantasy rpg cliches. The soundtrack is OK for the most part, the only one I especially liked is the theme song. Weapons and the skills are awesome to witness and have some light tactical layers to it, though I really would have appreciated it if the look of armors I put on my characters change more drastically. The story is entertaining and scales nicely as time passes, also have some pretty badass bossfights! :D
Have some nice references to other games and jokes about RPG cliches to put a smile on your face hidden in the dungeons and all over the world maps as well.
The only negatives for me despite the lack of customization (although it is a pretty common factor in JRPGs) are that for
1.) we get too little info about our main characters so you have a harder time developing a deep connection with them, but the moments you do get are nice and well written
2.) the level cap is pretty low so after about 2/3 of the game I was running around with maxed out skills and legendary weapons - wreaking havoc whenever something dared to stand in my way :D
So again I really DO RECOMMEND this wonderful piece of well written and nicely drawn fantasy adventure with a unique atmosphere to any RPG fans out there! It is a MUST BUY!

[[UPDATE 8/27/2016]]
The withering could best be described as State of Decay meets Day Z.
It gets its looks and feel from Day Z, but the meat of the game comes from State of Decay.  As in State of Decay, you will have to go out to scavenge for resources (food, wood, fuel, ammo & weapons) and survivors to join your camp.  You can also have multiple characters to roam the open-world portion with, but only the ones you create (up to 4: 1 leader and up to 3 heroes).  The rest of the survivors that join your camp will only be able to be used to scout, scavenge, and be used for production points that are used to upgrade the camp, build additions, and produce bits from the scavenged materials.
As in SoD, you will encounter other survivor groups that will open up diplomacy options (offer tribute, request supplies, trade, request aid, and request missions).  You can also build a radio tower to try and communicate with the outside world.
Time in the game is a bit odd.  When you are on the camp screen, time passes in phases: morning, daytime, evening, and night.  However, in the open world areas time passes in real-time, and this does not match up with camp time.  So, you could be out in the open world scaving and killing infected for days, but no time will have passed when you get back to camp.
There is also currently no permadeath for your Leader or Heroes.  They just return to camp and are out of play for a number of phases to heal.  The do loose all loose items in their inventory (except their weapons, clothes, armor, or backpack).
If you love survival games, this is worth checking out, even in early access.

TL;DR Bouncy combat, cool housing system, and challenging raids/dungeons. Very generous freeplay model. Low population means pvp and dungeon queues are pointless until max level. Bad optimisation means low framerates on some PCs.
I have a lot of hours pre-steam, but thought I would return as it's now free.
I like the action combat system - it's bouncy and fresh compared to most other games in the genre. The sci-fi setting is also a novelty compared to usual orcs and dragons etc, but the story and general atmosphere are immensely cheesy and forgettable (evil English space empire vs plucky space 'Muricans) so I'm ambivalent to that aspect.
Graphics are cartoonish which I don't mind. Presumably it's so the game will run more comfortably across a range of PC specs, but I've always had quite a poor framerate for such an average-looking game (despite a reasonably beefy computer). I was hoping for more graphics optimisation since the last time I played, but unfortunately this wasn't the case.
Server chat was active, but it seems that most players are at the level cap of 50. Pvp before reaching this point is non-existent according to chat (I can attest to this as I spent 2hrs+ in queues while doing other stuff). I was hoping for a bit of open-world pvp, but the only exiles I saw at a similar level to mine didn't have pvp enabled. Likewise any pre-endgame dungeon queues are described as pointless on forums and in-game.
Population is low now, but there are adequate numbers at lvl 50 for most activities according to chatter. I didn't stick around to find out though.

Not a bad game by any means, but I will say there isn't a lot to it. There are enough items and enemies to give proper variety, but there isn't much to come back to unless you're really determined to beat it, as there are so far (11/20/2017) no persistent elements like other roguelikes and really only one effective way to beat the game.
It handles well, gives a decent (then suddenly painful) challenge, and is easy to figure out. Magic is a bit too weak to rely on for actually killing enemies, but it remains useful enough to keep handy. Melee weapons degrading and arrows (sometimes) being a little hard to come by add a sense of caution as you can easily break your best weapon if you use it too often.
All in all, it's good if you buy it for what it is: a quick little dungeon delve that's more a test of skill and inventory management than an RPG like many other roguelikes. If you like what you see, it won't hurt to try it.

Poured quite a lot into this game. Within 200+ hours I have completed (that is, won or lost) game 3-4 times. Stellaris is a gem in grand strategy games, which I adore a lot. I could not comment on the game without the DLC's, as I have bought every single one of them upon release, there are numerous useful and interesting mechanics which are not offered in the base game.
One of the things I like the most about Stellaris is the modding support. I have roughly 140 mods, 90% of which are cosmetic improvements such as planet variety. I also use a couple of mods for balancing purposes and fixes of clunky AI.
Therefore, it's rather difficult to write a review about a product which was modded so heavily from my side, and, I believe, other players have different experience of Stellaris based on the mods they used.
As far as base game is concerned, I love it's combat system, ability to construct your own empire the way you see fit. At the moment I have a Swarm: a devouring empire which conquers others just to have a delicious meal of some moluscoid race, which is then served with some plantoids. ;]
One of the charming elements of Stellaris is its unpredictability of outcome. For instance, I was conquered by one neighbouring empires and became their vassal. Naturally I was considering to start a new game; however, I've decided to see if it's possible to rise from ashes. In 20 years (game time) I have built a strong enough fleet to declare war on my masters and completely crushed them, ceding their planets as mine; and so did the servant become the master.
I do like the game, and I think it is worth the price. ;)

- Lots of customazation of your bike is added.
- You can now run your own team.
- And quite a lot more new features...

- Great graphics, by far the best in its genre
- All the original tracks, teams, names (to me this is worth a lot)
- Loads of new features compared to the previous game
- Changes, like whip/scrub control, make me feel that the developers did listen to the players requests
Con's:
- Meh.... physics
- Still the terrible engine sounds
- Performace is great, but you've got to test quite a couple of settings before you find the right one
- Still some bugs from the previous game, but no game changing ones

I've been an SLRR fan for quite some time and I purchased this game to help and support the developers. I got into the game thinking, "I know what SLRR is gonna be like..." Well, I was right and wrong.
If you enoyed the previous versions of SLRR (2.2.1 or 2.3.0), you'll definitely enjoy this one as well. The game still maintains SLRR's unique, in-depth, highly detailed tuning/customization. To date, it's the only racing game I've ever played that allows you to build a car from scratch. Players can purchase engine blocks, heads, pistons, connecting rods, exhausts, intakes, camshafts, crankshafts, transmissions, turbochargers, superchargers, fuel rails/types, tires, brakes, springs, shocks, anti-roll bars, seats, pedals, steering wheels, etc. and then you're left to build the whole thing yourself. The tuning possibilities are endless. And if you crash, you pay for whatever damage you've made. If you crash and lose an engine (it's bound to happen at some point, lol), you're gonna have to buy more parts to rebuild another engine.
In comparison to the previous versions, this game does a lot of things better. There is a bigger variety of cars to purchase, the physics feel more solid (in my opinion), and the addition of new racing events allows players to race their vehicles on numerous amounts of racetracks, not just the streets of Valo City. Players can now also change the amount they want to wager on night races, allowing you to make some really quick cash.
My only concern is the game's stability. SLRR has a reputation for being unstable. It crashes A LOT, and you may come across some glitches and bugs every now and then. The recent updates have made a lot of improvements though. If the unstability isn't a huge concern to you, I would definitely recommend this game, and to anyone who is a car enthusiast.

A lot of people give a pretty one-on-one description of what kind of stuff happened in their games. Because interstellar war is no joke, I decided to use a metaphor to describe one of my playthroughs in Stellaris.
Imagine having a very rude and obnoxious next-door neighbor who terrorizes everyone in the neighborhood. This neighbor has several kids whom he keeps under strict supervision. His kids, and everyone else in the neighborhood dislike the guy.
One day, one of his kids runs away and asks if they can stay at your place, because you’re a cool guy. Being the nice person you are you agree and let them in. Neighbor does not like this.
Later, another one of his kids runs away and asks if you’re willing to look out for them a bit and in exchange they’ll help you if someone picks a fight with you. They’re weak as hell, but you’re still trying to be chill and say yes.
The neighbor doesn’t really care, and decides to let it rest.
But sometime after his kids running away, he decides he doesn’t like you, and demands you go work for him. The guy is seriously buff and is much stronger than you are, so you quickly decide to surrender before he can mess you up.
This results in you losing most of your freedom and you need to pay a lot of money before you’re allowed to do anything outside of your house. Furthermore, the neighbors with whom you had a pretty high standard pretend you don’t exist anymore.
This is pretty awful. So you decide to do something about it.
You go train at home. A lot. You become stronger and buffer than that pile of salt so you can stick up to him.
Fast forward a few years.
You’re not only one of the most well-trained people in the neighborhood, but the jerk of a neighbor has lost a lot of his muscle because he got in several fights with that cranky, crazy neighbor no one wants to mess with.
You laugh maniacally inside, and relish the freedom you’ll soon have again.
However, bad neighbor made a couple of buff friends who promise they’ll come help if he gets in a fight. Darn.
Still, you’re pretty strong so you decide to risk it. You go up to the neighbor and tell him to get lost.
He gets angry and attacks you.
Luckily for you, you’re so strong you manage to knock him out in basically one blow. Then you go on to wreck his house room by room, until his friends arrive.
His friends, however, are woefully unprepared for the 2 meter tall fighter which stands before them. They go at you one by one, and you knock them out too.
Eventually, the neighbor gives up and lets you free.  He also rudely tells you to get lost.
You’re happy, but you’re also pretty mad at the neighbor for being such a jerk.
Being one of the strongest people in the hood, you decide to put insult to injury and occupy a few of the neighbors rooms.
He does not like this, and calls for his friends. He and his friends are still weakened by the fight they had with you, and, like the brainless sods they are, also picked another fight with that crazy neighbor.
After a couple of fights the jerk has to give up several of his rooms, which you then use for your stuff.
It’s still not enough.
Finally, you decide to put up a middle finger to the guy who terrorized the neighborhood for years: You’ll force him to give up his house and then be an unpaid slave to you.
The only problem is, is that the loser became friends with the strongest person around. This is fairly annoying.
They’re still dumb, and are still picking fights with that crazy guy which decimates everyone in a fight. Thus, they’re pretty weakened.
So you go on to beat his butt and systematically occupy all of his rooms. He doesn’t want to give up, so you also beat up his friends repeatedly and occupy some of their houses as well.
After a couple of years the guy finally gives up, and gives the keys to his house to you, and promises to provide unpaid labor. He hates you, but eventually he finds out you’re a pretty cool guy and starts to like working for you.
At last, justice is served, and you’re free to dominate the galaxy with your stellar empire- I mean enjoy life in the neighborhood.

Disclaimer: I received this game before the region lock was lifted. Played on literally day one when the game came out for PC in North America. I do not know why SE would region lock such a highly acclaimed game, but now since the region lock is lifted, I can finally write a review.
NieR: Automata is by far one of the most engaging hack n' slash games in the decade.
The graphics are stable on Nvidia GTX970 and runs quite smoothly even on high particle density areas.
Combat is well-refined and innovative, splicing multiple game mechanics sunch as side-scroller, bullet-hell, and HnS.
The musical score is by far one of the most original that have ever been composed. The soundtrack is sold out in Japan, that should give you a clue.
The story is philosophical enough for an adult, and endearing ennough for a child. The characters are deeply refined as well. Even the average wall flower character has a story to be told.
Score Tally:
Story: 9.5/10 - A story well-written and beautifuly melded into the game.
Gameplay: 9/10 - Keyboard and mouse controls are good; having a controller -- even better.
Video: 9.5/10 - Stable at 1080p and 60fps with a GTX970 graphics card. Some drops to 40 during high particle scenes.
Audio: 10/10 - A unique masterpiece all in itself.
Overall: 9/10 - Simply a must-try one of a kind experience.
I would absolutely love to recommend this game to anyone, however, I cannot do so because of how Square Enix's corporate greed decided to region lock this game in Asia, giving no explanation whatsoever. For an avid follower such as myself, I found it a slap to the face of SE's and PlatinumGames's fans to do this. This region lock caused many players I know to simply bootleg this game from third party sources because demand was forcibly not met by Square Enix. The ban was meant to probably boost their console sales in Asia but very much backfired and a petition was signed by many clamoring fans to release it in Asia, the region with by far, the largest fanbase. I do not mean to condemn the game itself, just the producers who thought it was a good idea to embargo their Asian fans knowing that they can simply get this game from other sources other than Steam. For me, this is a shame that this even happened in the first place. I sincerely hope that Square Enix takes this to heart when making decisions such as this.

I will start off by admitting that this game does have some rough edges, as with any early access game. However, rough edges aside, there is some real potential displayed here and I quite enjoy loading it up after every update and checking out the new content.
Potential alone usually doesn't mean a whole lot these days, many games had it in droves and still ended up dead. However, seeing how committed and active the Dev team is really makes me confident that we will all see their vision for the game realized. They listen to feedback, update regularly and truely seem passionate about their project.
All that said, the game IS rough in places, it is an alpha. So if you want a refined, shiney experience maybe just hit the follow button and regularly check in on it's progress. Know what you're getting yourself into before you drop money on something all willy nilly and then leaving a bad review because you didn't get what you expected. It's not fair to the developers nor the folks interested in the game. Not to say legit criticism shouldn't be levied but playing for an hour, leaving a♥♥♥♥♥♥review then refunding the game is a pretty crappy practice when the game is changing so much, so often.
If you do however like testing new things, participating in feedback, finding/reporting bugs, etc then this really is a project I would recommend you check out! It lacks refinement but that comes later. The framework they are building is really shaping up to be awesome, there is fun to be had with it already and I hope the team and game gets the attention it deserves!

TL;DR: This game is a fantastic turn-based RPG. The art style is gorgeous and wonderful to look at, the environments and characters are well crafted, and the animations on attacks is basically flawless and never gets tiring to watch. The music is also good, but you have to get used to listening to the same tracks for long periods of time. The game does offer replayability with its 6 character roster, but only 3 in a party at a time and New Game+. I would give the game a solid 9/10 with my wishes being that I had supported them on Kickstarter and that they make another fantastic game.
Pros:
+Amazing visuals (I had faith former people from Darksiders could make a good looking game)
+Interesting characters (I never read the comics but I liked the characters almost immediately)
+Fantastic animation (looking at moves never gets old)
+Good variety (multiple party structures can prove successful)
+Nice mix of dungeons and exploration areas
+Navigating dungeons and the world map is easy
+Crafting is simple and adding more ingredients to improve results was a nice touch
+The alt-skins are a great way to mix things up visually (Gullibnretto looks dope, kinda like a heartless in a suit of armor)
+Sidequests and optional Hunt bosses are just as fun as the main storyline
Cons:
-Holding the Esc or E button to skip the intro every time got old quick (I get that it looks great but pressing Esc should auto skip it)
-There is a certain point about 10 or so hours into the game where the difficult jumps up (re-running old dungeons becomes necessary)
-Random spawning important items in dungeons can get frustrating (I ran Deadwatch 6 times looking for a skull)
-There isn't more of it (finished my first run in about 40 hours and I want another game :D)
Battle Chasers: Nightwar is a good game. It's a good game with great visuals, good music, fluid animations, and characters ytou can enjoy even if you haven't the comics. I found myself unable to stop playing and saying things like "maybe one more dungeon" or "maybe one more sidequest". Hell I even found myself fishing for WAY too long. The game does nearly everything right and not having some BS day one DLC or microtransactions only makes me appreciate it more in the current market. I'm a huge fan of how smaller (non-AAA) companies are producing fantastic simgle player content that I am more than happy to spend money on, while major companies keep shoveling out multiplayer, games-as-a-service that I'm quickly getting tired of. The game even does loot boxes right. The loot boxes are things you can purchase from the Collector for shadow coins. Shadow coins are very easy to get and loot boxes are only one of many things you can buy with them. These loot boxes contain random things from a specific dungeon. Anything from weapons, to armor, to materials and potions. Basically, you're looking for something from the dungeon and don't feel like running it again. A simple and non predatory way to put loot boxes into a game.
If I were to say anything negative about the game it would be nitpicky. Things like: having to hold a button to skip the intro cutscene every time, or the weird, sudden increase in difficulty, or randomized drops of important items in dungeons. Two of those things are even being patched out to make the game less of a grind and to even out that difficulty spike.
To wrap up, just support games like this. Support these smaller studios releasing games for $30 and being more enjoyable than traditional $60 experiences. We need a gaming economy where single player games are still important and worth your time. Where small studios can feel comfortable charging more than $30 for a masterpiece and games ridden with microtransactions must be F2P.

You ll be level 11 at the end of the 3rd dungeon if you do all the fights from the beginning of the game. The next mini dungeon and main dungeons are level 13. This might not seem like much but level up give huge boosts in this game and XP comes at a snail pace. Be prepared to redo each dungeon 2 or 3 times ( in a row) to be able to progress through the story.
This feels completely unecessary. The game could be a 20 hours great game, but instead it chooses to be a boring 40 hours game.
What made me stop is that on top of that, the characters do not get ANY xp if they are currently in the team. That means you can either stick for the whole game with 3 heroes or be ready for even more boring grinding. If the fights were super fun it'd be fine but they are not.
Minor other complaint: the battle musics are pretty lackluster. They give a nice mood, but none are there to pump you up or give a feel of intense action.

i'll try to address some problems that in my opinion stand in the way from delivering a good user experience in the game.
First off i have to say that i play this game only as a single player experience, and what i'm reviewing is merely based on the "my career" experience.
Long story short, this game has been developed year after year to become an arousing and visually stunning experience full of real world references and endorsements. Actual, basketball, gameplay is very marginalized compared to the visual content 2k is adding every year.
Going deep into the matter, first we have to think that this is no more a game, it is an industry. This is no more a game of basketball, it is a market broadcast of the NBA itself. What it delivers, and greatly, is about pulling the user of this software into the NBA universe as a whole.
This 2k industry is showcasing the NBA brand as a whole. While doing this, they are involving the users in their own social network. This media industry broadcast, ingame, perfectly shot "tv-shows", tries to involve people into their Esport-ish experience, while pulling prizes etcetera.
When launching this software, you are gaining axcess to a huge load of content, and statistics, and videos, trivia, easter eggs, etcetera.
Being the company mission to sell the NBA brand and to bring more fans and fanatics into the NBA franchise, they have to represent it in a certain way. and they excell in this. Me myself, have started to follow NBA intensively while playing this game over the years.
Where does all this i said collide with the gameplay development?
As i said, the company tries and delivers the best possible visuals a game could deliver in this videogame era. The animations in the game are, nowadays, countless. For each and every little move, they have a huge database of motion capture material. Most of it taken directly from the NBA players to better represent them. This galvanize, and most importantly, spoil the eye.
To link these animations alltogether, yet, is a problem. It's a drawback to the gameplay.
To represent a fadeaway and the d from two different build of players, in a realistic way to the eye, means that the control  the player has shall be taken away to a certain degree. Controls in this game are the most unresponsive in ANY sport game to present day.
The problem, with this, is that being the company mission what said above, considering this game is almost a monopoly over the genre, and considering the game entertains the players with the huge amount of visual content... considering all that, the controls being unresponsive is not an issue to the 2k industry. The controls being unresponsive, ITS A FEATURE.
It's the company "guarantee" that what will be shown on the screen it's visually stunning and entertain to watch, as close to "reality" as possible.
THE AI will be the same on any settings, because that's the representation of an NBA game this company wants to show; but most importantly, it's the best they can deliver WHILE fitting the animations alltogether, and all the variables regarding the statistics of every single player potrayed ingame.
To make everything believable, numbers HAS to be shown in a believable way. Statistic shall get close to "reality". While this being almost impossible (and ultimately failing to a certain degree, and most surely to the more exigent players), the player in this big hard equation, is a noisance, a variable that the game engine has to control, to limit, so that it won't break the movie the way it has to be potrayed.
The path this company has drawn is clear. To better represent the NBA wich they are showcasing, they are sacrificing the freedom and creativity of gameplay.
WE ALL HOPE one day they'll solve the franchise problems (listing a few, to represent the most):
-defenders sticking like glue to your player, while snapping magically out of hard d when YOU try to defend them
-defenders stealing the ball from you as soon as the ball collides to ANY other physical model on the court, while completely ignoring this rule when it's the ai attacking.
-passes rresponding to IQ statistics more than player choice (meaning easy assist are a nono, better to pass to the unreachable teammate behind 4 defenders)
-space-time continuum obliterations in the extraordinary ability of the defenders to leap in the air or to close up crossing all the fiels in the split of an eye blink just to avoid you to score an easy one.
-teammates that neverever GTFO your free path to the basked (and blocking you when you are trying to defend the paint)
-and so on
WE ALL HOPE that 2K could solve these problems one day.... but as said before, all these facts are not problems from their point of view, these are FEATURES, to represent the NBA game the way they HAVE TO, to SELL the NBA BRAND.
If the rules can't be bent for the sake of representation, then the final product would not respect the company mission.
So the path is as it follows: the engine is the same every bunch of years, then it's updated, and the series start again. What they do, it's just adding animations. ANIMATIONS ANIMATIONS ANIMATIONS. And make them compatible each other. If something is not scripted, then it's not in the game. if your eye sees a corridor betwean your player and the basket, it doesent mean that the engine is considering that a free lane to the basket. If you see something that the engine it's not enacting, you won't be able to exploit it. period. If you play smart, you get punished. Because game it's inconsistent. You won't jump to grab the rebound until the engine decides it's time for you to jump and get late to it. One time you have to react quickly, the other late, and there's no coherence to this. Because you have to stay on rails, and start to think the gameplay as the engine "thinks" it. You and the ai are not playing with the same set of rules. you are a little mice on a wheel.
So, the only hope that gameplay will get smoother and free in time, it's about hoping that 2k will be actually good enough to keep on adding animations until there are so many and so smoothly adjusted together that speed will mean speed, space and time will be respected and not bent, etcetera...
BUT, there's no reason to believe this will actyally ever happen.... PROBLEMS WON'T BE SOLVED,  for two main reasons:
1- to represent, with endorsements, and with motion capture, and licences and stuff, this big show of the NBA they need HUGE AMOUNTS OF MONEY. -> to get money they are pushing hard the online competition so that people is pulled down into the BUY TO WIN vc market. while wasting real money on stupid shirts and animations, haircuts etcetera -> since the online competition it's so central to the mission to make this game as eye candy as possible, gameplay can't change too much from one game to the other, because the central rule of an E-SPORT is that the game stays the same over time (or people can't become better at it if the rules change).
2- Being visually stunning and having build this huge money machine (the two things, as we have seen, are deeply but intricately involved), playing this game spoils the eye and the player to the point that ANY COMPETITION will seem awkward and unpolished in comparison, even if the gameplay of these competing games it's actually BETTER and FUNNIER. Being the sole game on the market, means they have no reason to change and tweak their winning horse.
THE GAME IT IS LIKE IT IS, AND IT WON'T CHANGE.
Should you buy this game? no. Because you are not the user, you are the product of this big marketing machine.

If you've played World of Warships (or World of Tanks, for that matter), the game progression is similar -- play ships in PvP matches against other players to earn EXP to unlock better modules and/or ships.
Where this title departs from being just a mere World of Warships clone is as follows:
+ Has submarines, which are powerful if let loose among the capital ships in the back of the fleet, but are weak against destroyers.
+ Torpedoes are manually fired one-at-a-time, requiring manual input to nicely spread, but also allowing for fine-tuning of said spreads.
+ Ammunition isn't unlimited! You can't just fire all the time and expect to have ammunition (especially torpedoes) left by the end of a match.
+ Battleships are actually powerful with their main guns, and can lob rounds well out of their own view range (which is what scouts like destroyers are useful for!).
+ Aircraft carriers can pick and choose their own plane loadout, allowing for customization to your own playstyle.
- Because of battleships being really powerful, they're currently (as of this writing) somewhat over-used. Matches can often have more battleships than other ship types.
- Cruisers as a whole tend to be VERY sparsely populated (because of the glut of battleships, which easily shred cruisers).
- Physics is arcadey at times. Ships can accelerate or stop much faster than would be possible for a ship of their size (battleships getting up to speed within a few seconds, for example).
Gameplay is somewhat of a mix between Battlestations: Pacific and World of Warships.
Overall I would recommend this game to anyone who wants a good naval-themed game.

The new, updated version of the old classics like Master of Orion, Space Empires and Galactic Civilizations, but instead of turn-based this game is real-time with the option to pause.
Way off from the earlier games of Paradox, this still is a very solid game, especially if you like these kind of space-civ building games. Very nice touches are the ability to completely customize your race, but also to allow custom made races to be drawn into future games as AI opponents. Also, Paradox events are part of this game, so expect a few laughters while reading through event descriptions, and there's more than a few references to historical events that could've taken place here on earth.
Still, compared to other similar games, this feels slightly streamlined, but I suppose that's on par with Paradox products. If you consider EU, CK or some other of their titles, much detail never went into the tactical parts, how machines were to be made or what composition units would have except for a variation of base troop types. In that sense, having 4 types of base ships that can be modified somewhat according to your liking is decent enough I suppose, but this and the sort of slim options on planet building, coupled with the almost total absence of tactics is the drawbacks of this title.
They don't bug me much though, those shortcomings I just listed. This game really shines in its strategic parts, and diplomacy can be really interesting and unexpected. There's options for building federations, as well as having vassals, contributaries and so forth, to alliances, non-agression pacts, trade deals and different types of war. The difference in war is determined by your nations focus, as pacifists wont' be able to wage conquest wars for example.
As for the strategic parts, instead of going for one of the classic star-travel choices of warp, wormhole or starlane hyperdrive, this game has all three. You'll get to choose one, and strategy will differ depending on what you pick.
The game also contains alot of references to sci-fi movies, like the alien genetic xeno-troopers, that turns out as "Bio-warfare divisions" and contains Xenomorphs (I guess
finally got their way, huh?), so it's clear that the homework has been done on sci-fi as well, wich at least helps me appreciate a game like this even more, and you can be the sci-fi component as well, by invading planets that have sentient beings that hasn't reached space yet. Land your troops amongst atomic-age sentient mammal beings, or establish an observation post in orbit, silently observing, try to enlighten them with technology, or maybe stay hidden and just do secret experiments on them, the choice is all yours.
Finally, there's also domestic politics, with different fractions, unrest, potential revolts and whatever you could imagine, and if you have aliens to your race as slaves in your area, expect an emancipation movement to start sooner or later. You can make political decisions, and those decisions will have an impact, not only on what your empire can do in the galaxy, but will also impact home opinion, and as always, there's always some people happy about a certain direction, as there's always people unhappy about it.
All in all, this makes for a game with surprising depth, and not all you can do have been mentioned in this review. As such it's well worth picking up and can provide with lots and lots of good gaming time. Some parts could've been more complex, but I suppose it's a balance between it all. One thing is for sure though, and that is that it is solid as it stands, and have potential to become a true classic. My opinion on Paradox DLCs are that they're very often solid and mostly brings new, interesting and depthening concepts to their games, so it's anyones guess how good this could actually end up becoming.

Independent game studios turn out countless games they refer to as "Rogue-like" every month. Somebody apparently spread a rumor around that disjointedly yelling "perma-death!" and "randomized dungeons!" will make players flock to your store page to pre-order your game in the thousands.
But it takes more than dodgy design choices to create a fun experience, so let's talk about why I like Delver.
Delver begins by dropping you in a clearing with some dudes hanging around in it, located conveniently adjacent to an unexplored dungeon containing vast amounts of treasure and/or gruesome death. You're given the implied instructions to go to the bottom and escape with a magical relic left by a nasty wizard.
The game is light on story, but heavy on game play. It handles like a third-person shooter, but mechanically it's very true to the authentic "Rogue-like" model. The game is really about exploration, managing resources (like healing and spell items), and solving puzzles. It has no class system or equipment restrictions, leaving it to the player to scavenge whatever they can find and ration arrows, wands, weapons, armor, food, and potions to overcome challenges as they appear.
As a result, the randomized treasure has very little chance of completely screwing over the player, leaving them with exactly the wrong combination of items to advance. By increasing the right ability scores, it really feels as though any attempt can be a good one. What's more, gold collected during a failed attempt can be spent on gear to give yourself a better edge on the next run. The game isn't easy, mind you, but it's difficult in a very fun way.
The visual design is great, too, with big cartoon-style monsters lurking in the dark corners of the blocky, pixel art architecture.
Delver is probably one of the only recent titles claiming the rogue-like label that actually appears to have taken its cues from the original "Rogue" title.  Moreover, Delver manages to minimize the drawbacks of a, "semi-randomized level structure and no continues," adventure game model while preserving a lot of the excitement.
I've had a lot of fun with Delver since it first entered early release, and it's only gotten better with some age and patches. Absolutely worth the price tag if you're craving a serious "Rogue-like" that isn't just some random game with generated levels and permanent death attached as an afterthought.

I must have played thousands of hours of the vanilla version of Medieval 2. Then I discovered the mods.
A review of the game, as it is now for 20 Euro, is that it is still a great strategy game with awesome tactical battles. If you haven't played any Total War, then I would recommend to start with Medieval 2. There are newer games, but those are tweaked away from what I think are the best features in the Total War series. And yes, buy the collection so you get Kingdoms (4 new game modes that each feels like a proper expansion, compatibility with Third Age mod) for 3 Euro more.
My only major complaint with Medieval 2 is the AI. The difficulty scaling is just how soon the AI will declare war on you. Even if you have a tiny neighbour that you've been allied with for hundreds of years and protected through dozens of war, it is only a matter of time before they will declare war on you. The tactical AI will form a solid battle line and try to flank you with cavalry. And do exactly that in nearly all situations.
Longbowmen (and some other archers as well, can't remember which ones) are also way overpowered, since the most lethal thing known to (horse)man in this game are wooden stakes, and longbowmen can plant those in the deployment phase of a battle.
Loved it although must say buy the dlc since many outstanding mods require it.Tthat is this games real strength the amazing mods which more than triple the play time for me!

When I first saw The Withering I was cautious, it looked like another game that is a huge scam(the health bar is what made me think it was THAT game just given a different name) but thankfully it isn't since it started out with singleplayer(Multiplayer is in closed beta) and will keep single player when the game is finished.  I would say that The Withering has the potential to be one of the better zombie survival management games out there.(The only other one that comes to mid is state of decay)  Your main task is to find supplies to keep your camp going, finding other survivors to increase your camp size so you can build upgrades to help your camp thrive.  You can send your survivors out to gather resources on missions too.  As of right now there is 3 locations you can go to scavenge for supplies(The newest map has a mission that you do to get some better loot.  You can also see that they have plans to expand this map as well as add new missions), there is also a freeroam map in the works.
The gunplay is good, it could be better but it is EA so it will more than likely get improved as time goes on.  Melee definetly need some improvement but it could be worse(if you time your swing right regular zombies can fall with one hit).  Zombie can sneak up on you if your not paying attention(especially crawlers) but the normal ones die from a single headshot.
I will say that you should ignore the negative review that have less than 5 hours, because it takes about that long to get a feel for the game and whether or not you'll like it.
Overall, I'd say that I would recommend this game for the price of $10 since it has the potential.

Ok so it’s about time I update my earlier review on Steel Ocean, as you can see so far I’ve put over 1000 hours in the game not the most by far but at least a decent amount to get a good feel for what’s going on right now and the hopeful future....that and I’m not a pasty skinned, sweaty basement boy.
So let’s get right into the pros and con’s of Steel Ocean:
Pros:
-It has playable submarines.
-The hitting power of a battleship is exactly as it should be and not like other naval games we know where the damage is significantly reduced depending on target size.
-DD’s can’t spam fires everywhere their shells land and can play multiple roles such as scouting, fast flanking, torpedo deterrent, kamikaze (if that’s your play style), advanced AA support screening and of course the all important anti submarine warfare to help keep those fat battlewagons safe.
-Simple things as well such as the ships propellers stopping when the ship does, the recoil of the gun barrels after firing and rudders that actually work!
-A more pleasing sinking animation that the idiotic stop dead, BBQ and sink on the spot as it is with another known naval game.
-Low and behold you can actually MANUALLY use all your guns in either salvo mode or single fire (yes you read it right that mains, secondaries and AA!). This also applies to torpedos too!
-The guns don’t take a year to traverse either which allows you to stay in the heat of battle for longer and play a more effective role.
-Although there is a time limit the battles can feel lengthy or as quick depending on how engrossed you get into the battle!
-Love them or hate them the night battles are an interesting change to the game play making you think more about your location  and distance to allied ships as the enemy could be right on top of you and you wouldn’t even know it until it’s too late.
-The growth plan (which is paid for with real money) is a nice addition to the game, Steel Ocean is by no means unplayable without premium but it does help you get to where you want faster and with the growth plan you get a nice little exp and gold bonus per tiering up.
-As for the ships themselves they are not floating citadels, you can still receive critical hits but they are nowhere near as game breaking as the other game alternative has it.
-The game has an active and working fleet system, enough said there.
-Through out the week there are a multitude of events which you can participate in from fleet battles which help your player made fleet get high up in the ranking system to the 5v5 event where a high enough score at season’s end can land you some nice rewards including free gold currency, there is also challenge mode where a group of 5 have to sink a player controlled overlord (supership) and trust me those ones hit hard! Scenario mode can be fun also where you can either be part of a Japanese invasion force or the defending American fleet. Other events are mostly related to levelling up or game participation but can still be fun with some nice awards.
-Ok so you may be wondering what kind of ships are available:
RN - Destroyers, cruisers, carriers, battleships and battle cruiser’s have full tech trees but still no sign of cruisers or subs yet.
IJN – Subs, destroyers, cruisers, carriers and battleships have full lines.
KM – Subs, cruisers and battleships have full lines but no destroyers yet and doubtful that there will be carriers as historically they only had the one almost complete carrier that never seen service.
US – Subs, destroyers, cruisers, carriers and battleships all have full lines.
China – Only has two premium ships at the minute, would be interesting to see what fictional ships they come up with mind you.
France – Only one premium sub at the minute though could be an interesting nation to have given that they had a modern and powerful navy during WWII just never had the chance to use it.
Italy – Only one premium battleship just now though is another nation that could show promise if given a full tech tree as they did have some quite impressive ships during WWII.
-	Damage models for the ships seem to be quite accurate and shell impact points do reflect damage textures which is a bonus.
Con’s:
-	The game has a small community due to inadequate game advertisement by the developers, in fact by talking about the growth plan above I have probably done more than they have.
-	Yes the graphics are not as good as world of warships, there I said it though they are not bad on ultra setting...I guess the developers don’t try to fool the dribbling masses with all the bells and whistles like our Russian friends.
-	I dare say that the game could do with a bit more optimization to run smoother.
-	Heard it in the grapevine though more than a German proxy server would be handy but at this stage pointless unless they are willing to advertise the game correctly.
-	Premium ship although fun do cost far too much.
-	The silver gain in the game isn’t bad but could be a lot better.
-	Dev team seem to be sucking down too much noodles to advertise their game (yes I mentioned it before and will do many, many times.
-	You can get chat muted without any reason given at any time if one of the devs or devs fan boys decide they have had enough of you asking questions in chat.
-	The chat cuss filter is idiotic at best, very ”engrish” with words being blocked that make no sense to block them and others that are cuss words not being blocked....you could almost say that the code was written by a blind five year old but that would be an insult to blind five year olds.
-	The US server doesn’t get given the same perks as the Chinese server plain and simple especially when it comes to events and bonuses.
-	They removed five player squads, probably because there aren’t enough players to justify it or the incredibly long wait time for battles though it’s their own idiotic fault for failing to advertise correctly.
Suggestions:
-Well some more optimization wouldn’t hurt.
-Advertise the game more...idiots.
-lower the prices of premium ships.
-You may want to explain to someone why they have been chat muted instead of just doing it and letting them wonder why you lot are idiots....just a suggestion.
-Bring back five player squads....or would you rather be wargaming fan boys with the current three person squads?
-Since you got some small details included in the game for realism i.e. working rudders, propellers that spin to the rate of the actual ship speed and stop! Why not add spinning radar’s and range finders the follow the guns direction?
In conclusion:
The game is very in depth, playable and good fun especially in groups though can get some getting used to. You do really have to get past tier IV for it to really start to grow on you which is what most of the whiney little cry baby Wargaming fan boys haven’t done before posting negative reviews and scurrying back to their dumbed down vodka fuelled idiot fest WoWs.
My advice would be to stick it out get some skill under your belt and research a fleet to join up with...don’t spam apply as you could end up with a bunch of unhelpful idiots.
