First of all, after reading the negative reviews, I did NOT have any of those problems, even more strictly, they're probably outdated and need to redo their reviews.
Take This review from someone who actually DID put time and effort into the game, to write an honest, unbiased review.
Basic sum up Pro's and Con's
Pro : It mixed games like Dead State and The Division in the good sense.
- Frequent updates
- Developers listen and love feedback
- Its playable for its state, I can say I'm in the safezone with almost everything build 8/10 progress, and could finish it 10/10. 14 hours of game time is not bad at all.
- Games a lot of fun, scavenging isnt that much of a pain, and the Beta overworld at least is pretty good
- It takes strategy to plan in what recourses (Ammo for instance,) you're going to get, and what upgrades matter the most to you at present.
- Its very versatile, its XCOM camp management does it rather well.
- Play with up to 4 different characters in 1 team (excluding extra survivors you can get for the camp management part) which you can create at the main menu, and immediatly acces and deploy in your game, (You can start with 1 / 2 and gather resources till they knock out before you create more).
-Events at night like the flare (Marks the spot of loot locations, ranging up to 3 colors that all have their own kind of loot, and fight intensity
- 2 Special infected so far, that are not that easy to beat, and hopefully a lot more
- Co-op feature coming up, mixed with more actually deploy missions (Or raids better said)
Now, Cons!
- The combat system is clunky. VERY CLUNKY.
(Explained : Guns arent too bad at all, they're just inaccurate like real guns, and sometimes shooting at the same spot takes a couple spots to hit, for example a headshot when an enemy is hiding behind barrels); against the Melee, which has zombies flying very random ways from where you hit, and you can stun lock yourself in a combo that you can only exit by a well timed kick)
That overal takes some time getting used to it.
-- Sum up for devs, Gun accuracy isnt a problem that needs to be adressed, the rest is. ESPECIALLY THE MELEE WHICH IS STUPENDOUSLY LOW ON DAMAGE, AND WITH ZOMBIE GLITCHES PRETTY MUCH USELESS. UNLESS GUNS ATTRACT ZOMBIES / HORDES, ITS ALL YOU"LL EVER NEED; JUST LIKE SIDE-ARMS BEING UTTERLY USELESS COMPARED TO THE DAMAGE, AND NOT YET IMPLEMENTED REPAIR COSTS.
-Bandits spawn way too much ammo, you can literally farm the hard quest, or city runs for more ammo than the red flare spawns.
- Fuel is a pain to get as a resource, its very impractical and unbalanced compared to the others; as it is the most actively used resource in various ways; so you're pretty much always stuck at 0 unless you do manual deploy city runs.
- Stand on a car, king of the hill. everything is frozen and an easy shot (Didnt play like this personal because of obvious it being lame, didnt try if it worked on bandits; probably not.
- There's way to much unexplained, the tutorial does not do much of a great job explaining much of anything, and the description of some constructions can be a bit vague, and lead to (positive) surprises, so game can be confusing.
- The WHITE loot boxes near where bandits are, are VERY poorly indicated, and VERY EASILY!!!!!<<<  DEVELOPERS READ confused for the random junk objects on the floor
-There's no indicator of where dropped loot is at, so its a pain to find.
- Guns are a bit unbalanced, most scoped rifles do far less damage than unscoped ones; makes no sense if you sport a game for realism like this one
All in all, for the 10 XDDD bucks I bought it for, I can say I didnt really regret playing this, and am happy to have finished it. Will wait for future updates to come back and play, but I hope the developers read this and understand their game is going the right direction, and they can expect (Me at least) and perhaps more following in the future if they continue building this game.
P.S To the developers, my friends laughed and made fun of your game for having written om the store page that basically this game is a pioneer at its field; It's really not. Its just a combination of in my best opinion (Scrambled into a nice omelette : DayZ, Xcom, State of Decay and the divison.) Your game does better than the latter 2; but still has a little to go before its a diamond. You do have serious potential of getting there though!

I have, what I feel, are quite a few hours invested into this game now, and I really enjoy this game. After stumbling across this I looked for others similar and came across World of Warships, so this is mostly comparing to that game.
This game seems to focus more on realism than WoWS. The travel speed of the ships, the responsiveness to turning, the rate of fire of the cannons/torpedoes/AA/etc feel much more real.
The graphics are beautiful, the ocean looks very realistic. The physics are great, but would like to see some more variation in the waves. The ships look awesome and are incredibly detailed. Customization is fairly minimal, with a set list of patterns avaialble and flags as options. This will transition into the cons of the game as these customizations are only avaialble permanently with the purchase of gold with real money.
The cons of this game come in to the upgrade system I feel. With 33.1 hrs in game at this point, playing between submarines and battleships, I have only been able to achieve a rank 5 ship. Moving forward from here I feel the upgrades are coming to come much slower. With the amount of XP required almost doubling each rank, without paying for their Premium Gold, which is rather expensive, seems like it woulds take hundreds of hours to reach rank 10.
To purchase even one of the cheapest avaialble ships via Gold, you're looking at probably spending 50+ dollars, and this would only get you about as far as rank 5 as well. The farthest avaialble gold purchase only seems to be rank 8 as well, which I personally feel is great since you can't immediately skip to the end, but again to reach this rank immediately would be looking at +$100 US to purchase.
Overall, as a casual player this game is a load of fun, and would recommend this game to anyone. Especially being free to play.

Wow - wasn't sure what to expect with this game, but it was a blast!  Highly recommended!  Fun all the way through - it can be "grindy" if you want to breeze through it, but I think the difficulty is more or less fine.  I love the way the characters are balanced - almost every character (one exception really) can be played in more than one way (in some cases, a perk gained later in the game makes this change possible).  I think that's an awesome feat - while you may think "oh this guy is just a healer" when you first get him, he can be damaging, backup-healing monster later on, etc.
There are a few things I'd have like changed but I wasn't really annoyed by them - stuff that realistically would take away from being "in the game" just for the sake of getting through it faster.  That's one thing I like too - in this age of gaming, we sometimes expect to keep going forever, chasing after esoteric and generally pointless achievements, just for the sake of what - killing time?  When this game is done, it's more or less done.  There's a new game + mode which is higher difficulty, but there's no real story changes you can force in the mode (as in no Chrono Trigger style endings etc).
Super fun, play it if you're at all inclined - very worth the price of admission.

as a world of warships player, I have to say, this game definitely shows promise. As it is currently however, I have no idea why anyone would claim its "better than word of warships". Frankly, there is no point comparing this game to WoWS, aside from them both being about naval warfare, its like trying to say warthunder is better than world of tanks (They're two different games going for two different styles of play...) lets get the negatives out of the way first
-- Momentum: torpedos are near useless when ships can stop and turn on a dime like  a tank. Part of these naval battles is calculating where your opponent will be when your shot lands. Part of those calculations are momentum, said calculations being voided when you can come to a complete stop at a rate of deceleration that should be impossible, its overly difficult to say the least.
--Punishing team killers: first match I played had no less than four teamkillers that started shooting allies and torpedo spamming right at the start, just on my team alone. teamkillers and greifers ruin the fun in a game, 'nuff said
-- Polish: currently, the game is poorly optimized and my alienware laptop has a hard time running it at low settings. I don't mind playing at low settings, but when my game on low settings has a framerate that looks like its having a seizure, I've got a problem with that...
OK, the bad is out of the way, now lets talk about the good, and there is a lot of good, which makes me looking forward to when this game gets some needed polish and updates
-- Battlestations midway style control: You have almost complete control over your arsenal on the warship. You can switch between gun salvos and individual barrel firing. you can launch one torpedo at a time or several at once, enabling you to lay down your own custom torpedo spreads and make some nasty strikes. You can also contrl your own AA guns and secondary batteries, not having to put your faith into AI gunnery.
-- Good graphics* : Ok, the game isn't very well optimized right now and I can barely run it at all in a match, but I can still see what the game "should" look like when in the tutorial by myself. It looks good, nice environments and good looking ships, nice details, etc. Once the game is properly optimized, I think its safe to say it will sure be pretty to look at
-- Sound: what can I say? the warships sound like warships. The guns sound as mean as you'd imagine a naval cannon should sound, the tropedos launching are convincing, the AA guns sound right...I haven't heard enough of the music to make a decision on whether I like it or not, but its definitely not bad. Firing your guns is almost as satisfying as hitting your target and dealing big damage
-- straightforward progression and upgrade system: self explanatory, if you played any of the "world of (vehicles)" games you know what I mean.
-- gameplay mechanics: there are many mechanics that just feel like they fit perfectly, assuming that the cons mentioned above can be adressed
-- Submarines: Ok, I'm not a fan, personally, but I can appreciate the addition of subs. some people like them, I'm still undecided if I like them or not, but they're here.
in short, there is a lot to like about this game, but there is still work to be done before I'd consider jumping in and really getting involved. Still...from what I've seen, I'm interested to see where this will go. When things get better and the game gets its needed optimization, I'll jump in and have another go, but as it is, I can't enjoy it just yet.

We waited 20 years for this... and it was kinda worth it.
Art - Visually, this game is stunning.  The color pallette is oversaturated and vibrant.  Animations are highly stylized and over-exaggerated, which compliment the comic book feel.  The 2D cutscenes are gorgeous, and voice acted as well.
Gameplay - This is old school JRPG.  If you wrote a review whining about how it's turn based, you obviously didn't do any homework.  This is how it should be.  Characters synchronize with each other and the abilities feel satisfying.
Is it perfect?  No.  It has some serious balance / pacing issues.  Early dungeons are too easy, later dungeons are too hard.  This makes you grind out early dungeons, which is never fun.  They're aware, and they're tweaking it.  Luckily for us, this is a relatively easy fix.
Thanks Joe Mad.  Wish I didn't have to wait so damned long though.

Battle Chasers starts out decent but get's old pretty quick.
I found this game by chance and bought it after reading / skimming some positive reviews, since I enjoy turn-based RPGs. I had no idea that the comic series, that this is based on, even existed.
In the beginning it's alright, even though it's pretty cheesy. Basically every character I encountered is a walking cliché and has some tough one-liner to spout. This is probably due to source material (comic series from 1998) but it didn't really help me enjoy the game more.
Walking around in the overworld is not very compelling. You can only move on pre-determined paths with some encounters or loot every couple of steps.
The dungeons I cleared before I stopped playing were alright the first time but didn't vary enough on subsequent runs. Since they are designed to be run multiple times (random layout, multiple difficulties, with the hardest not unlocked from the beginning) I expected more.
The combat is alright. I think if either health or mana refilled after a fight it would have been better (though they would have to rework the Overcharge system). Enemies can do a lot of damage, even if you outlevel them, so you are forced to heal. You probably don't want to spend too much mana that isn't overcharged, since you can only refill it while resting at the inn, once before the boss in a dungeon and potions (Knolan learned one burst that gives a bit mana to your party during my time with the game) and unless I know the game I play pretty reserved with my resources, since I don't know if I need them later (and finish the game, never having used a potion).
The turn order display during combat also feels really useless. Abilities are either instant or take a varying amount of time to complete. This means there are constantly changes in the order. This is a pretty minor issue though.
I really liked the look of the game. I think the models and animations look very nice, although some animations could be faster or cut (I don't think it's necessary to take 5-10s every time you start a battle).
Unless you like the comics you should probably skip this one or wait for a sale. At it's full price I can't recommend Battle Chasers.

This is a solid game. It lacks the brilliance of Borderlands 2, but retains much of what makes the Borderlands series so good. It's a first-person shooter that is built for co-op play. It's crazy and full of unique missions.
Pros:
Very tight combat. The controls are intuitive and give you a lot of freedom.
Interesting story and side missions. The story isn't the reason you should buy this game, but it is solid. The side missions are the real gems, though. Much of the game's humor resides in the incredible variety of side missions.
A real sense of character progression. Your combat experience revolves around your action skill, and you are given a lot of options of how to improve your character and your action skill. From reducing its cooldown to giving yourself bonuses when you kill an enemy to improving your damage and so on.
Very well-made classes. Each of the four base classes are a lot of fun and very unique. Athena is particularly satisfying.
Very small penalties for dying. You are encouraged to experiment and try new things, as the only penalty for dying is losing some of your cash. And since cash isn't too hard to come by in this game, dying is but a minor inconvenience.
The humor in this game hits the mark more often than not. It is a genuinely hilarious game.
Cons:
Solo play suffers. Two of the four base classes (Nisha, CL4P-TP) are difficult to use in solo play unless you are experienced. And one of the DLC characters (Aurelia) is extremely difficult to use in solo play.
An unfortunate amount of backtracking. There is a lot, and I mean A LOT, of backtracking in this game, where you are either just running from one mission point to another or driving in the moon buggy across large swathes of rocky terrain.
Not much variety in environments until the second half of the game. Most of the beginning areas look so much alike that it is hard to recall which area you are actually in.
Bad vehicle controls and terrible terrain for vehicles. The moon buggy handles awfully, and the terrain frequently gets in your way by launching you in unexpected directions.
Verdict: A game that succeeds due to its great combat and dark sense of humor despite frustrations stemming from a lot of backtracking and limitations in solo play. Giving it a 7.5/10.

Easily worth 7$.  The atmosphere, the lighting, the music, and the art are all spot on.  It reminds me very much of Ultima Underworld (a favorite from my childhood) and the developer has stated that was one of its primary inspirations.  I typically don't enjoy rogue-likes (terrible name for a mechanic imo).  I think my reason being is that I haven't played one that ever felt balanced, or fair.  They're typically too luck based.  Players often defend them as being more "difficult".  But often it ends up being a dice roll for the correct drop, or series of events to make advancement even possible.  I personally don't have the patients to re-roll until a game seeds correctly.  This game doesn't exhibit that quality.  To be clear, you will die.  But it won't be underserved.  I haven't died yet in a way where I was able to blame the game.  It's always been my fault.  Generally my cause of death is self immolation (don't underestimate the blast radius of your fireballs). Another general complaint I have about rouge-likes are that levels tend to not feel well designed.  They feel like they've been generated.  The levels in this game strike a really good balance between random and designed, in a way that gives the game good replay-ability.  Also the death animations are especially good :)

So, the politics of this game seems very deep. I started out with Holy Roman Empire. I built a high standing with the Pope. Then allied with the Papal States. Pope called for a crusade. I didn't join initially. In the meantime the Pope died and elections were called for. My cardinal became the Pope. Immediately became the most favoured nation with Pope. Joined the crusade with my king at the head of the crusading army...
What with managing your family tree, choosing your potential heirs, marrying off your family members, managing diplomacy with other factions etc. etc. you have your hands full. Unlike the Civ titles, there is no sense of randomness or emptiness when it comes to international politics as the game is founded in a historic setting, and every diplomatic move feels like it matters.
Haven't played further, but looking forward to smashing the enemies!

Went searching for videos on this game after finishing it to see what other people thought about it, and to be honest I was really disappointed with what I found, so I'm going to try to address all of the negative things I heard/saw about it in this review.
Firstly,
. Reading is the main focus of the game, it's a story based walking simulator, what did you really expect? It's barely even an hour long, if you can't read for at least an hour then I would be more worried about your attention span than how much you liked a game.
Second, "The game is so boring!". I seriously wonder if anyone who has said that actually finished the game. If you have said that without finishing the game, please complete it and then tell me what you think.
Third, "Oh my god! I found a typo! Game ruined!". If the only thing you have to complain about in this game is a typo, I think you might have better things to be complaining about.

This is a very preliminary review. I will try to update later after more play, but first impressions are not great. We'll have to see whether those positive reviews really make sense, or it's just a case of the "sweet lemon" fable.
First of all, it took me a while to even figure out what I was doing in terms of playing the game. There's no "play" button in the main menu, just "Camp" and "Survivors" (along with options, extras (currently empty), and quit). Then, once I had created a character under "Survivors" and gone to camp, it took me some time to realize how you actually get any sort of action sequence, as opposed to just automatically running missions and trying to read the results.
Actually, to talk about that: the interface is bad in camp, too. The tutorial, such as it is, does help, but you have to trawl through the menus to find out what happened after each time advance, instead of having it reported in some kind of simple pop-up dialog box or something like I expected.
Anyway, you actually go on a mission by going into the roster, selecting a "hero" that you've created, and clicking "Deploy". Not obvious at all.
Then... the tactical mission. My god, it's like '90s technology. Not only are the graphics poor, but at least in the first level, the zombies posed no threat, and often just stood there while I repeatedly shot at them. I wasn't even touched. Maybe that changes later, but meanwhile, running around the level was like trying to spring through water; the running pace was slower than many games' walking pace. Finally, the inventory space is critically limited; you will certainly be leaving things behind. Again, maybe all this gets better with better equipment, but it makes the first mission at least simply excruciating.
I did like the music and the incidental noises, if I'm pressed to find something rewarding. Oh, and the intro newscasts (which you can hear on the Steam store page) are nice enough.
I love games like this, I really do. Put hours and hours into everything from Project Zomboid, Dying Light, 7 Days to Die, and many others. Nonetheless, unless this game turns around dramatically very quickly, I will not be putting much more time into it.

Another Early Access from another small team.
Not a bad little game at all so far.
Keys to the future of note;
Multi player is planned.  The Dev ( as usual ) has answered countless times on that. The answer being, MP / and or Co op in the plans. Info available on details in the Forum.
More character customization.  Currently you do have both Male and Female models. But at the start of the game you can only change the character menu portrait and the starting clothing look.
and of course.. all the usual things that go with an EA.
I did not follow this from the start. I only looked it over today and did some research. The post and reports show it has changed much since it first arrived. That is always a plus. It also shows relevant answers from the Dev team often in the forum.
Game play wise, it is not a fast pace start off in the thick of it type Zombie game. Its a strange twist on several approaches to Zed gaming fans. First it is based on camp / survivor management. The system is simple to figure out and work with. Includes a quick in your face tutorial on getting started in the camp section. The UI is not the prettiest, but it serves well for now.
Then the ' sort'a ' open world. This is a ' sort'a ' moment because you dont just walk around an open world.  You start the game with knowledge of your general surroundings, but it is pretty limited. You learn more by assigning scouts to go and snoop. Once that is done you find either new fixed locations or event type. Fixed are sections of an area, say like a part of a residential zone. Events are like finding an abandoned camp, or a derelict vehicle, junk site etc. You then assign a team member to head out. Now comes the ' sort'a '. This takes place on an over the shoulder character. You have to have boots on the ground to explore, find items, equipment etc.
Combat is simple and varied. Different stats of the team member allow different affects. For example my high strength member can do a special move via double click RM and kill pretty much each time. My less buff can do the move.. but she has yet to kill on a first time strike. She is however much better with her firearm. See how that works?
Keys are mapped in the oddest fashion I ve ever seen. You just have to look to probably agree. But you can re-map with no problems. Movement is the normal.. other keys are weird. MAKE SURE you look and / or re-map.
CLIMBING on cars... this is important. Lesson learned. The first ' easy ' or ' baby ' zone it is not like it is other places. No idea why. After you leave the first area when you approach a vehicle at a climb / jump point you get a prompt.  In the first area you just cant get on them at all. You can however climb on a van.. its weird to read.. but if you experience you will get it.  No problems after the first area as I said tho'.
Finding loot... its hard. Its supposed to be. Unlike many games that just hand you finds.. other than obvious boxes laying around or tool chest, you have to look. You will find things like food, medicine, water, gear, weapons, and of course ammo. But its not marked with shiny lights or arrows to glowing boxes of goodies.  But it does give you a nice prompt when you do find it.. so you can ' sort'a ' just mouse around and make some finds that might not be obvious. But you have to be close to them.  BUILDING materials etc are usually easy finds. They are in boxes or took boxes. Easy being relative to the amounts tho'. Areas with an abundance are not easy to walk into and out of. Easy to pick areas are pretty empty.
Nice thing. When your out exploring you can leave the area via ESC and return to camp.. which causes a 10 second countdown, during which you are vulnerable.. so make sure your safe. Or you can walk out without the delay.
Overall, with its current EA price of $9.99 US its not a bad little thing.  But at its current state its not going to be for everyone. I see myself enjoying it, but not in large doses. More of a slow and steady time. BUT ON THAT. Not all the enemies are push over brain dead Zeds... that you will see on your own..
Great concept, but i don't recommend buying til it is fully release.

The new, updated version of the old classics like Master of Orion, Space Empires and Galactic Civilizations, but instead of turn-based this game is real-time with the option to pause.
Way off from the earlier games of Paradox, this still is a very solid game, especially if you like these kind of space-civ building games. Very nice touches are the ability to completely customize your race, but also to allow custom made races to be drawn into future games as AI opponents. Also, Paradox events are part of this game, so expect a few laughters while reading through event descriptions, and there's more than a few references to historical events that could've taken place here on earth.
Still, compared to other similar games, this feels slightly streamlined, but I suppose that's on par with Paradox products. If you consider EU, CK or some other of their titles, much detail never went into the tactical parts, how machines were to be made or what composition units would have except for a variation of base troop types. In that sense, having 4 types of base ships that can be modified somewhat according to your liking is decent enough I suppose, but this and the sort of slim options on planet building, coupled with the almost total absence of tactics is the drawbacks of this title.
They don't bug me much though, those shortcomings I just listed. This game really shines in its strategic parts, and diplomacy can be really interesting and unexpected. There's options for building federations, as well as having vassals, contributaries and so forth, to alliances, non-agression pacts, trade deals and different types of war. The difference in war is determined by your nations focus, as pacifists wont' be able to wage conquest wars for example.
As for the strategic parts, instead of going for one of the classic star-travel choices of warp, wormhole or starlane hyperdrive, this game has all three. You'll get to choose one, and strategy will differ depending on what you pick.
The game also contains alot of references to sci-fi movies, like the alien genetic xeno-troopers, that turns out as "Bio-warfare divisions" and contains Xenomorphs (I guess
finally got their way, huh?), so it's clear that the homework has been done on sci-fi as well, wich at least helps me appreciate a game like this even more, and you can be the sci-fi component as well, by invading planets that have sentient beings that hasn't reached space yet. Land your troops amongst atomic-age sentient mammal beings, or establish an observation post in orbit, silently observing, try to enlighten them with technology, or maybe stay hidden and just do secret experiments on them, the choice is all yours.
Finally, there's also domestic politics, with different fractions, unrest, potential revolts and whatever you could imagine, and if you have aliens to your race as slaves in your area, expect an emancipation movement to start sooner or later. You can make political decisions, and those decisions will have an impact, not only on what your empire can do in the galaxy, but will also impact home opinion, and as always, there's always some people happy about a certain direction, as there's always people unhappy about it.
All in all, this makes for a game with surprising depth, and not all you can do have been mentioned in this review. As such it's well worth picking up and can provide with lots and lots of good gaming time. Some parts could've been more complex, but I suppose it's a balance between it all. One thing is for sure though, and that is that it is solid as it stands, and have potential to become a true classic. My opinion on Paradox DLCs are that they're very often solid and mostly brings new, interesting and depthening concepts to their games, so it's anyones guess how good this could actually end up becoming.

I appreciated this game. You will too if you enjoy turn-based JRPGs with a bit of an exploration mechanic going on.
- Artstyle. Colorful and well-crafted. Cutscenes are 2D comic book style.
- Strategy. You can build some interesting teams with the six playable characters and perk system.
- Dungeons. They are fun and interactive. By the way, Gully's gauntlet stun field skill can break walls. I had no idea until the end of the game. Look for walls with dust falling out of them.
- Depth. Don't expect too much min-maxing beyond "how high can I push every character's attack stat and still have the other perks I want" because basically all skills (attacking / healing / buffing) without static values are influenced entirely by attack.
- Difficulty. This game starts easy, gets hard, and then gets easy again as the end-game approaches. It would be easy all around if you knew what you were doing the first time you played. Grinding at the "end game" will lead to absurd stuff like Garrison / Red Monika capable of 20k+ damage per action and heroes like Gully and that other guy generating shields of 7-10k.
- Grinding. I don't mind it. You might. Expect to repeat a dungeon at least once for RNG-related events, levelling up, more loot, etc.
- Some items require really obscure events (I'm looking at you, Gully's legendary weapon) to procure. I had to look up a few things the first time I played and that shouldn't be a requirement, frankly.
- RNG events for the above point makes it an even more sore spot. Don't make me run a dungeon ten times for one single event. The latest patch supposedly addresses this, but I did my time before that update. So, damage done to me. :(
- Battle transitions are slow. I would definitely like a way to speed them up or  otherwise skip more time.

I've put a lot of hours into this game (many more than Steam shows), and unfortunately the complete lack of statistical balance destroys what would be a really captivating and enjoyable version of Minecraft. The dungeon generation, music, and art are fantastic and initially kept me coming back for more, but the better I become at the game, the more infuriating it is to play and the less I can motivate myself to adventure further.
Money is useless. Not only is the drop rate absurdly low, but there are only two places to purchase items - at the beginning of the run, and just after the first two floors. It's ridiculous that I have to play 3+ runs to the boss just to get enough gold for one good item at the shop. And then the stores are so early that it's pretty much a waste to spend your money because you're bound to spend it all on that run where you accidentally get pushed into lava by a monster you didn't see. At the shop, you never feel like you're making a good run better.
Weapons are impossibly underpowered. At least 50% of the melee weapons you find on a given run you won't even want as backup due to random stat penalties. "Let's see, unholy dagger... +4 attack and -6 defense??" It's very rare that I even put on armor I find because the speed penalties are similarly high to the point where it takes you 10 minutes just to walk across one floor without fighting (and as anyone who has played past the boss knows, speed is REALLY important at the end of the game). Then you have magic wands, which come in two varieties: 1) fireball, which are absolutely wonderful but only have 6-12 shots (and usually insta-kill you if you hit something that is in melee range), and 2) all the other wands that are bad because they do so little damage, no matter how much you level up magic.
If that weren't enough, weapons break after a certain number of hits. Your inventory is way too small (24 slots) for the game to force you to carry around 6+ weapons because all the good (damage) weapons you found were in bad condition.
Finally, endgame. Actually getting to the boss is a healthy and enjoyable challenge. But then enemies pretty much flood out of the walls. Before the last few updates I was able to get ALMOST all the way back to the top of the dungeon. As of the last update, I can't get out of the boss room. I just had an amazingly lucky run with all the right items - I beat the boss, spent about 10 minutes in that room hacking away with my best weapon, gained 3 levels (each level gains you all your HP back), broke that weapon and 2 more, and then died because the enemies were simply spawning too fast for me to walk out the narrow hallway. My stats were 56 HP, 30 AC, something like 30 ATK with a fast-attacking Dusk and at least +2 default speed (with full armor). Every time I would get halfway down the path, enemies would continue to spawn and attack me from behind, forcing me to retreat and clear my back.
It's an addicting experience with a great foundation, but ultimately until the endgame (among other issues) gets fixed, I can't recommend a game that makes you feel like you've wasted your time with impossible goals. If I had gotten out of the dungeon, I don't even think I would have felt the victory. Only thing that can get you out right now is lucky enemy spawns and running, which any monkey with a Shift key could pull off eventually.

Graphics : For a game from 2012, it is quite ok. Some levels are nice, while some others show terrible textures. Definetely not at the top standards of TPS games, but quite enjoyable.
Sound: Gun sounds could have been a bit louder as we don't feel the calibers here.
Story : Ok, basically a usual Tom Clancy stuff. But I have to say, I like the atmosphere and how we can feel badass while extracting VIPs from a hot zone :).
I do recommend this game for any military shooter, and don't be misled by the "Future" stuff. Yes, some gadgets make it very futuristic, but overall, it feels like a modern era shooter.

There is content and playstyles for all types of gamers. If you are a rambo charging, goldfish attention span, CoD style player, you can take a destroyer or cruiser and blast things to your hearts content. You'll likely die a lot but then you normally have pretty low K/D ratios anyways.
If you are a more strategic player but you like to mix it up some, you'll love taking out a Battleship and just setting up shop on a map then grinning sadistically as your shells decimate attack routes. Then when things get in close, switching to your secondary cannons and making them regret ever approaching you.
Tactical player? Take a sub and decimate your foes from beneth the waves. Until you miss a torpedo and one comes in close enough to depth charge you.
Real strategic RTS player? Take a carrier out. Micro manage your fighter wings from behind the lines. Send bombers, fighters, and scouts up.
This game really has things for many types of gamers. Granted some are better than others. Which makes it hard to rate this game since it is more like an MMO and changes/balances all the time. Right now Carriers are a little weak. That doesn't mean you can't use them. Just gotta be even smarter with them.
The only major knocks I give this game are the fact you can't choose the gametypes to play. It's all randomized. Then the tutorials are a bit deceptive. Some of them are good, others seem to get you to spend coins or things that you earn that you might not want to spend. Granted they aren't gold coins which cost money but if you don't feel like spending something yet, you don't want a tutorial doing it for you. Keep in mind, esc button works to get out of this.
There is only one major knock that could be game ending for some. That is literally this game is highly populated in the lower tier ships but very sparse after you hit tier 5. You want to hang onto Tier IV and III vessels if you want populated games.
That all said, check it out, great time to be had and you don't have to spend a penny on it.

I'm a veteran player of NavyField, which certainly had its ups and downs, but won me over in terms of variety of play and quick matchmaking.  When I came back to it a few years later, the community had dried up and you could no longer reliably get into a full game.
NavyField 2 dropped one day and I was ecstatic - this was the game we'd been promised for years.  Unfortunately, NavyField 2 failed to deliver.  I could write a whole negative review on NavyField 2, but trust me, it wasn't worth the hours I put into it, and judging by the experience of high-tier players, it wasn't worth their time either.
Steel Ocean is the game that NavyField 2 should have been - third person instead of isometric view, more emphasis on teamplay, giving Destroyers and Cruisers roles beyond "rush the enemy, drop torpedoes, run, repeat", USABLE ANTI-AIRCRAFT GUNS, ship trees that make sense and steadily improve rather than getting worse in the middle tiers to force buying gold to make free exp with lower tiered ships, far less powerful microtransactions, far better graphical effects, more dynamic submarine play, and developers who actually work on improving the game instead of just talking about it.
It's not a perfect naval sim for the reasons others have noted - you tend to spend a lot of time just positioning and looking for something to fight, so games have a slow feel.  It's not a fast-paced FPS MOBA by any means.  At times it feels like turn-based strategy - I just shot, now my opponent gets to shoot, now I shoot back, eventually one of us dies.  Playing Destroyer or Cruiser is rewarding unless you get volleyed in the face before you can actually do anything.  Battleships are rewarding unless you get torpedoed in the back before you can actually do anything.  So combat sometimes takes a long time to happen, and when it does happen, it tends to be over really quickly.
Having said that, this is an excellent free-to-play MOBA with a very good tutorial and I'd highly recommend dumping at least a few hours into it.

I’ve played the three main games by now (I do want to try Tales of the Borderlands, but will wait for a sale), and being completely honest I was expecting this game to suck. I don’t know why, I just did. However I’m somewhat surprised in the end. As usual I’m gonna start talking about what the game does poorly, then go up from there.
First and foremost, the biggest issue I see on the game is the repetition. There’s not that much variety on enemies compared to the second game, and they don’t talk nearly as much as I hoped. What bothers me even more is that the big trailers of the game (specially the one with Mister Torgue) showed the Lost Legion to be the main enemies of the game, however they barely show up later in the game for a while, which sucks♥♥♥♥♥as they fought differently to the rest of them.
The second thing I didn’t like at all is how underused some characters are. Mister Torgue is by far one of the most loved characters in the entire franchise, yet he barely talks on three quests. Nina, the nurse, barely has one or two quests about her. Papa Crust, who sounded like an hilarious parody of Fidel Castro ended up only showing on a quest (a long quest, but just one). Even some of the main characters seem like that, Brick barely narrates anything and Tiny Tina, another well loved character by the fans only really appears in New Game +.
Something else I wasn’t a big fan have to be the weapons themselves. A few new kinds of weapons have been added, and some new kinds of elemental damage went into it as well, however I don’t think they were properly balanced. Laser weapons are way above everything, one of them (the E-Gun, a weapon that’s a parody of Ghostbusters that you get on a quest) was insanely powerful on the character I had picked (Nisha), to the point that I didn’t use ANY other gun for the next 10 levels until I got a good replacement as it was already getting weaker in comparison. And guess what, the replacement was also a laser weapon.
A problem that relates to the last one is the lack of difficulty. The game was quite easy from start to finish by myself. Now maybe it was because I ended up picking a broken character (I did feel like Nisha’s aimbot was too powerful and barely had any cooldown) but the only times I died was thanks to me getting suicidally overconfident. Also, the game’s new gimmick is the oxygen, but it barely does anything serious. The oxygen levels drop too slowly, are too big, and there’s pockets of oxygen EVERYWHERE, making it impossible to actually die because of asphyxiation. Also, the secret boss the game has after you finish the story wasn’t ANYWHERE as hard as bosses on previous games. Seriously, I beated him on my first try by myself. That’s kinda pathetic.
Lastly, the DLC’s. I’m not a big fan of them mainly because Gearbox keeps doing things right and then ♥♥♥♥ing it all up again, and this game doesn’t change that at all. There’s ONE DLC that adds a story, and one DLC that adds an arena. The rest are just two character DLC’s and weapons. Let’s look back at Borderlands 2 however, and A LOT of the DLC’s were characters and story based ones. What the ♥♥♥♥, man? The game advertises itself for having bazillions of weapons, WHY WOULD I PAY MORE FOR A FEW EXTRA!?
However, looking away from those issues you have a decent sequel to Borderlands 2.
The story is arguably the biggest point the game has running for itself, quite ironic since the story on Borderlands 1 was so lame and boring I couldn’t even bring myself to finish it. However, you SHOULD play Borderlands 2 before you go into this one to understand everything properly. Both are great, so you got nothing to lose on that. It shows that they have learned from their previous mistakes on actually making a good story line that hooks you up instead of a sorry excuse to just go shoot bandits in the face.
The characters themselves have also been expanded properly in comparison from previous games. In the original game the main characters barely even talked and nothing was explained that much. In Borderlands 2 your characters talked a bit more, and there was more story behind stuff. Here however, your characters actually do talk and express their opinions, the story is explained properly and if you happen to like your character, you’ll get really interested in seeing how things turn out for them. Extra points for having one of the main characters narrate it, however it would be great if all the characters would narrate their own story in their own way, not just Athena. I know the reason why they don’t, just saying each would have their own intro and reason behind it.
The enemies that are more or less unique to the game instead of recycled space versions are also interesting, mainly the Lost Legion and the enemies on the last areas. They got medics who heal each other, engineers who put turrets and other stuff, it’s interesting and changes the flow of gameplay quite nicely.
The references are also here as usual. Borderlands 2 had an insane amount of them and this game is not shy to show what inspired them at all. From escorting a pair of robots to an old man named Toby Van Adobe to making the Slammiest Dunk in history, the game won’t spend an hour without trying to crack a joke or two.
Lastly, the change in the setting of the game works quite well. Honestly I was kinda tired of the same areas over and over: desert wastelands, acid lakes and mystic dungeons that make no sense, all of that is gone. The game has more arctic and volcanic areas, and it feels less repetitive.
Do I recommend this game? Yeah! It was fun, even more fun with friends, even MORE fun in New Game + with Tina and Brick narrating most of it. However I would recommend buying it on a sale along with at least one friend to enjoy it more, and I would recommend to ignore the DLC’s all together. If anything, buy the one that adds story and the two characters to add more replayability, that’s it. I don’t think selling gun packs should be supported as it’s just a stupid idea sold to you for money.
TL;DR Edition: Borderlands 2 in space but with some fixed issues. The game is quite fun, and the story is way better than Borderlands 1 and 2 together. However it’s also easier and doesn’t have as much variety. Would recommend if you have friends to play it with.

I was looking for a cheap, short and easy walking simulator to pass the time and this turned out to be a lot better than I ever expected it to be.
Watching the trailer and flicking through the screenshots, it looked a little too bleak and bare to have much to it, but it was cheap and I thought it would at least be something to look at. The barren island however is a little misleading. It’s not much to look at but what you discover of it’s past is more than enough to keep you interested in exploring it’s bends and corners.
I found the story really interesting, and although it might start a little slow, I enjoyed the ending and how it was presented to you very much. It was intense and dramatic, and there is a depth to this game you don’t find that often. The questions of existence and belief come into play and it can be both thought provoking and a little daunting. For £1.60 it was well worth a go.
This game may not be for everyone, especially seeing as it’s been given the controversial tag of “Walking Simulator”, but if you can look past the fact that most of what you do is walk around, I think you’ll enjoy this game greatly. Even more so if you have philosophical or psychological interests.
Although only taking just under an hour to finish, I was left quite impressed by this game and decided to look at others by the same developer. If you enjoy this game, I also recommend that you play “The Music Machine”. It isn’t a sequel Per se, more so just a stand alone game that makes reference to and expands on The Moon Sliver. If you have questions after playing this game, that one might answer one or two for you.
All in all I’m very impressed with David’s games and look forward to any future games he puts out there.
TL;DR : It’s a short yet enjoyable walking simulator with more than meets the eye, it may look bleak but I found that the story, although starting quite slow, makes it a worth while buy. There is a depth to it you might enjoy if interested by psychology or philosophy.

First it is still alpha so some of the functionalities do not work yet.
In the future it could be a really good one player zombie game. You are gathering materials improving your base camp and you can go to 3rd person view scavenging 3 towns. The zombies are pretty easy to kill with for ex an iron bar except for two bosses. You collect weapons, ammo, materials. After a few hours it gets a little bit boring. They should add more zombies, more weapons, attack moves, more cities to scavenge. In the 3rd town there are also bandits with automatic weapons and they are moving in a group so you can kill them from distance if you fave a sniper rifle. They drop a lot of stuff after dying. Aah, zombies are a little bit stupid, you run away from them, the follow you, you jump on a car and they stop. You can then just aim with your gun and score a nice headshot - it is a good tactic to spare ammo but I do not know why you cant jump on some cars. Antibiotics are best to heal. If you are wounded use them or go back to base and wait a few days to recover. After you die you are still alive in your base but you have to wait a few days to be able to scavenge again. I liked the graphics, the sounds and the idea. Night is fun and it is a little scary to scavenge with the torch and all the noises out there. I struggled at the beginning with inventory capacity but after I found a backpack it was ok. In the camp you have also to improve storage to have more inventory slots. I did it at the begining. You can also launch scavenges parties form your camp. Your camp can also be attacked by zombies at some time and you have some tactic screen where you choose defensive strategies. At the beginning it was easy but after like 30 days I got overrun and everybody got killed - I had like 5 survivors including myself. It was strange because it was like 6 zombies and we had automatic weapons :) When everybody died the game did not end and I was able to scavenge towns with my survivor being officialy dead :) I love zombie games and this game has the potential to be a really good game. It needs still a lot of work from developers side. Keep it up!

The new, updated version of the old classics like Master of Orion, Space Empires and Galactic Civilizations, but instead of turn-based this game is real-time with the option to pause.
Way off from the earlier games of Paradox, this still is a very solid game, especially if you like these kind of space-civ building games. Very nice touches are the ability to completely customize your race, but also to allow custom made races to be drawn into future games as AI opponents. Also, Paradox events are part of this game, so expect a few laughters while reading through event descriptions, and there's more than a few references to historical events that could've taken place here on earth.
Still, compared to other similar games, this feels slightly streamlined, but I suppose that's on par with Paradox products. If you consider EU, CK or some other of their titles, much detail never went into the tactical parts, how machines were to be made or what composition units would have except for a variation of base troop types. In that sense, having 4 types of base ships that can be modified somewhat according to your liking is decent enough I suppose, but this and the sort of slim options on planet building, coupled with the almost total absence of tactics is the drawbacks of this title.
They don't bug me much though, those shortcomings I just listed. This game really shines in its strategic parts, and diplomacy can be really interesting and unexpected. There's options for building federations, as well as having vassals, contributaries and so forth, to alliances, non-agression pacts, trade deals and different types of war. The difference in war is determined by your nations focus, as pacifists wont' be able to wage conquest wars for example.
As for the strategic parts, instead of going for one of the classic star-travel choices of warp, wormhole or starlane hyperdrive, this game has all three. You'll get to choose one, and strategy will differ depending on what you pick.
The game also contains alot of references to sci-fi movies, like the alien genetic xeno-troopers, that turns out as "Bio-warfare divisions" and contains Xenomorphs (I guess
finally got their way, huh?), so it's clear that the homework has been done on sci-fi as well, wich at least helps me appreciate a game like this even more, and you can be the sci-fi component as well, by invading planets that have sentient beings that hasn't reached space yet. Land your troops amongst atomic-age sentient mammal beings, or establish an observation post in orbit, silently observing, try to enlighten them with technology, or maybe stay hidden and just do secret experiments on them, the choice is all yours.
Finally, there's also domestic politics, with different fractions, unrest, potential revolts and whatever you could imagine, and if you have aliens to your race as slaves in your area, expect an emancipation movement to start sooner or later. You can make political decisions, and those decisions will have an impact, not only on what your empire can do in the galaxy, but will also impact home opinion, and as always, there's always some people happy about a certain direction, as there's always people unhappy about it.
All in all, this makes for a game with surprising depth, and not all you can do have been mentioned in this review. As such it's well worth picking up and can provide with lots and lots of good gaming time. Some parts could've been more complex, but I suppose it's a balance between it all. One thing is for sure though, and that is that it is solid as it stands, and have potential to become a true classic. My opinion on Paradox DLCs are that they're very often solid and mostly brings new, interesting and depthening concepts to their games, so it's anyones guess how good this could actually end up becoming.

A game that slowly shows you different levels of complexity and strategy bit by bit. 8 hours in and you're still getting new perspectives on how you could win, or party members to use. No unneccesary tutorials or boring training grounds. The game believes you to be smart enough to pick up what it's putting down.
Everyone will tell you the art is phenomenal, but let me take a moment to praise the sound design. From the soundtrack to the choices made in sound effects, everything feels satisfying. Normally I enjoy some games while playing a podcast in the background, but I can't bring myself to mute the music to this game.
The artwork pulled me in, but the entire game won't let go of me.

I expected to get tired of the repetitive battles, but the enemies and their abilities are varied enough to keep it interesting. The story is the usual "heroes against all-powerful evil", but has a couple of unexpected twists and a range of likeable characters.
It took me a bit over 30 hours to complete the game, and I enjoyed them thoroughly.

With most of the time in any JRPG being spent in battles, this one's system delivers.
If I had one complaint, it would be the common one that benched party members don't get EXP, forcing you to read about about all of the characters and their skills in order to determine what team you want. There's not much room for experimentation in terms of character picks, but fortunately the Perk system gives a great depth of customization, letting you tailor you team around certain strategies or patch up certain weaknesses.
If you like JRPGs, then this game is right up your alley!

This game is a love letter to PS1/PS2 era dungeon crawlers/JRPGs, wrapped in a very modernized, polished, stylized shell. The art team has perfectly replicated Joe Mad's hyper excessive mangaish art style that was all the rage in the 90's comic scene for a bit. It's just a good fun time. The battle system is turn based, and at first doesn't seem like much, but as the game goes a long you're juggling buffs, debuffs, deciding which tier of ultimate moves you want to use and when. There's a lot going on, and there'sa bunch to do between crafting ultimate weapons, an arena, and even bounties for hunting extra boss fights.
No stink of mobile gaming on this game, feels like a true modern JRPG.

For about a year, I've been searching game stores in my Toronto neighbourhood, looking for a little gem on the PS2 called Eternal Ring by FromSoftware; perhaps you've heard of it? I never was able to find it and when it came on Playstation Store, I decided not to buy it in favour of Friday the 13th, the resulting situation ending in me hocking my PS4 due to a lack of customer support and quality control.
Then I came to Steam and thought I may never know the fun of Eternal Ring again, Delver has proved me wrong. It's like a more accessable, minecrafty version. Endearing to me right from the start, I started to play not knowing much, learning that the potions work off of a RNG, just like DeathState, you can build your Delver from the first time you set foot in a dungeon until you happen to fall victim to some devious creatures or traps, at which point you must start from scratch - save for your gold... your sweet, sweet gold. This allows later playthroughs some leniency and sets you up so you can at least have an idea of how you are going to build your Delver for the current new playthough.
In summation, buy this game! It's totally worth it for the price, if you don't like it you can just refund it, but I guarentee you'll find yourself dropping hours upon hours on it if you find it's your style. I've only played for about an hour and half at the time of writing but I can say I'll be putting many more hours in before I'm through. Happy delving, fellow Delvers!

Yet another cool rogue like dongeon game :D. Today Delver which is a good surprise. Let's start the review

GRAPHICS:
The game use a a pixel art 3D environement, The environment is in 3D and sprites are in 2D. Usually these kind of design creates a lot of problems of perspective but no here. The overall decoration is great and it really look like a dongeon, no doubt on this. Also the Rogue like side don't creates inconsistencies and the game don't even look like a rogue like :)
SOUNDS:
The songs are cool overall but not oustanding. The sounds disagn is simple and sometimes out of the ways, like the blade sound which is the same if you hit a wall, a door or a mushroom.
GAMEPLAY:
This game use procedural generation which mean than when you start a game you have a new character level 1 in a brand new dongeon.
Basically it use all of basics elements you can find in RPGs: level up with stats you can uprgrade (speed, damages, agility...). You have an inventory, you can find food, potions and armors and there is a a sort of "class selection" in the ways that you can fight with staffs, sword, bows ect...
The goal is to finish the dongeon by finding the exit of each floor and going down. The goal is to find an orb and the return out of the dongeon, pretty cool idea I have to say.
Overall the gameplay is very nice and dynamic, the fights are good and the fact that you lose your game when you die add a tension and make the game really immersive
STORY:
You can find notes in the dongeon but I was too lazy to read them lol
CONTENT:
Because this game use procedural generation for his world, there is a good replayability and all your games will be differents (rogue like's magic :D :DD :D <33).
There is also mods in this game, but not that many and they add... almost nothing, just new weapons, enemies ect..
But this is where the good sides stops, because the content is not that huge in Delver, I can even say that for a game like this, it is almost poor:
1: The game is really really really easy, I finished it after 2 hours, it's ridiculous compared to other rogue-like games.
2: There is nothing to unlock which mean that there is nothing to push you to continue playing after finishing it. Added with the first point it became the shortest rogue like I ever done (in comparison, I finished Rogue Legacy 100% after 50 hours)
3: The game is still on early access, because why would they finish it whereas it already sales pretty good... disgusting
CONCLUSION:
Delver is very simplistic, in his design like in his gameplay. But despite this is a very good and fun game that can be pretty fun to speedrun imo. Too bad that it do not offer that much content for a rogue-like and that the devellopers are to lazy to finish it -_-
Final rating: 13/20

Best total war I've played, it has to do with personal opinions and facts alike, now, before I'll get into the review, I want to point out that I have not played Attila or Warhammer, so it may change later.
Pros:
-[personal pro] to me, it has the right pace, Rome one was too fast paced and Rome II can't compare to both of those games
-easily modable, if you yourself wants to let's say, change the music, then no problem, as long as you have proficiency within modding, and you know Medieval II's modding language, this is also evidenced by the great mods that Medieval II has, an example of the great mods it fields  is Third Age total war, and more than that, Submods have been made for the mod, that makes Third Age alone be another game in itself
-unit balance, the units are very well balanced, and the system made for the units like: Cav fail vs spears, and speas fail against swordsmen, is brilliant, it makes you bring  some of every unit in your army
-special ability, the special abilities are very good, you're general can do a rally, the pikes can go into a spear wall, mounted knights into hedge formation, and the fact that they serve their purpose is very good. I.e Pikes form a spear wall so that they can keep their enemies at distance, they still do have weaknesses in their lack of shields, so that makes you want to bring skrimishers, it simply works.
-the campaign's recruitment system, the recruitment system is great, the way that you are restricted from getting a full stack of knights, or that you can do that, but in their stead get three armies of spear militia works great.
-the music, the mustic in the vanilla version of the game, as well as its expansions is very good, I have gained a love for the Britania music, and the others are also very good.
Cons:
-bad AI, the AI is far from good, therefore I recommend you to take a quick look on the internet and find an intelligent AI as a replacement.
-stack spamming, the stack spamming can get unreal, as the AI gets money bonuses, this might be to give it a chance against you, but I would have preferred a better AI, or some higher upkeep prices.
-lack of variety [Muslim factions only] even in the crusader expanision they lack vareity, and the jannisaries are not as good as they should be, they should be on par with the byzzantine Latinkon, but they are not, as other units also chew them up.
-bugs and glitches, there are many terrible bugs, such as wall bugs, and that's just sad, the two-handed glitch also is a shame, and that is why that some mods have redesgned the two-handed weapon animations for the two-hander weapons, the Jannisaries and the dismounted Gothic knights suffer from this, and therefore they are too easily beaten by other elite infantry, that was supposed to lose or be on par to them.
This is all, thank you for reading, as that you can fix most cons with mods, then I would definately recommend this to you all.

I’ve played the three main games by now (I do want to try Tales of the Borderlands, but will wait for a sale), and being completely honest I was expecting this game to suck. I don’t know why, I just did. However I’m somewhat surprised in the end. As usual I’m gonna start talking about what the game does poorly, then go up from there.
First and foremost, the biggest issue I see on the game is the repetition. There’s not that much variety on enemies compared to the second game, and they don’t talk nearly as much as I hoped. What bothers me even more is that the big trailers of the game (specially the one with Mister Torgue) showed the Lost Legion to be the main enemies of the game, however they barely show up later in the game for a while, which sucks♥♥♥♥♥as they fought differently to the rest of them.
The second thing I didn’t like at all is how underused some characters are. Mister Torgue is by far one of the most loved characters in the entire franchise, yet he barely talks on three quests. Nina, the nurse, barely has one or two quests about her. Papa Crust, who sounded like an hilarious parody of Fidel Castro ended up only showing on a quest (a long quest, but just one). Even some of the main characters seem like that, Brick barely narrates anything and Tiny Tina, another well loved character by the fans only really appears in New Game +.
Something else I wasn’t a big fan have to be the weapons themselves. A few new kinds of weapons have been added, and some new kinds of elemental damage went into it as well, however I don’t think they were properly balanced. Laser weapons are way above everything, one of them (the E-Gun, a weapon that’s a parody of Ghostbusters that you get on a quest) was insanely powerful on the character I had picked (Nisha), to the point that I didn’t use ANY other gun for the next 10 levels until I got a good replacement as it was already getting weaker in comparison. And guess what, the replacement was also a laser weapon.
A problem that relates to the last one is the lack of difficulty. The game was quite easy from start to finish by myself. Now maybe it was because I ended up picking a broken character (I did feel like Nisha’s aimbot was too powerful and barely had any cooldown) but the only times I died was thanks to me getting suicidally overconfident. Also, the game’s new gimmick is the oxygen, but it barely does anything serious. The oxygen levels drop too slowly, are too big, and there’s pockets of oxygen EVERYWHERE, making it impossible to actually die because of asphyxiation. Also, the secret boss the game has after you finish the story wasn’t ANYWHERE as hard as bosses on previous games. Seriously, I beated him on my first try by myself. That’s kinda pathetic.
Lastly, the DLC’s. I’m not a big fan of them mainly because Gearbox keeps doing things right and then ♥♥♥♥ing it all up again, and this game doesn’t change that at all. There’s ONE DLC that adds a story, and one DLC that adds an arena. The rest are just two character DLC’s and weapons. Let’s look back at Borderlands 2 however, and A LOT of the DLC’s were characters and story based ones. What the ♥♥♥♥, man? The game advertises itself for having bazillions of weapons, WHY WOULD I PAY MORE FOR A FEW EXTRA!?
However, looking away from those issues you have a decent sequel to Borderlands 2.
The story is arguably the biggest point the game has running for itself, quite ironic since the story on Borderlands 1 was so lame and boring I couldn’t even bring myself to finish it. However, you SHOULD play Borderlands 2 before you go into this one to understand everything properly. Both are great, so you got nothing to lose on that. It shows that they have learned from their previous mistakes on actually making a good story line that hooks you up instead of a sorry excuse to just go shoot bandits in the face.
The characters themselves have also been expanded properly in comparison from previous games. In the original game the main characters barely even talked and nothing was explained that much. In Borderlands 2 your characters talked a bit more, and there was more story behind stuff. Here however, your characters actually do talk and express their opinions, the story is explained properly and if you happen to like your character, you’ll get really interested in seeing how things turn out for them. Extra points for having one of the main characters narrate it, however it would be great if all the characters would narrate their own story in their own way, not just Athena. I know the reason why they don’t, just saying each would have their own intro and reason behind it.
The enemies that are more or less unique to the game instead of recycled space versions are also interesting, mainly the Lost Legion and the enemies on the last areas. They got medics who heal each other, engineers who put turrets and other stuff, it’s interesting and changes the flow of gameplay quite nicely.
The references are also here as usual. Borderlands 2 had an insane amount of them and this game is not shy to show what inspired them at all. From escorting a pair of robots to an old man named Toby Van Adobe to making the Slammiest Dunk in history, the game won’t spend an hour without trying to crack a joke or two.
Lastly, the change in the setting of the game works quite well. Honestly I was kinda tired of the same areas over and over: desert wastelands, acid lakes and mystic dungeons that make no sense, all of that is gone. The game has more arctic and volcanic areas, and it feels less repetitive.
Do I recommend this game? Yeah! It was fun, even more fun with friends, even MORE fun in New Game + with Tina and Brick narrating most of it. However I would recommend buying it on a sale along with at least one friend to enjoy it more, and I would recommend to ignore the DLC’s all together. If anything, buy the one that adds story and the two characters to add more replayability, that’s it. I don’t think selling gun packs should be supported as it’s just a stupid idea sold to you for money.
TL;DR Edition: Borderlands 2 in space but with some fixed issues. The game is quite fun, and the story is way better than Borderlands 1 and 2 together. However it’s also easier and doesn’t have as much variety. Would recommend if you have friends to play it with.

Hands down this is the best zombie game I've played, if not the best game on steam - I'm completely addicted.  Its designation as Early Access is misleading, the current version feels more like a highly polished game and is already in class of its own.  It is teeming with things to collect, places to explore and endless hours of entertainment.  I've spent over a 100 hours already and I still feel like I've only scratched the surface.  I can't wait to see what they do next - you won't regret this purchase.
Pros:
Perfect combination of fps and base management.
Huge number of weapons, craftable items and upgrades.
Highly active and dedicated developers.
You'd expect to pay $60 for content like this, the price is a steal.
Cons:
Navigation difficult at first.
Finding items at first is frustrating.  Once you figure out where to look and where not to look, the game becomes much more manageable.
Combat system confusing at first if you don't read the guides.
The zombies aren't so OP or numerous that you're constantly hanging on for dear life.  However, poor planning, decision making or aim and they'll tear you apart.  Different areas provide different risks and rewards that you choose based on your current need, available resources and ability to survive.  It really feels like you stepped into the walking dead - something most games promise but rarely deliver.  Scavenging the materials you need to survive, keep healthy, protect and expand your camp is a constant battle.  It's the perfect blend of these two elements that make this game a true gem.
Hints:
1.) Read the guides before you play for combat tips and the basic map of the area - knowing how to properly melee and where you are on the map makes a huge difference.
2.) Nightime is not pitch black if you wait for the moon to rise.  Find a safe place to wait it out, then continue scavenging until your backpack is completely filled with the items you need.  Leaving when it gets dark out means your camp has to survive on less than it has to.

This is an amazing game, and if you are considering buying it I would absolutely NOT recommend you do so.

Even if by some act of the gods this game works for an extended period of time, I may as well hand-draw every frame to give me a higher framerate than this game provides. Even at lower settings, without any of the fancy stuff, 30 FPS is a luxury rarely seen, and running the game in fullscreen somehow renders worse quality than running borderless windowed.
In summary I can heartily recommend this game to anyone going for a personal best deadlift or maybe prepping for a boxing match. Play for 5 minutes on this (and that's all you're gonna get whether you like it or not) and you'll be filled with hellish anger that would cause even Gordon Ramsey to run away scared.

With only 30 hours of gameplay under my belt, maybe 4 hours of it alt tabbed. I cannot say I am an expert at this game but I feel I am at a point to give my personal view on the game.
The novelty of your healer being a giant war golem and your tank being, well a little girl does wear off kind of fast and becomes just part of the game. That isn't bad though but just a heads up.
The major issues I have with this game is the grinding. I am pretty bad at overleveling my characters, I do it in any RPG I play. But the amount of time I have put into this game to try be over leveled is insane. And even then I tend to hit a wall and need to grind some more. A good example is the second boss in the sewers. Being 1 level under you can JUST do it but you will get wrecked. So I decided lets go back when 2 levels higher than the boss. It can still wreck you if you don't pay attention. That is not entirely a bad thing, challange is good. But what I find bad is how little xp you get.
The second issue I have. And this is kind of nit picking, is the opening FMV. Why if I put my audio sliders almost all the way down does it just play at full volume? I have a 7.2 surround sound system. And if I don't have E or ESC ready it is deafening. Having an option to skip that FMV or even turn ITS volume down would be great.
A final little issue is not being able to skip Burst abilities little FMV. Hey they look cool. But it does get repeatative.
Now for the good. I like the change on the fly system of specs with no penalties, the fact that your moves feel impactful. Like really you do even a jab it feels like you really hit them, and hard. All the skills really feel like they have power behind them.
I also like the system that seemingly makes lower leveled characters in your party catch up in levels fast. Nothing worse in other RPGs where you get a new character its underleveled and will forever remain that way. In this they catch up pretty fast and even if they die they will still get the XP and be revived at the end of the battle.
It can be played pretty easily with keyboard and mouse. I would LOVE to rebind the keys but its not too bad and seemingly has alot of redundant keys.
All in all I think this game is worth a look at if you liker RPGs. It does some things that are new but if you don't like the genre it may not be for you.

I got this game on sale; I am a fan of 4x strategy games.
Stellaris has many features that Civ series gets wrong... vassals and interstellar politics.
The game is deep, with the hardest learning curve I have seen yet in 4x.  (I didnt really know what was going on until 40 hours in, mastered it 60 hours in.  And that's not because I'm a 4x noob.)
It comes with all the features you would expect, with a sort of revolution in depth:
CON
* Inadequate interface and not enough alerts / automation.  One glaring example is that in vassals/sectors (i.e. "vassals"inside your empire) you cannot control building on planets.  Except space ports.  But if you want to build ships, there is no shortcut, you simply have to go through the map and open the planet manually, because it's not on quick reference bar.
* The early game drags on too long.
* Total lack of meaningful tutorial about game mechanics.  Examples abound, but in a late game event, I joined an alliance with an ancient empire to combat the galactic invaders.  Turns out I was their vassal.  Whoops.  Another example: modules for your ships are actually modules for your military starbases.  (Uh tooltip epic fail)
* While there is a wiki, it does not cover enough depth.  Now while figuring out finer points of mechanics is fun, this game can be misleading.
* Technology penalized for empire size (specifically, population), so that mid-late game research agreements are next to worthless.
PRO
* When Civ series and Master of Orion are headed towards simplicity, this game adds lots of systems no other game has.
* Tech system is tied to the government you have and randomness.  So therefore no one has the same techs.
* Intelligent AI.
* Heavy replayability.  Virtually infinite government types to experiment with.
* Community modding.  (Probably fixes the annoying interface problems, I have yet to see.)
